meta.title: Dragon Language Dictionary, Dragon-English and English-Dragon, Fifth Edition
meta.copy_used: research/sources/thuum/Dragon_Language_Print_Dictionary_5th_Edition.docx, a Word conversion of the PDF supplied by the project owner on 2026-11-15
meta.terms: Non-commercial use, with credit to Thuum.org. See research/sources/thuum/ATTRIBUTION.md for the basis.
meta.what_is_official: By the dictionary's own statement only the official definition and the usage quotations come from official sources. Word type, pronunciation, expanded definition, connotations, etymology and notes are its authors' analysis.
meta.limits: The copy is a PDF converted to Word, so columns are sometimes interleaved and section text can carry stray words from a neighbouring entry. It holds 646 entries; the introduction says 647. One region was read by hand. Word type is blank for 26 entries. Entries with a known misprint or doubt carry a "doubt" field. Section text is as printed and was not proofread.

fields.runes: rune spelling in the font's key codes (1 aa, 2 ei, 3 ii, 4 ah, 5 uu, 6 ur, 7 ir, 8 oo, 9 ey)
fields.official_definition: definition quoted from an official source
fields.remarks_in_definition: bracketed remarks that are part of the definition
fields.expanded_definition, usage, connotations: the other sections of the entry, as printed

entries.expanded_definition: v. to guide n. guide; guidance
entries.usage: Nafni wahlaan qethsegol bormahii vahrukt, Ragnvald, wen Zii fen mahfaeraak aak ok brod, ahrk folook ok hokoron. Nafni raised this stone for his father, Ragnvald, whose Spirit will forever guide his clan, and haunt his enemies. (Word Wall for Zii, Become Ethereal) Faas ni Brendon do Dinok, fah rok los qolaas do moro, ahrk hin aak wah lot Sovngarde. Fear not the Specter of Death, for he is the herald of glory, and your guide to great Sovngarde. (Word Wall for Faas, Dismay) Qostiid sahlo aak. Prophecy is a weak guide. (Paarthurnax, 0003F9E1)

entries.expanded_definition: v. may, might, to express possibility, wish, or prayer
entries.usage: Aal rek siiv unahzaal praan ko Feykro do Hahnu. May she find eternal rest in the Forest of Dreams. (Word Wall for Kaan, Kyne’s Peace) Orin pruzaan dwiin aal kreh ahrk kren, nuz Slen do vahzah muz los sindugahvon. Even the best steel may bend and break, but the Flesh of a true man is unyielding. (Word Wall for Slen, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: Associated with prayer. Used in formal addresses or commemorations.
entries.notes: Not used to indicate permission. May be the original of draal ‘to pray’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to serve, act as a servant, give loyalty to
entries.usage: Aam? Serve you? ...no. Ni tiid. If and when you defeat Alduin, I will reconsider. Serve you? No, not yet. If and when you defeat Alduin, I will reconsider. (Odahviing, 00048F03) Zu'u fent aam. I shall serve. (Tamed Dragon, 0201FB93) Aam uv dir. Serve or die. (Krosulhah, 020286FE)
entries.connotations: To serve someone out of duty or loyalty, such as a king or leader. Connotes subservience but not domination or loss of will.

entries.official_definition: A/An (Song of the Dragonborn, not generally used)
remarks_in_definition: Song of the Dragonborn, not generally used
entries.expanded_definition: art. a, an
entries.usage: Alduin, feyn do jun, kruziik vokun staadnau, voth aan bahlok wah diivon fin lein! Alduin, bane of kings, ancient shadow unbound, with a hunger to swallow the world! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Het nok Faal Vahlok, deinmaar do Dovahgolz ahrk aan Fus do unslaad rahgol ahrk vulom. Here lies The Guardian, keeper of the Dragonstone and a Force of eternal rage and darkness. (Word Wall for Fus, Unrelenting Force)
entries.notes: Rarely used outside of poetry or song, particularly absent in speech.

entries.expanded_definition: n. slave
entries.usage: Meyye! Tahrodiis aanne! Him hinde pah liiv! Zu'u hin daan! Fools! Treacherous slaves! Your hopes (are) all withered! I (am) your doom. (Alduin, 000CD9DF)
entries.connotations: Denotes a person who serves by free will, but owes their service as a function of strength or domination.
entries.etymology: Related to aar ‘servant/slave’.
entries.notes: Variant of aar that more specifically denotes a slave, possibly a mistake as it occurs in only a single line. Use aar ‘servant/slave’ or zaam ‘slave’ instead.

entries.expanded_definition: n. servant, slave, one who serves out of duty or loyalty
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do Hela, fahdon wah pah sivaas, aar do Kaan. Here lies the body of Hela, friend to all beasts, servant of Kyne. (Word Wall for Kaan, Kyne’s Peace) Qethsegol vahrukiv lot Miraak — sonaak do lot onikaan, aar do faal Diiv, ahrk hokoron do jul. This stone commemorates the great Miraak — priest of great wisdom, servant of the Wyrm, and enemy to man. (Word Wall for Diiv, Dragon Aspect) You are persistent, Dovahkiin. Pruzah ol aar. A fine slave you would have made. You are persistent, Dovahkiin. Good as (a) slave.. A fine slave you would have made. (Alduin, 000EDF49)
entries.connotations: Typically denotes a person who serves by their own free will, as an act of duty or loyalty, rather than by enslavement or domination. This distinction blurs in dragon culture, where loyalty is owed to the strongest and most dominant. Related word zaam specifically refers to a slave without free will.
entries.etymology: Related to aam ‘to serve’.
entries.notes: Also appears as aan in one line of dialogue, either a variant or possibly a mistake.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to join forces, efforts, sides, or company n. union, unison, unity
entries.usage: Fah ok unslaad mid rok aav dilon voth lot zin. For his eternal loyalty, he joins the dead with great honor. (Word Wall for Mid, Battle Fury) Aav uv dir. Join (me) or die. (Alduin, 000C64F2)
entries.connotations: Primarily relates to the military and battle. No occurrence yet refers to physical contact.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to relent, give quarter (to), have mercy (on) n. mercy, quarter, relent, respite
entries.usage: Bolog aaz, mal lir! Beg (for) mercy, little worm! (Draugr, 000C64F2) Nivahriin muz fent siiv nid aaz het. Cowardly men shall find no mercy here. (Morokei, 00080103)
entries.etymology: May relate to faaz ‘pain’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth no More
entries.expanded_definition: v. to burn n. burn; incineration, the act of burning
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv kiir jun Jafnhar, wo los ag nahlaas naal Yol do lot dovah Lodunost. This stone commemorates the child king Jafnhar, who was burned alive by the Fire of the great dragon Lodunost. (Word Wall for Yol, Fire Breath)
entries.notes: Molag is the Ehlnofex word for ‘fire’. External inspiration may also have come from the Sanskrit agni ‘fire’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. hunter
entries.usage: Od ah viing! Snow hunter wing! (Call Dragon Shout)
entries.connotations: Appears only as a Word of Power in the Call Dragon Shout.
entries.notes: Shortest word in the known language. Alternate interpretation of the dragon name Dovahkiin translates to ‘dragonkind hunter born’ or ‘born to hunt dragonkind’ rather than ‘dragon born’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. courage, bravery
entries.usage: But I honor your courage. Krif voth ahkrin. But I honor your courage. (You) fight bravely. (Mirmulnir, 00078DF7) Nonvul Bron mahfaeraak dahmaan sahrot Vahlok, wen lot ahkrin shaan ney muz ahrk dovah. Noble Nord, forever remember the mighty Vahlok, whose great courage inspired both men and dragons. (Word Wall for Shaan, Battle Fury)
entries.connotations: May share root with krii ‘to kill’, kriin ‘to slay’, and krif ‘to fight’, indicating ahkrin and its related words connotate courage and bravery in battle.
entries.etymology: From krin ‘courageous’.
entries.notes: The phrase voth ahkrin ‘with courage’ is used as an adverb to mean ‘courageously’ or ‘bravely’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. service
entries.usage: Tiidi do ahmik oblaan. My time of service is ended. (Tamed Dragon, 0202AD10) Het mah Siigoniis Neivaan, wo wundun gut nol hofkiin dir voth zin ko ahmik do Zeymahzin. Here fell the Argonian Neivaan, who travelled far from home (to) die with honor in service of the Companions. (Abandoned Word Wall for Gut,Throw Voice)
entries.connotations: Refers to service that is given out of duty or loyalty, not servitude or enslavement.
entries.etymology: From aam ‘to serve’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. husband
entries.usage: Lungerd wahlaan qethsegol ahmulii vahkrut, Thorgrima, deinmaar do sahqon yolos, ahrk drog do Lah. Lungered raised this stone in memory of her husband, Thorgrima, keeper of the crimson flame, and lord of Magicka. (Word Wall for Lah, Drain Vitality) Bekkhild wahlaan qethsegol ahmulii vahrukt, Eyolf, wen veysun los sizaan ko vul kest ko Okaaz do Luv. Bekkhild raised this stone in memory of her husband, Eyolf, whose ship was lost in a dark tempest in the Sea of Tears. (Word Wall for Kest, Whirlwind Sprint)
entries.connotations: Possible origins shed light on the role a husband would have had in ancient Nordic society; a hunter and protector of the clan, or someone who serves his spouse.
entries.etymology: Possibly a compound meaning ‘hunterstrong’, or from aam ‘to serve’, ‘servestrong’.

entries.official_definition: Wound (as in, injury/hurt/etc. - noun or verb)
remarks_in_definition: as in, injury/hurt/etc. - noun or verb
entries.expanded_definition: v. to wound, injure, hurt n. wound, injury, hurt
entries.usage: Ahraan. You wound me, Dovahkiin. (Odahviing, 0004DE37) If you brought that Kel, that Elder Scroll back here... to the Tiid-Ahraan, the TimeWound... (Paarthurnax, 0003FA49)
entries.connotations: Can refer to a physical, emotional, or metaphorical wound.

entries.official_definition: And (formal - not commonly used) (Dragon Language: Myth No More)
entries.expanded_definition: conj. and
entries.usage: Ahrk fin norok paal graan fod nust hon zindro zaan. And the fiercest foes rout when they hear triumph’s shout. (Songs of Skyrim) Su'um ahrk morah. Breath and focus. (Paarthurnax, 000E8276)
entries.notes: Mostly seen in Word Walls, song, and poetry. In written language, can be used to separate phrases where it would be otherwise unclear.

entries.expanded_definition: n. hill
entries.usage: Granite Hill — Quethsegol [sic] Ahrol — Three Farms and an Inn, just North of the Falkreath. (Book, Holdings of Jarl Gjalund)
entries.notes: Also found in Ahrolsedovah, dragon name for Whiterun, and Ahroldan, dragon name for ‘H’roldan’. Possibly inspired by Icelandic ‘hóll’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. H’roldan, place name
entries.usage: H’roldan — Ahroldan — A Spacious Wooden Hall and Pasturage, recently Seized from the Reachmen. (Book, Holdings of Jarl Gjalund)
entries.etymology: From ahrol ‘hill’.
entries.notes: Likely an adaptation of the Nordic name ‘H’roldan’ into the dragon language, coined by Jarl Gjalund to lend authority to his rule.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Whiterun, lit. ‘hill of the dragon’
entries.usage: Whiterun — Ahrolsedovah — The Jarl's Holding, with Plentiful Water and Pasturage. (Book, Holdings of Jarl Gjalund) Odahviing will come to your challenge. … He will not be able to resist your call, from the Hill of the Dovah itself... he will come. (Paarthurnax, 000D2CF4)
entries.connotations: If dragon in origin, likely refers to the geographical hill upon which Whiterun is built more so than the city itself.
entries.etymology: Se compound of ahrol ‘hill’ and dovah ‘dragon’, lit. ‘hill of the dragon’.
entries.notes: Paarthurnax refers to Whiterun as ‘the Hill of the Dovah’ (000D2CF4), indicating a dragon origin rather than an invention by Jarl Gjalund.

entries.expanded_definition: prep. at, indicating state or condition (‘at peace’, ‘at bay’); at, towards; at, instrumental (‘at the hands of’)
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, Dovahkiin, naal ok zin los vahriin, wah dein vokul mahfaeraak ahst vaal! Dragonborn, Dragonborn, by his honor is sworn, to keep evil forever at bay! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) But I cannot celebrate his fall. Zu'u tiiraaz ahst ok mah. He was my brother once. This world will never be the same. Zu'u tiiraaz ahst ok mah. = “I am sad at his fall.” (Paarthurnax, 0009C20A) Het nok kopraan do Iglif Iiz-Sos, wo grind ok oblaan ni ko morokei vukein, nuz ahst munax haalvut do liiv krasaar. Here lies the body of Iglif Ice-Boold, who met his end not in glorious combat, but at the cruel touch of the withering sickness. (Word Wall for Iiz, Ice Form)
entries.notes: Indicates state, condition, or instrumental (by or with). Also indicates direction, towards. Not used to reference location as in ‘by’ or ‘at’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to wear, as in clothing or armor n. wear, garments
entries.usage: Het ont kriist Miraak, wo ahtiid ok sahvot ol Qah, spaan naal Deyra fah ok unslaad midun. Here once stood Miraak, who wore his faith as Armor, shielded by the Daedra for his unending loyalty. (Word Wall for Qah, Dragon Aspect)
entries.etymology: Possibly from tiid ‘time’.
entries.notes: This word was likely created to mean ‘to wear or weather over time’, but is used to mean ‘to wear armor’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. bitter adv. bitterly n. bitterness v. to bitter, embitter, make or become bitter
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv ahzid Viik do Briinahmaar do Sot Peyt, naako wah fin laat naal ufiik do Korvag Kol. This stone commemorates the bitter Defeat of the Sisterhood of the White Rose, eaten to the last by the Trolls of Korvag Crag. (Word Wall for Viik, Disarm)
entries.connotations: Bitter in feeling or sentiment.
entries.etymology: Possibly from aaz ‘mercy’ and its family of words relating to pain.
entries.notes: Featured in the dragon priest name Ahzidal ‘bitter destroyer’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to destroy n. destruction; destroyer
entries.usage: Zu’u fen al. I will destroy (it). (Tamed Dragon, 0202BC4F)
entries.etymology: May share root with ag ‘to burn’.
entries.notes: Featured prominently in the dragon name Alduin ‘destroyer devour master’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Alik’r
entries.usage: Het mah sahrot konahrik Aaban, kiin se Klo se Alkir, praan nu denek Keizaal. Here fell the mighty warlord Aaban, born of the Sand of the Alik’r, at rest now in the soil of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Klo, Slow Time)
entries.notes: Direct loanword, indicating the name has existed at least since ancient Nordic times.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to rise, arise n. rise
entries.usage: Nuz aan sul, fent alok, fod fin vul dovah nok, fen kos nahlot mahfaeraak ahrk ruz! But a day, shall arise, when the dark dragon's lies, will be silenced forever and then! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Di [sic] kiirre fen alok. My children will rise. (Alduin, 000ED35E)
entries.connotations: To move towards the sky or from the earth. Can also refer to rising from the dead, or when a dragon’s body is restored.
entries.etymology: From lok ‘sky’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. necromancy
entries.usage: I began to explore what the dovah call “Alok-Dilon,” the ancient forbidden art that you call necromancy. (Durnehviir, 02013290)
entries.connotations: Held in superstition even among the dov. Their own powers to alok, regenerate their physical forms, is distinct from alok-dilon.
entries.etymology: Compound meaning ‘rising-dead’.

entries.expanded_definition: adv. ever, at any time
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv key Sarvirra, zok krin Raan alun wah fonaar odus frod, ahrk ofan ok sil fah ok drog. This stone commemorates the horse Sarvirra, the most courageous Animal to ever charge the snowy battlefields, and give his soul for his lord. (Word Wall for Raan, Animal Allegiance)
entries.connotations: Means ‘at any time,’ not ‘ever-present’ or ‘ever since’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. lion
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.

entries.expanded_definition: adv. forward, onward, ahead
entries.usage: Tiid bo amativ. Time flows ever onward. (Paarthurnax, 000BBEA8) Amativ! Mu bo kotin stinselok. Onward! We fly into the sky's freedom. (Odahviing, 000E16F5)

entries.expanded_definition: n. Atmora
entries.usage: Naal Thu'umu, mu ofan nii nu, Dovahkiin, naal suleyk do Kaan, naal suleyk do Shor, ahrk naal suleyk do Atmorasewuth. By our Voice we give it now (to you), Dragonborn, by (the) power of Kyne, by the power of Shor, and by the power of Atmora-ofold. (The Greybeards, 000C43A7)
entries.notes: Direct loanword from the ancient Nords.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to suffer n. suffering
entries.usage: Krii lun aus! Kill leech suffer! (Marked For Death Shout, 00068506) Thoringar wahlaan qethsegol monii vahrukt, Noomi, wen dez los wah Aus nin do pogaan Ogiim ronaaz. Thoringar raised this stone for his daughter’s memory, Noomi, whose fate it was to Suffer the sting of many Orc arrows. (Word Wall for Aus, Marked For Death)
entries.connotations: To experience pain and suffering without mercy or respite.
entries.etymology: May belong to the family of words rooted in aaz ‘mercy’ relating to pain and suffering.

entries.expanded_definition: n. wrath
entries.usage: Strun bah qo! Storm wrath lightning! (Storm Call Shout, 000684E5) Het mah Hrothmar, Bah Grohiik do bruniik pindaar. Aal ok sil rovaan Sovngarde mahfaeraak. Here fell Hrothmar, Wrath Wolf of the savage plains. May his soul wander Sovngarde forever. (Word Wall for Bah, Storm Call)
entries.connotations: Word of Power in the Storm Call Shout.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. worthy adv. worthily n. worth, worthiness v. to make or become worthy
entries.usage: Yes. They are very protective of me. Bahlaan fahdonne. Bahlaan fahdonne = “worthy friends” (Paarthurnax, 000B94C6)
entries.notes: Likely a misspelling or archaic form of balaan ‘worthy’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to hunger, long after, esp. violence or destruction n. hunger, a compulsion driven by wrath or power
entries.usage: Alduin, feyn do jun, kruziik vokun staadnau, voth aan bahlok wah diivon fin lein! Alduin, Bane of Kings, ancient shadow unbound, with a hunger to swallow the world! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Hin sil fen nahkip bahloki. Your soul will feed my hunger. (Alduin, 000ED360) Evenaar bahlok. There are many hungers it is better to deny than to feed. Extinguish (your) hunger. There are many hungers it is better to deny than to feed. (Paarthurnax, 0003F9E2)
entries.connotations: As dragons do not experience mortal hunger, bahlok is better defined as any compulsion driven by wrath, especially destructive in nature or to assert power.
entries.etymology: May derive from bah ‘wrath’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. worthy adv. worthily n. worth, worthiness v. to make or become worthy
entries.usage: Lingrah krosis saraan Strundu'ul, voth nid balaan klov praan nau. Long sorrowfully (has) waited the Stormcrown, with no worthy head to rest on. (Greybeards, 000C43AB) You are brave. Balaan hokoron. Your defeat brings me honor. You are brave. Worthy enemy. Your defeat brings me honor. (Mirmulnir, 00056382)

entries.expanded_definition: adj. foul adv. foully n. foulness v. to befoul, make or become foul
entries.usage: Paaz Keizaal fen kos stin nol bein Alduin jot. Fair Skyrim will be free from foul Alduin's maw. (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Het nok bein nahgahdinok Azaran faal Munax, wo unt wah Gron krilot dilon do Sovngarde wah lein do ul, ahrk funt. Here lies the foul necromancer Azaran the Cruel, who tried to Bind the valiant dead of Sovngarde to the world of man, and failed. (Word Wall for Gron, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Describes a foul character, purpose, or deed, not a foul smell.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to summon n. summons, summoning
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.
entries.connotations: Unknown whether this can refer to conjuration magic.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to open n. opening
entries.usage: Bex! Open! (Borri, 000C4374)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, typically a command.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to scorn n. scorn
entries.usage: Nonvul Bron, dahmaan daar rok do fin Fodiiz Bormah—Oblivion loost nid Nah med spaan vahdin beyn. Noble Nord, remember these words of the Hoar Father—Oblivion hath no Fury like a shield maiden scorned. (Word Wall for Nah, Whirlwind Sprint) I have already defeated your friends once. Beyn. I do not fear them. (Alduin, 000EDF48) Bii B3 +---------------------------------------+------------------------------+

entries.expanded_definition: adj. blue adv. bluely n. blue, blueness v. to make or become blue
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: v. to fly; to flow, move, go; to arrive; to come n. flight; flow; movement; arrival; coming
entries.usage: Tiid bo amativ. Time flows/flies (ever) onward. (Paarthurnax, 000BBEA8) Zu'u ni bo nol het. I (am) not moving from here. (Odahviing, 0004DE37) Alduin, thuri! Boaan tiid vokriiha suleyksejun kruziik? Alduin, my king (overlord)! Has the time arrived (flown) to restore (unkill) your ancient dominion (power-of-king)? (Sahloknir, 00035B4A)
entries.connotations: Movement, particularly flight or forward movement. Can also reference time.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to borrow n. borrowing
entries.usage: Het mah spaan vahdin Valkrys, wo krif voth ahkrin, nuz los folaas wah Ov mulaag do bodiis tuz. Here fell the shield maiden Valkrys, who fought bravely, but was wrong to Trust the strength of a borrowed blade. (Word Wall for Ov, Kyne’s Peace)
entries.connotations: May share root with bolaav ‘to grant’ and bolog ‘to beg’ related to possession or ownership.

entries.expanded_definition: n. age, era, length of time; time
entries.usage: Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, Ahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: A period or length of time, or a moment in time. Not the age of a person or thing.
entries.etymology: May derive from bo ‘to fly/flow’ in the sense of ‘a flight/flow of time’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to grant n. grant
entries.usage: Pah werid morokei Miraak, zok suleykaar do pah Sonaak wen Mul bolaav naal Fahluaan do Jul. All praise the glorious Miraak, most powerful all priests, whose Strength was granted by the Gardener of Men. (Word Wall for Mul, Dragon Aspect)
entries.etymology: May share root with bodiis ‘to borrow’ and bolog ‘to beg’ related to possession or ownership.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to beg (for), beseech n. begging
entries.usage: Bolog aaz, mal lir! [Beg (for) mercy, little worm!] (Draugr, 0004C59E)
entries.connotations: To ask for possession of something, or to ask to be granted something. Usually implies submission.
entries.etymology: May share root with bodiis ‘to borrow’ and bolaav ‘to grant’ related to possession or ownership.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. humble adv. humbly n. humbleness, humility v. to humble, make or become humble
entries.usage: Pahlok joorre! Hin kah fen kos bonaar. Arrogant mortals! Your pride will be humbled. (Alduin, 000ED361) Loknir Mal-Tu wahlaan qethsegol aarii vahrukt, bonaar Vakeeza, wo vaat Mir wah jun do Keizaal, ahrk di ko sadon gravuun. Loknir Little-Hammer erected this stone in memory of his servant, humble Vakeeza, who swore Allegiance to the kings of Skyrim, and died in the gray autumn. (Word Wall for Mir, Animal Allegiance)
entries.connotations: Indicates submission, a positive word in the context of servants and a negative word in the context of foes.

entries.expanded_definition: n. father; leader, origin, or otherwise metaphorical father figure
entries.usage: Nafni wahlaan qethsegol bormahii vahrukt, Ragnvald, wen Zii fen mahfaeraak aak ok brod. Nafni raised this stone for his father, Ragnvald, whose spirit will forever guide his clan. (Word Wall for Zii, Become Ethereal) Nonvul Bron, dahmaan daar rok do fin Fodiiz Bormah—Pruzaan Zun ko Keizaal los hahdrim do dwiin-sil kendov. Noble Nord, remember these words of the Hoar Father—The best Weapon in Skyrim is the mind of a steel-souled warrior. (Word Wall for Zun, Disarm)
entries.notes: Fodiiz Bormah ‘Hoar Father’, seen often on Word Walls, may refer to Shor or Ysgramor.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Akatosh, father of dragons; our father
entries.usage: His doom was written when he claimed for himself the lordship that properly belongs to Bormahu - our father Akatosh. (Paarthurnax, 0009C21A) Zeymahi lost ont du'ul Bormahu. My brother was once the crown of our father. (Paarthurnax, 0009C213)
entries.connotations: Not a name but a grammatical construction that refers to the speaker’s father. Only refers to Akatosh when used by dragons.
entries.etymology: Bormah ‘father’ with the possessive suffix ‘u’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: v. to flee n. flight
entries.usage: Alduin bovul. One reason I came to your call was to test your Thu'um for myself. Alduin fled (from you). One reason I came to your call was to test your Thu'um for myself. (Odahviing, 00048F0D) Qethsegol vahrukiv daanik Fahliil kiir do Gravuun Frod, wo bovul ko Maar nol kinzon zahkrii do kruziik hokoron. This stone commemorates the doomed elf children of the Autumn Field, who fled in Terror from the sharp swords of the ancient enemy. (Word Wall for Maar, Dismay)
entries.connotations: Flight from destruction, death, or doom. Connotates cowardice, terror, or hopelessness.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. bold adv. boldly n. boldness v. to embolden, make bold
entries.usage: Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, Ahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Boziik, Dovahkiin. Nuz mey. (You are) bold, Dovahkiin. But a fool. (Dragon, 000E1707) Odahviing will come to your challenge. Boziik. Krilot. He will not be able to resist your call, from the Hill of the Dovah itself... he will come. (Paarthurnax, 000D2CF4)
entries.connotations: Connotes bravery, fearlessness, lack of hesitation, potentially to a fault. Rashness.
entries.etymology: May share adjective suffix iik with bruniik ‘savage’, daniik ‘doomed’, and kruziik ‘ancient’.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: n. specter
entries.usage: Nonvul Bron, dahmaan daar rok do fin Fodiiz Bormah—Faas ni Brendon do Dinok, fah rok los qolaas do moro, ahrk hin aak wah lot Sovngarde. Noble Nord, remember these words of the Hoar Father—Fear not the Specter of Death, for he is the herald of glory, and your guide to great Sovngarde. (Word Wall for Faas, Dismay)
entries.connotations: The shadow or presence of something to be feared.

entries.expanded_definition: n. beauty; fulfillment, satisfaction
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv paaz kulaas Yrsa, wo ensosin pah do Taazokaan voth ek Dun ahrk brii. This stone commemorates the fair princess Yrsa, who bewitched all of Tamriel with her Grace and beauty. (Word Wall for Dun, Elemental Fury)
entries.connotations: Physical beauty, or otherwise the quality of being pleasing, satisfying, fulfilling, or extraordinary.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. sister
entries.usage: Aesa wahlaan qethsegol briinahii vahrukt, Thohild fin Toor, wen smoliin ag frin ol Sahqo Heim. Aesa raised this stone for her sister, Thohild the Inferno, whose passion burned hot as the Red Forge. (Word Wall for Toor, Fire Breath)
entries.etymology: May be compound of brii ‘beauty’ and nah ‘fury’, ‘beautiful fury’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. sisterhood
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv ahzid Viik do Briinahmaar do Sot Peyt, naako wah fin laat naal ufiik do Karvag Kol. This stone commemorates the bitter Defeat of the Sisterhood of the White Rose, eaten to the last by the Trolls of Krovag Crag. (Word Wall for Viik, Disarm)
entries.etymology: From briinah ‘sister’ with the reflexive suffix -maar.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. beautiful, in form or spirit; appealing; fulfilling, satisfying adv. beautifully; satisfyingly; in an appealing manner v. to beautify, to make or become beautiful; to make or become fulfilling
entries.usage: Brit grah. I had forgotten what fine sport you mortals can provide! Beautiful battle. I had forgotten what fine sport you mortals can provide! (Mirmulnir, 00056381) Orin brit ro. I cannot leave here until you defeat Alduin, which you cannot do without my help. (A) fully beautiful balance. I cannot leave here until you defeat Alduin, which you cannot do without my help. (Odahviing, 0004DE36) Het nok brit kaaz Anurassa, wen faad nis kos evenaar orin naal Krah dinok. Here lies the beautiful cat Anurassa, whose warmth cannot be extinguished even by the Cold of death. (Word Wall for Krah, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: Physically beautiful or beautiful in spirit. Appealing, satisfying, fulfilling, or otherwise extraordinary.
entries.etymology: From brii ‘beauty’.
entries.notes: The phrase orin brit ro ‘a fully beautiful balance’ is used to express irony.

entries.expanded_definition: n. clan, esp. Nordic
entries.usage: Modir fin Gut wahlaan qethsegol zeymahii vahrukt, oskar fin Mey, wen Zul los ahlo ahrk ni sahrot Thu’um do ok brod. Modir the Far raised this stone for his brother, Oskar the Fool, whose Voice was weak, and not the mighty Thu’um of his clan. (Word Wall for Throw Voice) Brothi wahlaan qethsegol kulii bahrukt, Odrav Keyn-Haal, wo drun pogaas zin wah Brod Sahqo-Strunmah. Brothi raised this stone for her son, Odrav Anvil-Hand, who brought much honor to Clan Red-Mountain. (Word Wall for Haal, Disarm)
entries.etymology: Likely related to bron ‘Nord’ and brom ‘north’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. north, northern, northward adv. north, northerly n. north v. to move or face north
entries.usage: Meyz nu Ysmir, Dovahsebrom. Dahmaan daar rok. (You have) become now Ysmir, Dragon of the North. Remember these words. (Greybeards, 000C43AE) Ahrk ond drey sahrot Heimverlund meyz, nol hevno Brom, med Strun do uznahgaar nahkriin nol Sovngarde nimaar. And lo did the mighty Heimverlund come, from the brutal North, like a Storm of unbridled vengenace from Sovngarde itself. (Word Wall for Strun, Storm Call)
entries.etymology: Related to bron ‘Nord’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Bromjunaar, former capital of Skyrim
entries.usage: Bromjunaar - Bromjunaar - An Old Settlement, much Reduced from Former Days. Lumber and Stone. (Book, Holdings of Jarl Gjalund)
entries.etymology: Lit. ‘north kingdom’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Nord
entries.usage: Nonvul Bron, dahmaan daar rok do fin Fodiiz Bormah—Orin pruzaan dwiin aal kreh ahrk kren, nuz Slen do vahzah muz los sindugahvon. Noble Nord, remember these words of the Hoar Father—Even the best steel may bend and break, but the Flesh of a true man is unyielding. (Word Wall for Slen, Ice Form)
entries.etymology: Related to brod ‘clan’ and brom ‘north’.
entries.notes: The word bron is ‘nord’ reversed.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Jarl
entries.usage: I do not know how he came to be caught. But the bronjun... the Jarl... was very proud of his pet. (Paarthurnax, 00045D09)
entries.etymology: Lit. ‘nord-king’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. savage adv. savagely n. savageness, savagery; a savage v. to make or become savage
entries.usage: Yes. This was ages ago, you understand. There were more of us then. Before the bruniikke - the Akaviri - came and killed all my zeymah. (Paarthurnax, 00045D09) Het dir bruniik rek-grohiik Ulfeidr, kriid muz ahrk sunvaar, bruniik kinbok Sahqon Tah. Here died the savage she-wolf Ulfeidr, slayer of men and beasts, and savage leader of the Crimson Pack. (Word Wall for Tah, Animal Allegiance)
entries.etymology: May share adjective suffix iik with boziik ‘bold’, daniik ‘doomed’, and kruziik ‘ancient’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to return n. return
entries.usage: Zu'u lost daal. I have returned. (Alduin, 000ED35C) Mu daal wah golt. We will return to the ground. (We will land.) (Tamed Dragon, 0202BC5A)
entries.notes: Word of Power in Tsun’s Shout nahl daal vus ‘living return Nirn’ used to return the player from Sovngarde.

entries.expanded_definition: n. doom; fate, destiny, esp. ill-fated or unavoidable
entries.usage: Meyye! Tahrodiis aanne! Him hinde pah liiv! Zu'u hin daan! Fools! Treacherous slaves! Your hopes (are) all withered! I (am) your doom. (Alduin, 000CD9DF)

entries.expanded_definition: adj. doomed adv. doomed
entries.usage: Daanik Kendov! Doomed warrior! (Draugr, 00016949) Qethsegol vahrukiv daanik Falhliil kiir do Gravuun Frod, wo bovul ko Maar nol kinzon zahkrii do kruziik hokoron. This stone commemorates the doomed elf children of the Autumn Field, who fled in Terror from the sharp swords of the ancient enemy. (Word Wall for Maar, Dismay)
entries.etymology: From daan ‘doom’ with adjective suffix -iik.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. this, these, those, that
entries.usage: Sahloknir, krii daar joorre. Sahloknir, kill these mortals. (Alduin, 000C8EA1) Nau daar revak golt drey Freda zahrahmiik ek Laas, ful tol ek pogaan kiir filok, ahrk osos sul qahnaar ek hokoron. On this sacred ground did Freda sacrifice her life, so that her many children might escape, and some day vanquish her enemies. (Word Wall for Laas, Aura Whisper)
entries.notes: Used to indicate a specific person, place, or thing. Not a pronoun as in ‘this is good’. Not to be confused with the conjunction tol ‘that’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to push n. push
entries.usage: Fus ro dah! Force balance push! (Unrelenting Force Shout) You are ready to learn the final word of Unrelenting Force, “Dah,” which means “Push.” (Arngeir, 00078B3B)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, to physically push back or aside, exert physical force.
entries.notes: Not used to mean ‘to insist’ (‘to push for something’), or to influence a decision (as in ‘he was pushed to retreat’).

entries.expanded_definition: v. to remember n. remembrance
entries.usage: Meyz nu Ysmir, Dovahsebrom. Dahmaan daar rok. (You have) become now Ysmir, Dragon of the North. Remember these words. (Greybeards, 000C43AE) Nonvul Bron, mahfaeraak dahmaan sahrot Vahlok wen lot ahkrin shaan ney muz ahrk dovah. Noble Nord, forever remember the mighty Guardian whose great courage inspired both men and dragons. (Word Wall for Shaan, Battle Fury)
entries.connotations: Most often used as a command.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. doomed adv. doomed v. to doom, make or become doomed
entries.usage: Daanik Kendov! Doomed warrior! (Draugr, 00016949) Qethsegol vahrukiv daanik Falhliil kiir do Gravuun Frod, wo bovul ko Maar nol kinzon zahkrii do kruziik hokoron. This stone commemorates the doomed elf children of the Autumn Field, who fled in Terror from the sharp swords of the ancient enemy. (Word Wall for Maar, Dismay)
entries.etymology: From daan ‘doom’ with adjective suffix -iik.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to keep, guard, safeguard n. keeping, guarding, safeguard
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, Dovahkiin, naal ok zin los vahriin, wah dein vokul mahfaeraak ahst vaal! Dragonborn, Dragonborn, by his honor is sworn, To keep evil forever at bay! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Zu'u uth nall [sic] thurri [sic] dein daar miiraak. I (was) ordered by my lord to keep/guard this portal. (Nahkriin, 000E16FA)

entries.expanded_definition: n. keeper, guardian
entries.usage: Het nok Faal Vahlok, deinmaar do Dovahgolz ahrk aan Fus do unslaad rahgol ahrk vulom. Here lies The Guardian, keeper of the Dragonstone and a Force of eternal rage and darkness. (Word Wall for Fus, Unrelenting Force)
entries.etymology: From dein ‘to keep’ with the suffix -maar.

entries.expanded_definition: n. soil, earth
entries.usage: Het mah sahrot konahrik Aaban, kiin se Klo se Alikr, praan nu denek Keizaal. Here fell the mighty warlord Aaban, born of the Sand of the Alik’r, at rest now in the soil of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Klo, Slow Time)
entries.connotations: Possibly associated with burial.
entries.etymology: May share root with denos ‘to decline’ indicating something below or beneath.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to decline n. decline
entries.usage: Het mah Arnvid faal Staadnau, wen Haas denos mindin Kein do Galik, kolos rok ofaal dilos ahraan. here fell Arnvid the Unbound, whose Health declined after the War of Pines, in which he received a deadly wound. (Word Wall for Haas, Drain Vitality)
entries.connotations: To worsen in state or condition, to fail to improve.
entries.etymology: May share root with denek ‘soil’ indicating something below or beneath.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Daedra
entries.usage: Het ont kriist Miraak, wo ahtiid ok sahvot ol Qah, spaan naal Deyra fah ok unslaad midun. Here once stood Miraak, who wore his faith as Armor, shielded by the Daedra for his unending loyalty. (Word Wall for Qah, Dragon Aspect)
entries.connotations: Appears to refer to the Daedric Princes as a whole or in general.
entries.etymology: Possibly a loanword daedra from the ancient meric languages.
entries.notes: Only word to end with the letter ‘a,’ as opposed to ‘ah’, further indicating a loanword.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to bury n. burial
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.

entries.expanded_definition: n. fate, destiny
entries.usage: Do you have no better reason for acting than destiny? Are you nothing but a plaything of dez... of fate? (Paarthurnax, 0003F9E1) Dez motmahus. Even to the dov, who ride the currents of Time, destiny is elusive. (Paarthurnax, 000556DB) Thoringar wahlaan qethsegol monii vahrukt, Noomi, wen dez los wah Aus nin do pogaan Ogiim ronaaz. Thoringar raised this stone for his daughter’s memory, Noomi, whose fate it was to Suffer the sting of many Orc arrows. (Word Wall for Aus, Marked for Death)
entries.connotations: A person’s eventual fate, or the sense of purpose or prophecy. Personified as something that wild and fickle, beyond mortal influence.
entries.notes: Likely from the English word ‘destiny’.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. my; mine
entries.usage: Daar Lein los dii. This world is mine. (Alduin, 000ED35F) Wo meyz wah dii vul junaar? [Who comes to my dark kingdom?] (Morokei, 0008010B)
entries.connotations: First person singular possessive.
entries.notes: The possessive suffix -i can be used instead of dii to indicate first person possession.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. undead adv. undeathly, in an undead manner n. undeath v. to make or become undead
entries.usage: Diil qoth zaam! Undead tomb slave! (Soul Cairn Summon Shout)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, refers to something that is non-living. Does not refer to immortality.
entries.etymology: Shares root with other death-related words such as dilon ‘dead’ and dilos ‘deadly’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to freeze n. freezing, frost
entries.usage: Fo krah diin! Frost cold freeze! (Frost Breath Shout, 00050346) Wulfik wahlaan qethsegol judii vahrukt, Hrefna Ruvaak-Om, wen miin Diin sos do naan jul. Wulfik raised this stone in memory of his queen, Hrefna Raven-Hair, whose eyes could Freeze the blood of any man. (Word Wall for Diin, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: Word of Power alongside fo ‘frost’, both directly tied to coldness.

entries.expanded_definition: n. dragonkind, the collective spirit and embodiment of dragonkind
entries.usage: Mul qah diiv! Strength armor wyrm! (Dragon Aspect Shout, 0203540D) Qethsegol vahrukiv lot Miraak – sonaak do lot onikaan, aar do faal Diiv, ahrk hokoron do jul. This stone commemorates the great Miraak – priest of great wisdom, servant of the Wyrm, and enemy of man. (Word Wall for Diiv, Dragon Aspect)
entries.connotations: Word of Power that embodies the essence of dragonkind. Similar to related word dov ‘dragonkind’, does not refer to an individual dragon or creature, but to the entirety of their race and the power they wield. To be a ‘servant of the Wyrm’ is to serve dragonkind and its ambitions.
entries.etymology: Related to dov ‘dragon/dragonkind’.
entries.notes: Not to be confused with the vulgar word lir ‘worm’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to swallow n. swallow, swallowing
entries.usage: Alduin, feyn do jun, kruziik vokun staadnau, voth aan bahlok wah diivon fin lein! Alduin, Bane of Kings, ancient shadow unbound, with a hunger to swallow the world! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.etymology: May share root with du ‘to devour’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. dead adv. in a dead or death-like manner
entries.usage: So, it is done. Alduin dilon. The Eldest is no more, he who came before all others, and has always been. (Paarthurnax, 0009C20B) Qiilaan us dilon! [Bow before (the) dead!] (Draugr, 0004C5A1)
entries.connotations: Permanently dead, or no longer living. Can be used to describe the undead.
entries.etymology: Shares root with diil ‘undead’, dilos ‘deadly’, and dinok ‘death’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. deadly, lethal, fatal, causing death adv. lethally, fatally, in a manner that causes death n. deadliness, lethality v. to make or become deadly
entries.usage: Het mah Arnvid faal Staadnau, wen Haas denos mindin Kein do Galik, kolos rok ofaal dilos ahraan. Here fell Arnvid the Unbound, whose Health declined after the War of Pines, in which he received a deadly wound. (Word Wall for Haas, Drain Vitality)
entries.etymology: Shares root with diil ‘undead’, dilon ‘dead’, dinok ‘death’, and dir ‘to die’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. death, loss of life; end
entries.usage: Het siiv nunon dinok. Here (you will) find only death. (Dragon, 000E1706) Even I cannot see past Time's ending to what comes next. Niid [sic] koraav zeim dinoksetiid. Niid [sic] koraav zeim dinoksetiid. = “(there is) no seeing through (the) end of time” (Paarthurnax, 0009C20D) Het nok brit kaaz Anurassa, wen faad nis kos evenaar orin naal Krah dinok. Here lies the beautiful cat Anurassa, whose warmth cannot be extinguished even by the Cold of death. (Word Wall for Krah, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: Refers to literal loss of life, or metaphorically to the end of something.
entries.etymology: Shares root with diil ‘undead’, dilon ‘dead’, dilos ‘deadly’, and dir ‘to die’. Also possibly related to nok ‘to lie (dead or buried)’. Dinoksetiid DINOKSE T3D

entries.expanded_definition: n. the end of time, the ending of the current kalpa
entries.usage: Even I cannot see past Time's ending to what comes next. Niid [sic] koraav zeim dinoksetiid. Niid [sic] koraav zeim dinoksetiid. = “(there is) no seeing through (the) end of time” (Paarthurnax, 0009C20D)
entries.etymology: Se compound of dinok ‘death’ and tiid ‘time’, lit. ‘death of time’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to die
entries.usage: Dir ko maar. Die in terror. (Dragon, 00103400) Het dir bruniik rek-grohiik Ulfeidr, kriid muz ahrk sunvaar, bruniik kinbok Sahqon Tah. Here died the savage she-wolf Ulfeidr, slayer of men and beasts, and savage leader of the Crimson Pack. (Word Wall for Tah, Animal Allegiance)
entries.etymology: Shares root with diil ‘undead’, dilon ‘dead’, dilos ‘deadly’, and dinok ‘death’. Do DO +------------------------------------+---------------------------------+

entries.official_definition: Of/About, often unused in sentence formation
citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: prep. of, from, belonging to; made up of, consisting of, characterized by; about
entries.usage: Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, Aahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Het nok Faal Vahlok, deinmaar do Dovahgolz ahrk aan Fus do unslaad rahgol ahrk vulom. Here lies The Guardian, keeper of the Dragonstone and a Force of eternal rage and darkness. (WOrd Wall for Fus, Unrelenting Force) Nonvul Bron, dahmaan daar rok do fin Fodiiz Bormah - Nii los heyv do enook mun wah lahney voth ahkrin ahrk zin, leh rok Feim vodahmin kotin vulom. Noble Nord, remember these words of the Hoar Father – It is the duty of each man to live with courage and honor, lest he Fade unremembered into darkness. (Word Wall for Feim, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: More common in writing than in speech.
entries.notes: Likely inspired de "of/from" in many languages including Latin, French, Irish, and Portuguese.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: n. see dovahkiin
entries.usage: Dohaviin, your Voice is no match for mine! (Odahviing, 000CA644)
entries.notes: Most likely a misspelling of dovahkiin ‘dragonborn’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. hound, dog
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list and the Prima Games official guide.
entries.notes: Likely from English ‘dog’.

entries.official_definition: Dragon/Dragonkind/Wyrm (referring to the race of dragons)
remarks_in_definition: referring to the race of dragons
entries.expanded_definition: n. dragonkind, dragon, wyrm, the race of dragons
entries.usage: Wo lost fron wah ney dov, ahrk fin reyliik do jul, voth aan suleyk wah ronit faal krein! Who was kin to both wyrm, and the races of man, with a power to rival the sun! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) How to explain in your tongue? The dov have words for such things that joorre do not. (Paarthurnax, 000BBEAA)
entries.connotations: Refers to the race of dragons as a whole, not individual or multiple dragons. Related word diiv refers to the power and spirit of the Dov.

entries.official_definition: Dragon (also means “me” when a dragon speaks)
remarks_in_definition: also means “me” when a dragon speaks
entries.expanded_definition: n. dragon pron. me
entries.usage: Nuz aan sul, fent alok, fod fin vul dovah nok, fen kos nahlot mahfaeraak ahrk ruz! But a day, shall arise, when the dark dragon's lies, will be silenced forever and then! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Nonvul Bron, mahfaeraak dahmaan sahrot Vahlok wen lot ahkrin shaan ney muz ahrk dovah. Noble Nord, forever remember the mighty Guardian whose great courage inspired both men and dragons. (Word Wall for Shaan, Battle Fury) Sahloknir! Ziil gro dovah ulse! Sahloknir! Your soul is bound to me for eternity! (Alduin, 000CC4F2) as a pronoun is very rare, only usable in this way by dragons.
entries.connotations: Refers to an individual dragon. May also refer to dragons in general (not all dragons or the race of dragons).
entries.etymology: From dov ‘dragonkind’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. dragonstone, a ritual stone bearing a map of dragon burial mounds throughout Skyrim
entries.usage: Het nok Faal Vahlok, deinmaar do Dovahgolz ahrk aan Fus do unslaad rahgol ahrk vulom. Here lies The Guardian, keeper of the Dragonstone and a Force of eternal rage and darkness. (Word Wall for Fus, Unrelenting Force)
entries.etymology: Compound of dovah ‘dragon’ and golz ‘stone’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. dragonborn, a mortal born with the blood and soul of a dragon
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, Dovahkiin, naal ok zin los vahriin, wah dein vokul mahfaeraak ahst vaal! Dragonborn, Dragonborn, by his honor is sworn, To keep evil forever at bay! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Ful, losei Dovahkiin? Zu'u koraav nid nol dov do hi. So, you're the Dragonborn? I see nothing of the dragon about you. (Alduin, 000C8EA0)
entries.connotations: Dragon name for a mortal individual born with the soul of a dragon. Dragonborn possess a dragon’s ability to Shout and devour the souls of other dragons.
entries.etymology: Compound of dovah ‘dragon’ and kiin ‘to bear’.
entries.notes: Alternate, unofficial interpretations translate dovahkiin as dov ah kiin (‘born to hunt dragonkind’).

entries.expanded_definition: n. dragonslayer, a slayer of dragons or the slayer of a specific dragon
entries.usage: Dovahkiin los ok dovahkriid. The Dragonborn is his dragonslayer - The Dragonborn slew him. (Dragon, 000C8EA0)
entries.connotations: A formal title for someone who has slain a dragon, usually permanently. Can be used to describe past action.
entries.etymology: Compound of dovah ‘dragon’ and kriid ‘slayer’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Dragon of the North
entries.usage: Lingrah krosis saraan Strundu'ul, voth nid balaan klov praan nau. Naal Thu'umu, mu ofan nii nu, Dovahkiin, naal suleyk do Kaan, naal suleyk do Shor, ahrk naal suleyk do Atmorasewuth. Meyz nu Ysmir, Dovahsebrom. Dahmaan daar rok. Long sorrowfully (has) waited the Stormcrown, with no worthy head to rest on. By our Voice we give it now (to you), Dragonborn, by (the) power of Kyne, by the power of Shor, and by the power of Atmora-of-old. Meyz nu Ysmir, Dovahsebrom. Dahmaan daar rok.(You have) become now Ysmir, Dragon of the North. Remember these words. (Greybeards, 000C43AB, 000C43A7, 000C43A6, 000C43AE)
entries.connotations: Refers to the title ‘Ysmir Stormcrown’.
entries.etymology: Se compound of dovah ‘dragon’ and brom ‘north’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to pray n. prayer
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, fah hin kogaan mu draal! Dragonborn, for your blessing we pray! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Nonvul Bron, dahmaan daar rok do fin Fodiiz Bormah – Draal ni fah Drem, fah grik los hind do sahlo ahrk nivahriin. Noble Nord, remember these words of the Hoar Father – Pray not for Peace, for such is the wish of the weak and cowardly. (Word Wall for Drem, Kyne’s Peace)
entries.connotations: To pray to a god or deity, or to wish or hope for.
entries.etymology: Possibly related to aal ‘may’ used in prayer and well wishes.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to do n. doing, action
entries.usage: Dreh ni nahkip. Do not feed. (Paarthurnax, 0003F9E2) Het nok Fjolmod Bein-Su, wo pook ol pogaas nau gol ol ok kopraan dreh nu ko golt. Here lies Fjolmod Foul-Air, who stank as much on earth as his body does now in the ground. (Word Wall for Su, Elemental Fury)
entries.connotations: Modal verb that indicates present action. Generally unused but can specify present tense.

entries.expanded_definition: n. peace; patience, withholding aggression or eagerness
entries.usage: Kaan drem ov! Kyne peace trust! (Kyne’s Peace Shout) Drem. Patience. There are formalities which must be observed, at the first meeting of two of the dov. (Paarthurnax, 0003F890) Drem Yol Lok. Greetings. (Paarthurnax, 00077360) Nonvul Bron, dahmaan daar rok do fin Fodiiz Bormah – Draal ni fah Drem, fah grik los hind do sahlo ahrk nivahriin. Noble Nord, remember these words of the Hoar Father – Pray not for Peace, for such is the wish of the weak and cowardly. (Word Wall for Drem, Kyne’s Peace)
entries.connotations: Withholding inborn aggressiveness and hostility. In the Kyne’s Peace Shout, restrains the aggressive tendencies of wild animals. For a dragon, represents restraint from violent power rather than its absence.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: v. did, past tense of dreh
entries.usage: Ahrk fin zul, rok drey kod, nau tol morokei frod, rul lot Taazokaan motaad voth kein! And the Voice, he did wield, on that glorious field, when great Tamriel shuddered with war! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Kel drey ni viik. The Elder Scroll did not defeat me. (Alduin, 000ED35D) Het nok Yngnavar Gaaf-Kodaav, wo drey Yah moro nau Frod do Krosis, nuz sinon siiv dinok ahrk dukaan. Here lies Yngnavar Ghost-Bear, who did Seek glory on the Battlefield of Sorrows, but instead found death and dishonor. (Word Wall for Yah, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: Used to specify past tense where it might otherwise be unclear. Also indicates formality, common in prayer and commemorations.
entries.etymology: From dreh ‘to do’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. lord, master
entries.usage: Het nok un mahlaan drogge erei suleyk se Alduin vokrii. [Here lie our fallen lords until the power of Alduin (is) restored.] (Dragonstone Inscription) Het mah faasnu ronaan Undveld, aar, kriid grohiik, ahrk drog do Lot Nir. Here fell the fearless archer Undveld, servant, slayer of wolves, and lord of the Great Hunt. (Word Wall for Nir, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: May have initially referred to a dragon lord or master, but is found in broader contexts to reference a master of any kind.
entries.notes: May be from English ‘dragon’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to bring; to cause, make happen; to usher (in) n. bringing, the act of bringing; cause; causation
entries.usage: Zok frini grind ko grah drun viiki, Dovahkiin. My most eagerness (to) meet (you) in battle brought my defeat. (Odahviing, 00048F09) Brothi wahlaan qethsegol kulii vahrukt, Odrav Keyn-Haal, wo drun pogaas zin wah Brod Sahqo-Strunmah. Brothi raised this stone for her son Odrav, Anvil-Hand, who brought much honor to Clan Red-Mountain. (Word Wall for Haal, Disarm)
entries.connotations: To physically or metaphorically bring something, or to bring about something.
entries.etymology: May relate to dreh ‘to do’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to devour, consume, feast on n. devouring, consumption
entries.usage: Thurri du hin sille ko Sovngarde! My lord will feast on your souls in Sovngarde! (Mirmulnir, 00056380) Sahrotaar! Ziil los dii du! Sahrotaar, your soul is mine to devour! (Miraak, 0202A8F0)
entries.notes: Prominently featured in the dragon name Alduin ‘destroyer devour master’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. crown; any symbol of authority, power, or rightness
entries.usage: Lingrah krosis saraan Strundu'ul, voth nid balaan klov praan nau. Long sorrowfully (has) waited the Stormcrown, with no worthy head to rest on. (Greybeards, 000C43AB) Zeymahi lost ont du'ul Bormahu. My brother was once the crown of our father. (Paarthurnax, 0009C213) Dukaan DUK1N +--------------------------------------+-------------------------------+

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: adj. dishonored, dishonorable adv. dishonorably n. dishonor v. to dishonor, make or become dishonored
entries.usage: Het nok Yngnavar Gaaf-Kodaav, wo drey Yah moro nau Frod do Krosis, nuz sinon siiv dinok ahrk dukaan. Here lies Yngnavar Ghost-Bear, who did Seek glory on the Battlefield of Sorrows, but instead found death and dishonor. (Word wall for Yah, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: If related to Kaan ‘Kyne’, denotes something that is sacrilege to Kyne and the Nords as a whole.
entries.etymology: May relate to Kaan ‘Kyne’ involving a negative prefix du-.
entries.notes: Namesake of one of Miraak’s acolyte priests.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: adj. graceful, skilled adv. gracefully, skilfully; with grace n. grace, gracefulness, finesse, skill v. to make graceful or skilled
entries.usage: Su grah dun! Air battle grace! (Elemental Fury Shout) Qethsegol vahrukiv paaz kulaas Yrsa, wo ensosin pah do Taazokaan voth ek Dun ahrk brii. This stone commemorates the fair princess Yrsa, who bewitched all of Tamriel with her Grace and beauty. (Word Wall for Dun, Elemental Fury)
entries.connotations: Word of Power that embodies grace in battle. Refers to particular finesse or skill, as with a weapon or with words. Cannot be used as a verb meaning ‘to grace with one’s presence’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to curse n. curse adj. cursed, accursed; cursing
entries.usage: Dur neh viir! Curse never dying! (Summon Durnehviir Shout)
entries.connotations: Word of Power. Refers to a supernatural curse, not expletives.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. steel, steely, made of steel adv. in a steel-like manner, as if made of steel n. steel v. to make steel; to become like steel
entries.usage: Pruzaan Zun ko Keizaal los hahdrim do dwiin-sil kendov. The best Weapon in Skyrim is the mind of a steel-souled warrior. (Word Wall for Zun, Disarm) Orin pruzaan dwiin aal kreh ahrk kren, nuz Slen do vahzah muz los sindugahvon. Even the best steel may bend and break, but the Flesh of a true man is unyielding. (Word Wall for Slen, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: Significant in ancient Nordic culture as the main material of arms and armor. Anything said to be steel-like imbues the strength of the arms and armor they crafted.
entries.etymology: May share root with dwiirok ‘to carve’ relating to solid material.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to carve n. carving
entries.usage: Sigruuf wahlaan qethsegol briinahii vahrukt, Lanal, wen brit luft los ol kinzon ahrk sot ol Nus, dwiirok nol nahlaas ozinvey. Sigruuf raised this stone for his sister, Lanal, whose beautiful face was as sharp and white as a Statue, carved from living ivory. (Word Wall for Nus, Ice Form)
entries.etymology: May share root with dwiin ‘steel’ pertaining to solid material. May also relate to rok ‘word’.

entries.official_definition: Her (used equally with the “ii” form of the possessive)
remarks_in_definition: used equally with the “ii” form of the possessive
entries.expanded_definition: pron. her; hers
entries.usage: Nau daar revak golt drey Freda zahrahmiik ek Laas, ful tol ek pogaan kiir filok, ahrk osos sul qahnaar ek hokoron. On this sacred ground did Freda sacrifice her Life, so that her many children might escape, and some day vanquish her enemies. (Word Wall for Laas, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: Third person singular possessive.
entries.etymology: From rek ‘she’.
entries.notes: The possessive suffix -ii can be used instead of ek to indicate third person possession.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. each, every, all
entries.usage: Nii los heyv do enook mun wah lahney voth ahkrin ahrk zin, leh rok Feim vodahmin kotin vulom. It is the duty of each man to live with courage and honor, lest he Fade unremembered into darkness. (Word Wall for Feim, Become Ethereal)

entries.expanded_definition: v. to bewitch n. bewitchment
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv paaz kulaas Yrsa, wo ensosin pah do Taazokaan voth ek Dun ahrk brii. This stone commemorates the fair princess Yrsa, who bewitched all of Tamriel with her Grace and beauty. (Word Wall for Dun, Elemental Fury)
entries.connotations: To be enchanted by a witch, or to be enchanted as though by a witch’s spell. Negative connotation in its association with sos ‘blood’ and the Nords’ general fear of magic and witchcraft.
entries.etymology: May derive from an unattested word sosin meaning ‘witch’ or ‘witchcraft’, lit. ‘blood-master’.

entries.expanded_definition: conj. until
entries.usage: Het nok un mahlaan drogge erei suleyk se Alduin vokrii. [Here lie our fallen lords until (the) power of Alduin (is) restored.] (Dragonstone Inscription)

entries.expanded_definition: n. year
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Hrodmir fin Krent, wo sov pah ok eruvos ahrk faraan wah Nos tum krivaan do ok zeymah. This stone commemorates Hrodmir the Broken, who spent all his years and fortune to Strike down the killer of his brother. (Word Wall for Nos, Cyclone)

entries.expanded_definition: v. to extinguish n. extinguishment
entries.usage: Evenaar bahlok. Extinguish (your) hungers. (Paarthurnax, 0003F9E2) Het nok brit kaaz Anurassa, wen faad nis kos evenaar orin naal Krah dinok. Here lies the beautiful cat Anurassa, whose warmth cannot be extinguished even by the Cold of death. (Word Wall for Krah, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: To put out or end, esp. fire, light, or warmth, or something that is physically or metaphorically burning.

entries.expanded_definition: n. season
entries.usage: Evgir Unslaad has come at last. The “Season Unending.” War... without end. (Bergritte Battle-Born, 0002A795) But once Alduin is defeated - then it will be the Empire's turn. Remember - “Evgir Unslaad.” (Ulfric Stormcloak, 0004BA40)
entries.notes: Seen exclusively in the phrase evgir unslaad ‘season unending’, an ancient Nordic phrase for war. Faad F1D +--------------------------------------+-------------------------------+

entries.expanded_definition: adj. warm adv. warmly n. warmth, warmness v. to warm
entries.usage: Het nok brit kaaz Anurassa, wen faad nis kos evenaar orin naal Krah dinok. Here lies the beautiful cat Anurassa, whose warmth cannot be extinguished even by the Cold of death. (Word Wall for Krah, Frost Breath)
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.official_definition: The (rare, only used with specific proper nouns or as a sign of reverence, as in “Faal Krein - The Sun”)
entries.expanded_definition: art. the (formal)
entries.usage: Faal Kel...?! Nikriinne… Elder Scroll...? Cowards... (Alduin, 000CD9DE) Het nok Faal Vahlok, wo kron pogaas moro. Fah ok unslaad mid, rok aav dilon voth lot zin. Here lies the Guardian, who won much glory. For his eternal loyalty, he joins the dead with great honor. (Word Wall for Mid, Battle Fury) Het nok bein nahgahdinok Azaran faal Munax, wo unt wah Gron krilot dilon do Sovngarde wah lein do jul, ahrk funt. Here lies the foul necromancer Azaran the Cruel, who tried to Bind the valiant dead of Sovngarde to the world of man, and failed. (Word Wall for Gron, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Rarely used, indicates a proper noun or otherwise indicates respect or reverence. Found in more formal speech or writing, and epithets.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to fear, be afraid of n. fear
entries.usage: Faas ru maar! Fear run terror! (Dismay Shout) Ni faas, Dovahkiin! (I do) not fear (you), Dragonborn! (Odahviing, 000D2DBB) Faas ni Brendon do Dinok, fah rok los qolaas do moro, ahrk hin aak wah lot Sovngarde. Fear not the Specter of Death, for he is the herald of glory, and your guide to great Sovngarde. (Word Wall for Faas, Dismay)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, to be afraid of something that warrants fear, as in a danger, threat, or higher power.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. fearless adv. fearlessly n. fearlessness v. to make or become fearless
entries.usage: Do not be afraid. Faasnu. Let me feel the power of your Thu'um. (Paarthurnax, 000559DE) Het mah faasnu ronaan Undveld, aar, kriid grohiik, ahrk drog do Lot Nir. Here fell the fearless archer Undveld, servant, slayer of wolves, and lord of the Great Hunt. (Word Wall for Nir, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: Connotes bravery, disregarding what may be perceived by others as a threat or danger.
entries.etymology: Faas ‘fear’ with the suffix -nu.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. painful adv. painfully n. painfulness; pain v. to pain, make or cause pain
entries.usage: Faaz! Nah! “Pain, fury!” = “damn you!” (Alduin, 000D2D72) Faaz! Paak! Dinok! [Pain! Shame! Death!] (Draugr, 0004C59F)
entries.connotations: Used as a curse or a taunt in battle.
entries.etymology: May relate to aaz ‘mercy’, indicating the absence of mercy or respite. Fah F4 +-------------------------------------+--------------------------------+

entries.expanded_definition: prep. for; in order to gain or acquire; in payment or punishment of; suiting the purpose of; in the interest of, on behalf of; conj. for, because, since
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, fah hin kogaan mu draal! Dragonborn, for your blessing we pray! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Sosaal fah hin vothaarn. (You will) bleed for your disobedience (Nahkriin, 000E16F9) Dov wahlaan fah rel. Dragons were created for domination. (Paarthurnax, 0003C574) Qethsegol vahrukiv key Sarvirra, zok krin Raan alun wah fonaar odus frod, ahrk ofan ok sil fah ok drog. This stone commemorates the horse Sarvirra, the most courageous Animal ever to charge the snowy battlefields, and give his soul for his lord. (Word Wall for Raan, Animal Allegiance) Draal ni fah Drem, fah grik los hind do sahlo ahrk nivahriin. Pray not for Peace, for such is the wish of the weak and cowardly. (Word Wall for Drem, Kyne’s Peace)
entries.connotations: Not used to indicate the passage of time, eg. ‘for many years’.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: n. friend, ally or companion
entries.usage: They are very protective of me. Bahlaan fahdonne. Bahlaan fahdonne = “worthy friends” (Paarthurnax, 000B94C6) Krosis. So los mid fahdon. [Apologies]. Sorrow is (a) loyal friend. (Paarthurnax, 0009C212) Het nok kopraan do Hela, Fahdon wah pah sivaas aar do Kaan. Aal rek siiv unahzaal praan ko Feykro do Hahnu. Here lies the body of Hela, friend to all beasts and servant of Kyne. May she find eternal rest in the Forest of Dreams. (Word Wall for Kaan, Kyne’s Peace)
entries.connotations: The dragon concept of friendship differs greatly from that of mortals, closer in meaning to ‘ally’ or ‘companion’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. elf
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv daanik Fahliil kiir do Gravuun Frod, wo bovul ko Maar nol kinzon zahkrii do kruziik hokoron. This stone commemorates the doomed elf children of the Autumn Field, who fled in Terror from the sharp swords of the ancient enemy. (Word Wall for Maar, Dismay)
entries.connotations: Unknown if formal or informal, or respectful or derogatory. Ancient Nords may have used this word to avoid using the elves’ own name, ‘Mer’.
entries.etymology: May share suffix with gogil ‘goblin’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. gardener
entries.usage: Pah werid morokei Miraak, zok suleykaar do pah Sonaak wen Mul bolaav naal Fahluaan do Jul. All praise the glorious Miraak, most powerful of all priests, whose Strength was granted by the Gardener of Men. (Word Wall for Mul, Dragon Aspect)
entries.connotations: Only known usage is in the epithet fahluaan do jul ‘Gardener of Men’, referring to Hermaeus Mora.
entries.etymology: Possibly from an unattested word fahlu ‘garden’ with the suffix -aan.

entries.expanded_definition: n. fortune, wealth
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Hrodmir fin Krent, wo sov pah ok eruvos ahrk faraan wah Nos tum krivaan do ok zeymah. This stone commemorates Hrodmir the Broken, who spent all his years and fortune to Strike down the killer of his brother. (Word Wall for Nos, Cyclone)

entries.expanded_definition: v. to fade n. fade
entries.usage: Feim zii gron! Fade spirit bind! (Become Ethereal Shout) “Fade” in your tongue. Mortals have greater affinity for this Word than the dov. Everything mortal fades away in time, but the spirit remains. Ponder the meaning of spirit. Unslaad zii. Where mortal flesh may wither and die, the spirit endures. That is “Feim.” Let that meaning fill you. Su'um ahrk morah. You will find that your spirit will give you more strength. (Paarthurnax, 000E8274) Nii los heyv do enook mun wah lahney voth ahkrin ahrk zin, leh rok Feim vodahmin kotin vulom. It is the duty of each man to live with courage and honor, lest he Fade unremembered into darkness. (Word Wall for Feim, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, connototes mortality and ephemeralness. What fades away is not as significant as what is left behind. Fel FEL +---------------------------------------+------------------------------+

entries.expanded_definition: adj. feral, ferocious adv. ferociously n. ferocity, ferociousness v. to make or become feral
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list and the Prima Games official guide.
entries.notes: Likely from English ‘fell’, Old English ‘fel’ meaning ‘cruel, savage, fierce’.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: v. will (indicates future tense)
entries.usage: Nuz aan sul, fent alok, fod fin vul dovah nok, fen kos nahlot mahfaeraak ahrk ruz! But a day, shall arise, when the dark dragon's lies, will be silenced forever and then! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Nafni wahlaan qethsegol bormahii vahrukt, Rognvald, wen Zii fen mahfaeraak aak ok brod, ahrk folook ok hokoron. Nafni raised this stone for his father, Rognvald, whose Spirit will forever guide his clan, and haunt his enemies. (Word Wall for Zii, Become Ethereal) Fen du hin sille ko Sovngarde! (I) will devour your souls in Sovngarde! (Alduin, 000ED35B)
entries.connotations: Modal verb used to indicate future action.

entries.expanded_definition: v. shall (indicates future tense)
entries.usage: Nuz aan sul, fent alok, fod fin vul dovah nok, fen kos nahlot mahfaeraak ahrk ruz! But a day, shall arise, when the dark dragon's lies, will be silenced forever and then! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Fent ni filok. (You) shall not escape. (Nahkriin, 000E16F8) Nivahriin muz fent siiv nid aaz het. Cowardly men shall find no mercy here. (Morokei, 00080103)
entries.connotations: Modal verb used to indicate future action. Largely indistinguishable from fen ‘will’, except that the speaker governs the future action; e.g. fent ni filok ‘you shall not escape’ implies the speaker is directly responsible for preventing escape. This differs from fen ‘will’, where the future action may result from sources other than the speaker.
entries.etymology: From fen ‘will’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. forest
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do Hela, Fahdon wah pah sivaas aar do Kaan. Aal rek siiv unahzaal praan ko Feykro do Hahnu. Here lies the body of Hela, friend to all beasts and servant of Kyne. May she find eternal rest in the Forest of Dreams. (Word Wall for Kaan, Kyne’s Peace)

entries.expanded_definition: n. bane Alduin, feyn do jun, kruziik vokun staadnau, voth aan bahlok wah diivon fin lein! Alduin, Bane of Kings, ancient shadow unbound, with a hunger to swallow the world! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
n. mirror
entries.usage: Fiik lo sah! Mirror deceive phantom! (Phantom Form Shout) Het ont kriist Fiik do Amusan, miiraad wah hahvulon ahrk miiraak do hahnu. [Here once stood the Mirror of Amusan, doorway to nightmares and portal of dreams.] (Unused Word Wall for Fiik, Phantom Form)
entries.connotations: Word of Power in the Phantom Form Shout used by the Greybeards during the Dragonborn’s trials. Connotates illusion and departure from reality.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to escape n. escape
entries.usage: Fent ni filok. (You) shall not escape. (Nahkriin, 000E16F8) Nau daar revak golt drey Freda zahrahmiik ek Laas, ful tol ek pogaan kiir filok, ahrk osos sul qahnaar ek hokoron. On this sacred ground did Freda sacrifice her Life, so that her many children might escape, and some day vanquish her enemies. (Word Wall for Laas, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: Unlike bovul ‘to flee’, does not connotate terror or cowardice; finding safety, respite.
entries.etymology: May be from lok ‘sky’ in association with freedom and openness.

entries.official_definition: The (not commonly used in regular sentence structure)
citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
remarks_in_definition: not commonly used in regular sentence structure
entries.expanded_definition: art. the
entries.usage: Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, Ahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Qethsegol vahrukiv Vulgrum fin Zahkrii ko fin Ven, sovrahzun wen moro lost maltiid, nuz ko vahrukt unslaad. This stone commemorates Vulgrum the Sword in the Wind, the mercenary whose glory was brief, but in memory eternal. (Word Wall for Ven, Cyclone)
entries.notes: Rarely used, esp. in speech. Most commonly found in poetry where it can lend an extra syllable. See related word faal ‘the (formal)’, which is used more commonly in epithets and with proper nouns.

entries.expanded_definition: n. frost
entries.usage: Fo krah diin! Frost cold freeze! (Frost Breath Shout) Pah werid sonaan Lunerio, wen yuvon lovaas meyz Fo, het ko vulon. All praise the bard Lunerio, whose golden voice became Frost, here in the night. (Word Wall for Fo, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, tied to freezing cold and wind.

entries.expanded_definition: conj. when; at the time of, in the event that Ahrk fin norok paal graan fod nust hon zindro zaan! And the fiercest foes rout when they hear triumph's shout! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Ahrk fin Kel lost prodah, do ved viing ko fin krah, tol fod zeymah win kein meyz fundein! And the Scrolls have foretold, of black wings in the cold, that when brothers wage war come unfurled! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.notes: See synonym rul ‘when’, which is used exclusively at the beginning of sentences and phrases.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. hoar, hoary; venerable; weathered by age adv. venerably, in a hoary manner n. hoar, hoarfrost v. to make or become hoary; to age or grow venerable
entries.usage: Nonvul Bron, dahmaan daar rok do fin Fodiiz Bormah – Kendov krif ok kosill Vokul, nuz kaal Gaar ok jun kosill niin nau ok hokoron. Noble Nord, remember these words of the Hoar Father – the warrior fights his inner evils, but the king unleashes them on his enemies. (Word Wall for Gaar, Cyclone)
entries.connotations: Occurs only in the epithet fodiiz bormah ‘Hoar Father’ found in several Word Walls, possibly in reference to either Ysgramor or Tsun.
entries.etymology: Possibly a compound of fo ‘frost’ and iiz ‘ice’, referring to something or someone who is weathered, ancient, and almost part of the land.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. wrong, misjudged, mistaken, incorrect in judgment or opinion adv. wrongly n. wrongness, misjudgment, mistake v. to make or become wrong or misjudged Het mah spaan vahdin Valkrys, wo krif voth ahkrin, nuz los folaas wah Ov mulaag do bodiis tuz. Here fell the shield maiden Valkrys, who fought bravely, but was wrong to Trust the strength of a borrowed blade. (Word Wall for Ov, Trust)
entries.connotations: Wrong action, choice, or judgment. Does not refer to something that is morally wrong. As a verb, does not mean ‘to do wrong’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to haunt, torment, plague with fear n. haunting
entries.usage: Nafni wahlaan qethsegol bormahii vahrukt, Rognvald, wen Zii fen mahfaeraak aak ok brod, ahrk folook ok hokoron. Nafni raised this stone for his father, Rognvald, whose Spirit will forever guide his clan, and haunt his enemies. (Word Wall for Zii, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: To strike pervading fear, esp. from something that is incorporeal, inanimate, or metaphorical.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to charge (into battle) n. charge, battle charge
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv key Sarvirra, zok krin Raan alun wah fonaar odus frod, ahrk ofan ok sil fah ok drog. This stone commemorates the horse Sarvirra, the most courageous Animal ever to charge the snowy battlefields, and give his soul for his lord. (Word Wall for Raan, Animal Allegiance) Frin FRIN +--------------------------------------+-------------------------------+

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: adj. hot; eager; fervent adv. hotly; eagerly; fervently n. heat; eagerness; fervor v. to heat; to make or become eager Zok frini grind ko grah drun viiki, Dovahkiin. My most eagerness (to) meet (you) in battle brought my defeat. (Odahviing, 00048F09) Aesa wahlaan qethsegol briinahii vahrukt, Thohild fin Toor, wen smoliin ag frin ol Sahqo Heim. Aesa raised this stone for her sister, Thohild the Inferno, whose passion burned hot as the Red Forge. (Word Wall for Toor, Fire Breath)
entries.connotations: Burning with heat. Metaphorically describes a heated eagerness or fervor.

entries.expanded_definition: n. field, esp. field of battle; battlefield
entries.usage: Ahrk fin zul, rok drey kod, nau tol morokei frod, rul lot Taazokaan motaad voth kein! And the Voice, he did wield, on that glorious field, when great Tamriel shuddered with war! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Het nok Yngnavar Gaaf-Kodaav, wo drey Yah moro nau Frod do Krosis, nuz sinon siiv dinok ahrk dukaan. Here lies Yngnavar Ghost-Bear, who did Seek glory on the Battlefield of Sorrows, but instead found death and dishonor. (Word Wall for Yah, Aura Whisper) Qethsegol vahrukiv daanik Fahliil kiir do Gravuun Frod, wo bovul ko Maar nol kinzon zahkrii do kruziik hokoron. This stone commemorates the doomed elf children of the Autumn Field, who fled in Terror from the sharp swords of the ancient enemy. (Word Wall for Maar, Dismay)
entries.connotations: A field where battle has taken place or will take place. Fron FRON +-------------------------------------+--------------------------------+

entries.expanded_definition: adj. kin, kindred, related adv. in a kindred manner n. kinship, relations v. to make or become kin or related
entries.usage: Wo lost fron wah ney dov, ahrk fin reyliik do jul, voth aan suleyk wah ronit faal krein! Who was kin to both wyrm, and the races of man, with a power to rival the sun! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: Related by blood or heritage.
