entries.expanded_definition: adj. ephemeral, temporary adv. ephemerally, temporarily n. ephemeralness, temporariness v. to make or become temporary
entries.usage: Joor zah frul! Mortal finite temporary! (Dragonrend Shout)
entries.connotations: Attested only as a Word of Power in the Dragonrend Shout. Not immortal or everlasting, entirely contrary to a dragon’s perspective of existence.
entries.etymology: Likely an antonym from ul ‘eternity’.

entries.expanded_definition: adv. so, thus, in this way conj. so, so that, in order that
entries.usage: Ful nii los. So it is / So be it. (Paarthurnax, 0009C20C) Nau daar revak golt drey Freda zahrahmiik ek Laas, ful tol ek pogaan kiir filok, ahrk osos sul qahnaar ek hokoron. On this sacred ground did Freda sacrifice her Life, so that her many children might escape, and some day vanquish her enemies. (Word Wall for Laas, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: Occurs separately as an adverb and a conjunction.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to tell n. telling
entries.usage: Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, Ahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)

entries.expanded_definition: v. to unfurl, unfold, esp. wings n. unfurling, unfolding
entries.usage: Ahrk fin Kel lost prodah, do ved viing ko fin krah, tol fod zeymah win kein meyz fundein! And the Scrolls have foretold, of black wings in the cold, that when brothers wage war come unfurled! (Book, Song of Skyrim)

entries.expanded_definition: v. to fail n. failure, failing
entries.usage: Rok funta koraav. He failed to see. (Paarthurnax, 0009C218) Het nok bein nahgahdinok Azaran faal Munax, wo unt wah Gron krilot dilon do Sovngarde wah lein do jul, ahrk funt. Here lies the foul necromancer Azaran the Cruel, who tried to Bind the valiant dead of Sovngarde to the world of man, and failed. (Word Wall for Gron, Become Ethereal)
entries.etymology: From unt ‘to try’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. force
entries.usage: Fus ro dah! Force balance push! (Unrelenting Force Shout) Ro fus... maybe you only balance the forces that work to quicken the end of this world. (Paarthurnax, 00055771) It is called “Force” in your tongue. But as you push the world, so does the world push back. Think of the way force may be applied effortlessly. Imagine but a whisper pushing aside all in its path. That is “Fus.” Let its meaning fill you. Su'um ahrk morah. You will push the world harder than it pushes back. (Paarthurnax, 000E8276) Het nok Faal Vahlok, deinmaar do Dovahgolz ahrk aan Fus do unslaad rahgol ahrk vulom. Here lies The Guardian, keeper of the Dragonstone and a Force of eternal rage and darkness. (Word Wall for Fus, Unrelenting Force)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, noun only. Embodies physical force and power.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. ghost
entries.usage: Zu'u ni faas gaaffesejul. I do not fear mortal ghosts (“ghosts of men/humans”). (Alduin, 000ED366) Het nok Yngnavar Gaaf-Kodaav, wo drey Yah moro nau Frod do Krosis, nuz sinon siiv dinok ahrk dukaan. Here lies Yngnavar Ghost-Bear, who did Seek glory on the Battlefield of Sorrows, but instead found death and dishonor. (Word Wall for Yah, Aura Whisper)

entries.expanded_definition: n. mortal ghosts, souls of mankind
entries.usage: Zu'u ni faas gaaffesejul. I do not fear mortal ghosts (“ghosts of men/humans”). (Alduin, 000ED366)
entries.connotations: Refers to mortal souls in the afterlife.
entries.etymology: Se compound of gaaffe ‘ghosts’ and jul ‘mankind’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. stamina, endurance
entries.usage: Gaan lah haas! Stamina magicka health! (Drain Vitality Shout) Het nok kopraan do Svolo, wo piraak mulaag wah kriin dovah nuz ni gaan wah kriin pogaan. Here lies the body of Svolo, who possessed the strength to slay dragons, but not the stamina to slay many. (Word Wall for Gaan, Drain Vitality)
entries.connotations: Word of Power that embodies enduring strength, unyielding to fatigue. In the Drain vitality Shout, drains the victim’s stamina.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to unleash or release n. unleashing, release
entries.usage: Ven gaar nos! Wind unleash strike! (Cyclone Shout) Kendov krif ok kosiil vokul, nuz jun Gaar niin nau ok hokoron. The warrior fights his inner evils, but the king unleashes them on his enemies. (Word Wall for Gaar, Cyclone)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, connotates hitherto restrained power or force and the threat of its release.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: v. to steal n. theft, thievery
entries.usage: Het mah tahrodiis tafiir Skorji Lun-Sinak, wen klov govey naal rinik hahkun rok togaat wah gahrot. Here fell the treacherous thief Skorji LeechFingers, whose head was removed by the very axe he was attempting to steal. (Word Wall for Lun, Marked For Death)
entries.notes: Reference to Garrett, protagonist of the Thief video game series.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to yield, surrender, give up; to renounce n. yielding, surrender; renouncement
entries.usage: Dovahkiin zol [sic] mul. Zu'u gahvon miri Alduin. Dovahkiin is most strong (=stronger). I yield my allegiance (to) Alduin. (Odahviing, 000E16FF)
entries.connotations: To surrender or renounce an allegiance.

entries.expanded_definition: n. pine, pine tree
entries.usage: Het mah Arnvid faal Staadnau, wen Hass denos mindin Kein do Galik, kolos rok ofaal dilos ahraan. Here fell Arnvid the Unbound, whose Health declined after the War of Pines, in which he received a deadly wound. (Word Wall for Haas, Drain Vitality)

entries.expanded_definition: adv. yes
entries.usage: Geh, Sahloknir, kaali mir. Yes, Sahloknir, my loyal champion. (Alduin, 00035B4B)
entries.connotations: Affirmation to a question.
entries.notes: Likely from Old English ġēa ‘yes, thus, so’, origin of German ja and English yeah.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. one, a single person or thing; a person in general adj. one, single
entries.usage: Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, Ahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Wo lost fron wah ney dov, ahrk fin reyliik do jul, voth aan suleyk wah ronit faal krein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! Who was kin to both wyrm, and the races of man, with a power to rival the sun! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Pruzah wundunne wah Wuth Gein. Good travels to the old one. (Odahviing, 0009E069) Onikaan koraav gein miraad. Wisdom sees the one doorway. (Odahviing, 0004DE40) as a number should generally be avoided. Possibly from German ein or eins, meaning the number ‘one’. Geinmaar G2NM1R
entries.notes: Officially defined as the pronoun ‘one’ (‘one must be careful’, ‘the one who will save us’), but also used in dialogue as the number ‘one’.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. oneself
entries.usage: Wah Krii ko morokei kein los wah zin geinmaar. Wah dir ko morokei kein los wah zin pah do Keizaal. To Kill in glorious war is to honor oneself. To die in glorious war is to honor all of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Krii, Marked for Death)
entries.etymology: From gein ‘one’ with the reflexive suffix ‘maar’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. goblin
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do sonaan Romerius, wo unt Ru nol osos gogil, nuz motmah. Here lies the body of the bard Romerius, who tried to Run from some goblins, but slipped. (Word Wall for Ru, Dismay)
entries.etymology: May share suffix -iil with fahliil ‘elf’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. earth, land, ground
entries.usage: Gol hah dov! Earth mind dragon! (Bend Will Shout) Kreh zini! The freedom of the sky beckons! Yet I stay here, nau gol, as promised. (You) bend my honor! The freedom of the sky beckons! Yet I stay here, on earth (grounded), as promised. (Odahviing, 0004DE42) He is too strong on the wing! Bring him to gol with Dragonrend! (Paarthurnax, 000C64EE) Qethsegol vahrukiv Bhor fin Golah, wo praal het mulhaan ol Gol saraan onikiv, nunon wah meyz wuth sinon do onik. This stone commemorates Bhor the Stubborn, who sat here still as Earth awaiting enlightenment, only to become old instead of wise. (Word Wall for Gol, Bend Will) Het nok Fjolmod Bein-Su, wo pook ol pogaas nau gol ol ok kopraan dreh nu ko golt. Here lies Fjolmod Foul-Air, who stank as much on earth as his body does now in the ground. (Word Wall for Su, Elemental Fury)
entries.connotations: Word of Power that cleanses the All-Maker Stones of Solstheim from Hermaeus Mora’s influence. Antonym of lok ‘sky’. of being constant, immutable, also constricting.
entries.notes: The phrase nau gol ‘on earth’ is used to mean both ‘grounded’ (‘on the earth’) and as an idiom that means ‘while alive’, though the latter is exclusive to humans.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. stubborn, unmoving adv. stubbornly n. stubbornness v. to make or become stubborn
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Bhor fin Golah, wo praal het mulhaan ol Gol saraan onikiv, nunon wah meyz wuth sinon do onik. This stone commemorates Bhor the Stubborn, who sat here still as Earth awaiting enlightenment, only to become old instead of wise. (Word Wall for Gol, Bend Will)
entries.connotations: Connotates earth- or stone-like stubbornness, unable to be moved or changed; as fixed or set as stone.
entries.etymology: Likely from gol ‘earth’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. ground; place
entries.usage: Mu daal wah golt. We will return to the ground. / We will land. (Tamed Dragon, 0202BC5A) Nau daar revak golt drey Freda zahrahmiik ek Laas, ful tol ek pogaan kiir filok, ahrk osos sul qahnaar ek hokoron. On this sacred ground did Freda sacrifice her Life, so that her many children might escape, and some day vanquish her enemies. (Word Wall for Laas, Aura Whisper) Het nok Fjolmod Bein-Su, wo pook ol pogaas nau gol ol ok kopraan dreh nu ko golt. Here lies Fjolmod Foul-Air, who stank as much on earth as his body does now in the ground. (Word Wall for Su, Elemental Fury)
entries.connotations: Refers to the physical ground and surface of the earth, and also a metonym referring to a place or location (revak golt ‘sacred ground’). Nau golt can mean ‘on the ground’ or ‘on this ground / at this place’’.
entries.etymology: From gol ‘earth’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. stone
entries.usage: Het nok Faal Vahlok, deinmaar do Dovahgolz ahrk aan Fus do unslaad rahgol ahrk vulom. Here lies The Guardian, keeper of the Dragonstone and a Force of eternal rage and darkness. (Word Wall for Fus, Unrelenting Force)
entries.connotations: More general than qethsegol ‘stone’, which more specifically refers to Word Walls or other commemorative stones. Golz refers to any piece of the earth.
entries.etymology: From gol ‘earth’.
entries.notes: Occurs only in the compound word dovahgolz ‘dragonstone’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. young; characterized by youth-like strength and spirit adv. youngly, in a strong and spirited manner n. youth, youngness; youth-like strength and spirit v. to make or become young; to regain the strength of youth
entries.usage: Goraan! I feel younger than I have in many an age. (Paarthurnax, 0009E073)
entries.connotations: For dragons, may be closer in meaning to liveliness, spirit, and strength that would be characteristic of youth, rather than youth itself.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: v. to remove, esp. by cutting; to cut off or cut out n. removal, esp. by cut
entries.usage: Het mah tahrodiis tafiir Skorji Lun-Sinak, wen klov govey naal rinik hahkun rok togaat wah gahrot. Here fell the treacherous thief Skorji LeechFingers, whose head was removed by the very axe he was attempting to steal (Word Wall for Lun, Marked For Death)
entries.connotations: Specifically to remove with a blade or by cutting. May be used metaphorically to describe sudden or violent removal.
entries.etymology: Likely from vey ‘to cut’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. green adv. greenly n. green, greenness v. to make or become green
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to rout, flee from battle n. rout
entries.usage: Ahrk fin norok paal graan fod nust hon zindro zaan! And the fiercest foes rout when they hear triumph's shout! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: To flee from battle, esp. in defeat or a loss of courage.
entries.etymology: Possibly related to grah ‘battle’.
entries.notes: Intransitive verb, not used to mean ‘to defeat or drive to rout’ (‘the enemy routed’ versus ‘we routed the enemy’).

entries.expanded_definition: v. to battle, face in battle n. battle
entries.usage: Su grah dun! Air battle grace! (Elemental Fury Shout) There is no distinction between debate and combat to a dragon. Tinvaak los grah. For us it is one and the same. (Paarthurnax, 0005597E) Zok frini grind ko grah drun viiki, Dovahkiin. My most eagerness (to) meet (you) in battle brought my defeat. (Odahviing, 00048F09) Qethsegol vahrukiv kril Thjodrek, wo dir zohungaar ko Grah do Vith Okaaz. This stone commemorates the brave Thjodrek, who died heroically in the Battle of the Serpent Sea. (Word Wall for Grah, Elemental Fury)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, embodies the contest of strength, ability, and Voice. Refers to a singular battle, not overarching struggle or conflict.

pronunciations_as_printed: /ˈgrɑ zeɪˌmɑ zin, ˈgrɑ zeɪˌmɑ noun zɪn/
entries.expanded_definition: n. ally, battle companion
entries.usage: Do me this simple honor and I will fight at your side as your Grah-Zeymahzin, your Ally, and teach you my Thu’um. (Durnehviir, 0201157B)
entries.connotations: A person who fights alongside someone in battle. Connotates loyalty but not subservience, allegiance that is given as a matter of respect but not owed.
entries.etymology: Hyphenated compound of grah ‘battle’ and zeymahzin ‘companion’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. stratagem, trick; strategy, tactic, esp. one involving trickery
entries.usage: My... eagerness to meet you in battle was my... undoing, Dovahkiin. I salute your, hmm, low cunning in devising such a grahmindol - strategem. (Odahviing, 00048F09) Zu'u ni tahrodiis. It was you that lured me here and took me prisoner... vobalaan grahmindol. I (am) not treacherous. It was you that lured me here and took me prisoner... unworthy stratagem. (Odahviing, 0004DE32)
entries.connotations: A deception or trick in battle, connotations of cowardice and dishonor, something no worthy opponent would resort to.
entries.etymology: Compound of grah ‘battle’ and mindol ‘thought’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. cloud
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.
entries.connotations: Dragon perspective of clouds might connotate gloom, uncertainty, or turbulence.
entries.notes: In Norse mythology, Gram is the sword with which Sigurd kills the dragon Fafnir.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. autumn, fall
entries.usage: Loknir Mal-Tu wahlaan qethsegol aarii vahrukt, bonaar Vakeeza, wo vaat Mir wah jun do Keizaal, ahrk dir ko sadon gravuun. Loknir Little-Hammer erected this stone in memory of his servant, humble Vakeeza, who swore Allegiance to the kings of Skyrim, and died in the gray autumn. (Word Wall for Mir, Animal Allegiance) Qethsegol vahrukiv daanik Fahliil kiir do Gravuun Frod, wo bovul ko Maar nol kinzon zahkrii do kruziik hokoron. This stone commemorates the doomed elf children of the Autumn Field, who fled in Terror from the sharp swords of the ancient enemy. (Word Wall for Maar, Dismay)
entries.connotations: If related to grah ‘battle’, may connotate times of war and the hardships resulting from those times.
entries.etymology: May derive from grah ‘battle’.
entries.notes: Only instance of uu that is transliterated without an apostrophe, and the only instance where uu is not the only vowel of the word. Should not be spoken as three syllables or with a glottal stop.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. such, so, someone or something indicated
entries.usage: Grik los lein. Such is the world. (Paarthurnax, 0009C20C) Draal ni fah Drem, fah grik los hind do sahlo ahrk nivahriin. Pray not for Peace, for such is the wish of the weak and cowardly. (Word Wall for Drem, Kyne’s Peace)
entries.notes: Pronoun only, not ‘such’ as in ‘such bravery’ or ‘such a fool’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to meet, come together, encounter n. meeting, encounter
entries.usage: Zok frini grind ko grah drun viiki, Dovahkiin. My most eagerness (to) meet (you) in battle brought my defeat. (Odahviing, 00048F09) Het nok kopraan do Iglif Iiz-Sos, wo grind ok oblaan ni ko morokei vukein, nuz ahst munax haalvut do liiv krasaar. Here lies the body of Iglif Ice-Blood, who met his end not in glorious combat, but at the cruel touch of the withering sickness. (Word Wall for Iiz, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: To meet, come together, or encounter, as in battle. Metaphorically, to encounter a fate or consequence.
entries.etymology: May relate to gron ‘to bind’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. bound, tied, linked, past part. of gron adv. in a bound, tied, or linked manner
entries.usage: Sahloknir! Ziil gro dovah ulse! Sahloknir! Your soul is bound to me for eternity! (Alduin, 000CC4F2)
entries.connotations: Closer in meaning to ‘linked’, describing a physical or metaphysical bond or relationship, rather than ‘tethered’ or ‘fastened’ (‘bound by chains’). Describes a bond between spirits or fates, or a bond to an oath, but not imprisonment.
entries.etymology: From gron ‘to bind’.
entries.notes: Not a verb indicating eventuality, as in ‘they are bound to lose’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. wolf
entries.usage: Het dir bruniik rek-grohiik Ulfeidr, kriid muz ahrk sunvaar, bruniik kinbok Sahqon Tah. Here died the savage she-wolf Ulfeidr, slayer of men and beasts, and savage leader of the Crimson Pack. (Word Wall for Tah, Animal Allegiance) Het mah faasnu ronaan Undveld, aar, kriid grohiik, ahrk drog do Lot Nir. Here fell the fearless archer Undveld, servant, slayer of wolves, and lord of the Great Hunt. (Word wall for Nir, Aura Whisper) Het mah Hrothmar, Bah Grohiik do bruniik pindaar. Aal ok sil rovaan Sovngarde mahfaeraak. Here fell Hrothmar, Wrath Wolf of the savage plains. May his soul wander Sovngarde forever. (Word Wall for Bah, Storm Call)
entries.connotations: Fearsome, savage, and vicious. No connotations of nobility or respect. More ‘beast’ than ‘animal’.
entries.etymology: May share suffix -iik with ufiik ‘troll’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to bind, tie, link n. bond, tie, link
entries.usage: Feim zii gron! Fade spirit bind! (Become Ethereal Shout) Het nok bein nahgahdinok Azaran faal Munax, wo unt wah Gron krilot dilon do Sovngarde wah lein do jul, ahrk funt. Here lies the foul necromancer Azaran the Cruel, who tried to Bind the valiant dead of Sovngarde to the world of man, and failed. (Word Wall for Gron, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, closer in meaning to ‘link’ rather than ‘tether’ or ‘chain’. Describes a permanent physical or metaphysical bond or relationship, a bond between spirits or fates, or a bond to an oath. Generally does not refer to imprisonment.
entries.notes: Pronunciation of /grɑn/ is atypical and should be avoided to prevent a homophone with graan ‘to rout’.
entries.doubt: definition is cut short in the copy; the expanded definition has "to bind"

entries.expanded_definition: v. to betray n. betrayal
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.
entries.connotations: Possibly specific to defying an order.
entries.etymology: May derive from uth ‘order, command’, to defy an order or command.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. far adv. distantly n. distance v. to distance, make or become far Zul mey gut! Voice fool far! (Throw Voice Shout) And he is no fool. Ni mey, rinik gut nol. Far from it. He began as the wisest and most far-seeing of us all. (Paarthurnax, 000556DB) Modir fin Gut wahlaan qethsegol zeymahii vahrukt, Oskar fin Mey, wen Zul los sahlo, ahrk ni sahrot Thu’um do ok brod. Modir the Far raised this stone for his brother, Oskar the Fool, whose Voice was weak, and not the mighty Thu’um of his clan. (Word Wall for Throw Voice)
entries.connotations: Physical distance, or conceptual distance.

entries.expanded_definition: n. hand
entries.usage: Zun haal viik! Weapon hand defeat! (Disarm Shout) Brothi wahlaan qethsegol kulii vahrukt, Odrav Keyn-Haal, wo drun pogaas zin wah Brod Sahqo-Strunmah. Brothi raised this stone for her son Odrav, Anvil-Hand, who brought much honor to Clan Red-Mountain. (Word Wall for Haal, Disarm)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, encompasses the physical hand and its involvement with weapons in battle.
entries.notes: Noun only, not the verb ‘to exchange by hand’. Also does not mean ‘worker’ or ‘helper’ as in ‘farmhand’.

citations: Book: Dragon Language, Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: v. to touch, feel with one’s hand n. touch, feeling, esp. by hand
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do Iglif Iiz-Sos, wo grind ok oblaan ni ko morokei vukein, nuz ahst munax haalvut do liiv krasaar. Here lies the body of Iglif Ice-Blood, who met his end not in glorious combat, but at the cruel touch of the withering sickness. (Word Wall for Iiz, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: Specifically to touch with one’s hand. May be used metaphorically, as though touched by the hand of something.
entries.etymology: From haal ‘hand’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. health
entries.usage: Gaan lah haas! Stamina magicka health! (Drain Vitality Shout) Het mah Arnvid faal Staadnau, wen Haas denos mindin Kein do Galik, kolos rok ofaal dilos ahraan. Here fell Arnvid the Unbound, whose Health declined after the War of Pines, in which he received a deadly wound. (Word Wall for Haas, Drain Vitality)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, embodies physical health and strength, living power.
entries.etymology: Possibly from laas ‘life’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. mind
entries.usage: Gol hah dov! Earth mind dragon! (Bend Will Shout)
entries.connotations: Occurs independently only as Word of Power. Is the root of many related words such as hahnu ‘dream’ and hahvulon ‘nightmare’. Synonym hahdrim ‘mind’, not a Word of Power, is more common in speech than hah. Encompasses the faculties of thought, understanding, and free will.

entries.expanded_definition: n. mind Our hadrimme [sic], our minds cannot even... comprehend its concepts. (Paarthurnax, 000B94B7) Pruzaan Zun ko Keizaal los hahdrim do dwiin-sil kendov. The best Weapon in Skyrim is the mind of a steel-souled warrior. (Word Wall for Zun, Disarm)
entries.connotations: Encompasses the faculties of thought, understanding, and free will. More commonly used than synonym and root hah ‘mind’, which exclusively occurs as a Word of Power.
entries.etymology: From hah ‘mind’.
entries.notes: Not the verb ‘to tolerate’. Officially listed as hahdrim but plural form is misspelled in the dialogue file as hadrimme.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. axe, ax
entries.usage: Het mah tahrodiis tafiir Skorji Lun-Sinak, wen klov govey naal rinik hahkun rok togaat wah gahrot. Here fell the treacherous thief Skorji LeechFingers, whose head was removed by the very axe he was attempting to steal. (Word Wall for Lun, Marked for Death)
entries.notes: Likely from French hache ‘axe’, related to English ‘hatchet’ and ‘hack’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to dream n. dream
entries.usage: Het mah Herfodr Shul-Kriid, sahrot konahrik do Lumnaar do Krent Hahnu. Here fell Herfodr Sun-Slayer, mighty warlord of the Valley of Broken Dreams. (Word Wall for Shul, Fire Breath) Het ont kriist Fiik do Amusan, miiraad wah hahvulon ahrk miiraak do hahnu. [Here once stood the Mirror of Amusan, doorway to nightmares and portal of dreams.] (Unused Word Wall for Fiik, Phantom Form)
entries.connotations: Connotates a departure from consciousness and free will, separation from the living mind.
entries.etymology: From hah ‘mind’ with the suffix -nu, lit. ‘mindless, without mind’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to have a nightmare n. nightmare
entries.usage: Het ont kriist Fiik do Amusan, miiraad wah hahvulon ahrk miiraak do hahnu. [Here once stood the Mirror of Amusan, doorway to nightmares and portal of dreams.] (Unused Word Wall for Fiik, Phantom Form)
entries.connotations: A dream that involves darkness, horror, or doom.
entries.etymology: Compound of hah ‘mind’ and vulon ‘night’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: v. to forge, work at a forge n. forge; forging
entries.usage: Aesa wahlaan qethsegol briinahii vahrukt, Thohild fin Toor, wen smoliin ag frin ol Sahqo Heim. Aesa raised this stone for her sister, Thohild the Inferno, whose passion burned hot as the Red Forge. (Word wall for Toor, Fire Breath)
entries.notes: Does not mean ‘forge’ as in ‘to produce a fake’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: adv. here, this place, at this place Zu'u ni bo nol het. I (am) not moving from here. (Odahviing, 0004DE37) Het nok brit kaaz Anurassa, wen faad nis kos evenaar orin naal Krah dinok. Here lies the beautiful cat Anurassa, whose warmth cannot be extinguished even by the Cold of death. (Word Wall for Krah, Frost Breath)
entries.notes: Commonly used in Word Walls and other commemorations. Generally not used to mean ‘present’ as in ‘I am here’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: adj. brutal, harsh adv. brutally, harshly v. to harshen, make or become brutal or harsh
entries.usage: Ahrk ond drey sahrot Heimverlund meyz, nol hevno Brom, med Strun do uznahgaar nahkriin nol Sovngarde nimaar. And lo did the mighty Heimverlund come, from the brutal North, like a Storm of unbridled vengeance from Sovngarde itself. (Word Wall for Strun, Storm Call)
entries.connotations: Brutal or harsh, especially a brutal storm or a brutal winter. Describes severity in conditions, particularly weather, landscape, or other natural phenomenon.

entries.expanded_definition: n. brutality
entries.usage: Occurs only in the dragon priest name Hevnoraak.
entries.connotations: Brutal or harsh, especially a brutal storm or a brutal winter. Describes severity in conditions, particularly weather, landscape, or other natural phenomenon.
entries.etymology: From hevno ‘brutal’.
entries.notes: Second pronunciation is attributed to a character who does not speak the dragon language and should be avoided.

entries.expanded_definition: n. duty, moral or ritual obligation
entries.usage: Not until introductions are complete. Zin. Heyv. Test your Thu'um against mine, Dovahkiin! (Paarthurnax, 0003F9E6) Nii los heyv do enook mun wah lahney voth ahkrin ahrk zin, leh rok Feim vodahmin kotin vulom. It is the duty of each man to live with courage and honor, lest he Fade unremembered into darkness. (Word Wall for Feim, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Bound by honor, formality, or morals. Inborn sense of moral duty that drives action. Generally does not refer to duty as sworn by oath or owed by service (‘a servant’s duties’).

entries.expanded_definition: pron. you
entries.usage: Zu'u lost kriaan hi ont, nu hin sille fen nahkip suleyki. I've killed you once, now your souls will feed my power. (Alduin, 000ED365) Ful, losei Dovahkiin? Zu'u koraav nid nol dov do hi. So, you're the Dragonborn? I see nothing of the dragon about you. (Alduin, 000C8EA0)
entries.connotations: Second person accusative, singular or plural. Only observed in the accusative case, but unknown if it may also be nominative.
entries.notes: Pronunciation of /haɪ/ is atypical and should be avoided.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Ivarstead, formerly known as Hillgrund's Steading
entries.usage: Hillgrund's Steading - Hillgrundhofkah - A Large Farmstead Near the Base of the Monahven. (Book, Holdings of Jarl Gjalund)
entries.connotations: From hofkah ‘house’.
entries.etymology: From hofkah ‘house’.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. your
entries.usage: Meyye! Tahrodiis aanne! Him hinde [sic] pah liiv! Zu'u hin daan! Fools! Treacherous slaves! Your hopes (are) all withered! I (am) your doom. (Alduin, 000CD9DF)
entries.etymology: From hi ‘you’.
entries.notes: Special form of hin ‘your/yours’. Possibly used before words that begin with ‘h’, or particular in usage with hind ‘wish’. Use hin if unsure of whether to use hin or him. The possessive suffix -iil may be used instead of him to indicate second person possession.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: pron. your
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, fah hin kogaan mu draal! Dragonborn, for your blessing we pray! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Thurri [sic] du hin sille ko Sovngarde! My lord will feast on your souls in Sovngarde! (Mirmulnir, 00056380) Faas ni Brendon do Dinok, fah rok los qolaas do moro, ahrk hin aak wah lot Sovngarde. Fear not the Specter of Death, for he is the herald of glory, and your guide to great Sovngarde. (Word Wall for Faas, Dismay)
entries.etymology: From hi ‘you’.
entries.notes: Alternative form him possibly used before words that begin with ‘h’. The possessive suffix -iil may be used instead of hin to indicate second person possession.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to wish (for); to hope (for) n. wish; hope
entries.usage: Meyye! Tahrodiis aanne! Him hinde [sic] pah liiv! Zu'u hin daan! Fools! Treacherous slaves! Your hopes (are) all withered! I (am) your doom. (Alduin, 000CD9DF) Draal ni fah Drem, fah grik los hind do sahlo ahrk nivahriin. Pray not for Peace, for such is the wish of the weak and cowardly. (Word Wall for Drem, Kyne’s Peace)

entries.expanded_definition: n. house; farm, steading, farmstead
entries.usage: Rorik's Steading - Rorikhofkah - A Small Farmstead in the Western Plains. Grain, Leather, Horses. (Book, Holdings of Jarl Gjalund)
entries.connotations: Occurs only in place names and compound words. Denotes a house or hall that is a source of work or pride.
entries.etymology: May derive from an unattested word hof meaning ‘hall’, and kah ‘pride’, lit. ‘hall of pride’.
entries.notes: Hof is Old English for ‘house, dwelling, hall, or court’. Hofkahsejun HOFK4SE JUN

entries.expanded_definition: n. palace, hall of a king or ruler
entries.usage: The hofkahsejun has been known as Dragonsreach ever since. … Perhaps the hofkahsejun - the palace in Whiterun... Dragonsreach. It was originally built to house a captive dovah. (Paarthurnax, 00045D09, 0004591B)
entries.connotations: General word for any hall of a king or ruler, not Dragonsreach specifically.
entries.etymology: Se compound of hofkah ‘house’ and jun ‘king’, lit. ‘house of the king’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. home; homeland
entries.usage: Het mah siigonis Neivaan wo wundun Gut nol hofkiin, dir voth zin ko ahmik do Zeymahzin. [Here fell the lizard Nievaan, who wandered Far from home, and died with honor in service of the Companions.] (Unused Word Wall for Gut, Throw Voice)
entries.connotations: Birthplace, the hall where one was born and raised.
entries.etymology: May derive from an unattested word hof meaning ‘hall’, and kiin ‘birth’, lit. ‘hall of birth’.
entries.notes: Hof is Old English for ‘house, dwelling, hall, or court’.
entries.doubt: pronunciation is printed identically to that of Hofkah

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. enemy, adversary, opponent
entries.usage: Sahrot Thu'um, med aan tuz, vey zeim hokoron pah, ol fin Dovahkiin komeyt ok rein! Mighty Thu'um, like a blade, cut through enemies all, as the Dragonborn issued his roar! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) You are brave. Balaan hokoron. Your defeat brings me honor. (Mirmulnir, 00056382) Qethsegol vahrukiv daanik Fahliil kiir do Gravuun Frod, wo bovul ko Maar nol kinzon zahkrii do kruziik hokoron. This stone commemorates the doomed elf children of the Autumn Field, who fled in Terror from the sharp swords of the ancient enemy. (Word Wall for Maar, Dismay)
entries.connotations: An enemy or adversary, esp. in battle.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to hear; to listen (to), heed n. hearing; listening
entries.usage: Ahrk fin norok paal graan fod nust hon zindro zaan, Dovahkiin, fah hin kogaan mu draal! And the fiercest foes rout when they hear triumph's shout, Dragonborn, for your blessing we pray! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) I warned them against such a rash action. Even I could not foresee its consequences. Nust ni hon. They would not listen. (Paarthurnax, 0003FA42)
entries.connotations: To audibly perceive, or to listen to words or advice.

entries.expanded_definition: n. trap, lure, snare; appeal
entries.usage: Zin krif horvut se suleyk. Honor (is) fighting the lure of power. (Paarthurnax, 0003C574)
entries.connotations: A physical trap, or a metaphorical lure, appeal.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to trap, catch, ensnare
entries.usage: Horvutah med kodaav. Caught like a bear in a trap… (Odahviing, 00048F04)
entries.connotations: To catch in a trap, or as though in a trap.
entries.etymology: From horvut ‘trap’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. hero
entries.usage: Hun kaal zoor! Hero champion legend! (Call of Valor Shout)
entries.connotations: Word of Power that calls a hero from Sovngarde, embodies the heroism of legendary deeds and great strength in battle.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. heroic adv. heroically n. heroism v. to become or make heroic
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.
entries.etymology: From hun ‘hero’.
entries.notes: To avoid confusion with zohungaar ‘heroically’, hungaar should be used solely as a noun (‘heroism’), and zohungaar should be used solely as a weak adjective (‘heroic/heroically’).

entries.expanded_definition: v. to hearken (to), heed n. hearkening
entries.usage: Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, ahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.notes: Typically used in the imperative.

entries.expanded_definition: n. ice
entries.usage: Iiz slen nus! Ice flesh statue! (Ice Form Shout) Het nok kopraan do Iglif Iiz-Sos, wo grind ok oblaan ni ko morokei vukein, nuz ahst munax haalvut do liiv krasaar. Here lies the body of Iglif Ice-Blood, who met his end not in glorious combat, but at the cruel touch of the withering sickness. (Word Wall for Iiz, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, connotates enduring cold, permanency. Also connotates a lack of warmth or compassion.
entries.notes: From English ‘ice’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. master (of a skill or role)
entries.usage: Appears only in the dragon name Alduin ‘destroyer devour master’, and as the root word of inhus ‘mastery’.
entries.connotations: Refers to a master of a skill, role, or position, e.g. ‘a guild master’ or ‘a master of evil’. A leader who rules due to their skill or ability, but not in the connotation of ‘a slave master’ or ‘to serve one’s master’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. mastery
entries.usage: Thu'um se Dovahkiin inhus, Miraak. Hin suleyksejun oblaan. The Dragonborn's Voice has the mastery, Miraak. Your dominion is ended. (Sahrotaar, 0202BC55)
entries.connotations: The state of being a master, or possessing the mastery of a skill, role, or position; the right to rule based on that mastery.
entries.etymology: From in ‘master’ with the suffix -hus.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. east, eastern, eastward adv. east, easterly n. east v. to move or face east
entries.usage: Vegunthar wahlaan qethsegol bormahii vahrukt, Hungunthar Tiid-Naak, kriaan se junnesejer, kroniid se Dunkreath. Vegunthar built (this) stone (in) his father’s memory, Hungunthar Time-Eater, slayer of the Kings of the East, conqueror of Dunkreath. (Word Wall for Tiid, Slow Time)

entries.expanded_definition: n. mortal
entries.usage: Joor zah frul! Mortal finite temporary! (Dragonrend Shout) Your kind - joorre - mortals - created it as a weapon against the dov... the dragons. (Paarthurnax, 000B94B7) Bahloki nahkip sillesejoor. My hunger has been fed by mortal souls. (Alduin, 000CDDF1) Ruth wah nivahriin joor! Rage/curses to (you) cowardly mortal! (Alduin, 000C64F1)
entries.connotations: Word of Power in the Dragonrend Shout, forces a dragon to comprehend mortality. Often used to defame or slander, typically derogatory.

entries.expanded_definition: n. maw, jaws; jaw
entries.usage: Paaz Keizaal fen kos stin nol bein Alduin jot! Fair Skyrim will be free from foul Alduin's maw! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.notes: Likely from English ‘jaw’, from Old French joe. Appears in the dragon name Vuljotnaak ‘dark maw eat’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. queen
entries.usage: Wulfik wahlaan qethsegol judii vahrukt, Hrefna Ruvaak-Om, wen miin Diin sos do naan jul. Wulfik raised this stone in memory of his queen, Hrefna Raven-Hair, whose eyes could Freeze the blood of any man. (Word Wall for Diin, Frost Breath)
entries.etymology: Related to jun ‘king’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. man, men, mankind, humans, the races of man
entries.usage: Wo lost fron wah ney dov, ahrk fin reyliik do jul, voth aan suleyk wah ronit faal krein! Who was kin to both wyrm, and the races of man, with a power to rival the sun! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Zu'u ni faas gaaffesejul. I do not fear mortal ghosts (“ghosts of men/humans”). (Alduin, 000ED366) Qethsegol vahrukiv lot Miraak – sonaak do lot onikaan, aar do faal Diiv, ahrk hokoron do jul. This stone commemorates the great Miraak – priest of great wisdom, servant of the Wyrm, and enemy of man. (Word Wall for Diiv, Dragon Aspect) Wulfik wahlaan qethsegol judii vahrukt, Hrefna Ruvaak-Om, wen miin Diin sos do naan jul. Wulfik raised this stone in memory of his queen, Hrefna Raven-Hair, whose eyes could Freeze the blood of any man. (Word Wall for Diin, Frost Breath) referring to an individual man is incorrect and should be mun ‘man’ instead.
entries.connotations: Similar to dov, refers to mankind as a whole, not individual men.
entries.etymology: Possibly related to joor ‘mortal’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. king; supreme ruler of any kind; a king’s guidance, guiding light as though led by a king
entries.usage: Alduin, feyn do jun, kruziik vokun staadnau, voth aan bahlok wah diivon fin lein! Alduin, Bane of Kings, ancient shadow unbound, with a hunger to swallow the world! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Pogaan nahlaas, vokrii wah jun. Many alive, restored to (the) light. (Paarthurnax, 000D2CF5) Kendov krif ok kosiil Vokul, nuz jun Gaar niin nau ok hokoron. The warrior fights his inner evils, but the king unleashes them on his enemies. (Word Wall for Gaar, Cyclone) as meaning ‘light’ is likely a typo of kun ‘light’. Junaar JUN1R
entries.connotations: A person with supreme rule to whom all loyalty is owed. May also refer to a king’s guidance (‘light’), not ‘light’ as in ‘sunlight’ or ‘light armor’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. kingdom, any place ruled by a king
entries.usage: Wo meyz wah dii vul junaar? [Who comes to my dark kingdom?] (Morokei, 0008010B)
entries.connotations: A place ruled by a king. Refers to a geographical area, in contrast with the general word suleyksejun ‘dominion’.
entries.etymology: From jun ‘king’.
entries.notes: Also featured in the place name Bromjunaar (lit. ‘north-kingdom’).

entries.expanded_definition: n. champion, victor of battle; defender of a cause or person
entries.usage: Hun kaal zoor! Hero champion legend! (Call of Valor Shout) Geh, Sahloknir, kaali mir. Yes, Sahloknir, my loyal champion. (Alduin, 00035B4B)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, connotates someone who has conquered the field of battle and serves a higher cause or authority.
entries.notes: The Kaal Kaaz (‘Champion Cat’) is the name of a ship that the Five Hundred Companions sailed from Atmora to Skyrim in Songs of the Return.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Kyne, Nordic goddess of the wind
entries.usage: Kaan drem ov! Kyne peace trust! (Kyne’s Peace Shout) Naal Thu'umu, mu ofan nii nu, Dovahkiin, naal suleyk do Kaan, naal suleyk do Shor, ahrk naal suleyk do Atmorasewuth. By our Voice we give it now (to you), Dragonborn, by (the) power of Kyne, by the power of Shor, and by the power of Atmora-ofold. (Greybeards, 000C43A7) Het nok kopraan do Hela, Fahdon wah pah sivaas aar do Kaan. Aal rek siiv unahzaal praan ko Feykro do Hahnu. Here lies the body of Hela, friend to all beasts and servant of Kyne. May she find eternal rest in the Forest of Dreams. (Word Wall for Kaan, Kyne’s Peace)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, Kyne is closely associated with the wind, animals, and nature. Nords believe she gave birth to them at the Throat of the World. She is credited with giving mankind the power of the Thu’um, either by her own doing or through the use of Paarthurnax.
entries.etymology: Possibly related to kiin ‘birth’, as Kyne is the ‘Mother of Men’. May be a loanword of the Nordic name Kyne, or the origin of the Nordic name.

entries.expanded_definition: n. cat; Khajiit
entries.usage: Het nok brit kaaz Anurassa, wen faad nis kos evenaar orin naal Krah dinok. Here lies the beautiful cat Anurassa, whose warmth cannot be extinguished even by the Cold of death. (Word Wall for Krah, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: Originally means ‘cat’ but also used to refer to Khajiit, likely not derogatory.
entries.notes: The Kaal Kaaz (‘Champion Cat’) is the name of a ship that the Five Hundred Companions sailed from Atmora to Skyrim in Songs of the Return. Kah K4 +---------------------------------------+------------------------------+

entries.expanded_definition: adj. proud, prideful adv. proudly n. pride v. to make proud
entries.usage: Pahlok joorre! Hin kah fen kos bonaar. Arrogant mortals! Your pride will be humbled. (Alduin, 000ED361)
entries.connotations: Self-worth or esteem, superior in worth or strength.
entries.notes: Featured in the dragon name Kahvozein ‘pride undo worship’.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: v. to war (against) n. war
entries.usage: Ahrk fin zul, rok drey kod, nau tol morokei frod, rul lot Taazokaan motaad voth kein! And the Voice, he did wield, on that glorious field, when great Tamriel shuddered with war! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Ahrk fin Kel lost prodah, do ved viing ko fin krah, tol fod zeymah win kein meyz fundein! And the Scrolls have foretold, of black wings in the cold, that when brothers wage war come unfurled! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Wah Krii ko morokei kein los wah zin geinmaar. Wah dir ko morokei kein los wah zin pah do Keizaal. To Kill in glorious war is to honor oneself. To die in glorious war is to honor all of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Krii, Marked for Death)
entries.connotations: Refers to a specific war or war in general, prolonged conflict.
entries.notes: Not to be confused with Kaan ‘Kyne’. The phrase evgir unslaad ‘season unending’ is an idiom for war.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Skyrim
entries.usage: Paaz Keizaal fen kos stin nol bein Alduin jot! Fair Skyrim will be free from foul Alduin's maw! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) I warn you, once you've flown the skies of Keizaal, your envy of the dov will only increase. (Odahviing, 0004DE3C) Het mah sahrot konahrik Aaban, kiin se Klo se Alikr, praan nu denek Keizaal. Here fell the mighty warlord Aaban, born of the Sand of the Alik’r, at rest now in the soil of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Klo, Slow Time)
entries.connotations: May refer to a broader geographical region than contemporary boundaries would indicate; the lands and sky east of the Draudach Mountains, north of the Jerall Mountains, and west of the Velothi Mountains.
entries.etymology: May share root with unahzaal ‘unending’ that means ‘end’ or ‘edge’.
entries.notes: The Nords once referred to Skyrim as ‘Mereth’ in reference to the elves who dwelled there (Book, Yngol and the SeaGhosts).

entries.official_definition: Elder Scroll (abbreviated to “Scroll” in the Song of the Dragonborn)
remarks_in_definition: abbreviated to “Scroll” in the Song of the Dragonborn
entries.expanded_definition: n. Elder Scroll
entries.usage: Ahrk fin Kel lost prodah, do ved viing ko fin krah, tol fod zeymah win kein meyz fundein! And the Scrolls have foretold, of black wings in the cold, that when brothers wage war come unfurled! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Kel drey ni viik. The Elder Scroll did not defeat me. (Alduin, 000ED35D) Kelle vomindok. The Elder Scrolls are unknown/unknowable. (Paarthurnax, 000BD16A) It is an... artifact from outside time. It does not exist, but it has always existed. … They are...hmm... fragments of creation. The Kelle... Elder Scrolls, as you name them, they have often been used for prophecy. Yes, your prophecy comes from an Elder Scroll. But this is only a small part of their power. (Paarthurnax, 000BBEAA, 000BBEA8)
entries.connotations: Proper noun that refers exclusively to the Elder Scrolls and they powers they possess.
entries.etymology: May be related to pel ‘to write’.
entries.notes: PrimaGames.com definition suggests kel is a general word for ‘scroll’ rather than a proper noun. However, kel is only ever used in reference to the Elder Scrolls, and there is no indication besides the PrimaGames.com note that an unabbreviated name exists. Kel should be used only to mean ‘Elder Scroll’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. warrior
entries.usage: Kendov krif ok kosiil Vokul, nuz jun Gaar niin nau ok hokoron. The warrior fights his inner evils, but the king unleashes them on his enemies. (Word Wall for Gaar, Cyclone) Pruzaan Zun ko Keizaal los hahdrim do dwiin-sil kendov. The best Weapon in Skyrim is the mind of a steel-souled warrior. (Word Wall for Zun, Disarm) Qethsegol vahrukiv Kendov se Ved Ronax, Sille nu yoriik pindaar se Sovngarde pah Ul. This stone commemorates the warriors of the Black Regiment, whose souls now march on the plains of Sovngarde for all Eternity. (Word Wall for Ul, Slow Time)
entries.connotations: A person in battle sworn to a king or oath. Connotes bravery and honor.
entries.etymology: Possibly from kein ‘war’ and/or ov ‘trust’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. tempest
entries.usage: Wuld nah kest! Whirlwind fury tempest! (Whirlwind Sprint Shout) Bekkhild wahlaan qethsegol ahmulii vahrukt, Eyolf, wen veysun los sizaan ko vul Kest ko Okaaz do Luv. Bekkhild raised this stone for her husband, Eyolf, whose ship was lost in a dark Tempest in the Sea of Tears. (Word Wall for Kest, Whirlwind Sprint)
entries.connotations: Word of Power in the Whirlwind Sprint Shout, embodies swift and sudden power, esp. that of the wind.

entries.expanded_definition: n. horse, steed
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv key Sarvirra, zok krin Raan alun wah fonaar odus frod, ahrk ofan ok sil fah ok drog. This stone commemorates the horse Sarvirra, the most courageous Animal ever to charge the snowy battlefields, and give his soul for his lord. (Word Wall for Raan, Animal Allegiance)

entries.expanded_definition: v. to work or shape at an anvil; to beat, hammer, or shape as though on an anvil n. anvil
entries.usage: Brothi wahlaan qethsegol kulii vahrukt, Odrav Keyn-Haal, wo drun pogaas zin wah Brod Sahqo-Strunmah. Brothi raised this stone for her son Odrav, Anvil-Hand, who brought much honor to Clan Red-Mountain. (Word Wall for Haal, Disarm)

entries.expanded_definition: n. wife
entries.usage: Lo ni hin kiim, fah rek los wol ko hin spaan, dwiin ko hin zahkrii. [Deceive not your wife, for she is (the) oak in your shield, and (the) steel in your sword.] (Unused Word Wall for Lo, Phantom Form)
entries.connotations: Connotes motherhood.
entries.etymology: Shares root with kiin ‘to birth’ and kiir ‘child’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to bear, birth, give birth to; to begin n. birth; beginning adj. birthing; born, originating (from), descended (from)
entries.usage: Het mah sahrot konahrik Aaban, kiin se Klo se Alikr, praan nu denek Keizaal. Here fell the mighty warlord Aaban, born of the Sand of the Alik’r, at rest now in the soil of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Klo, Slow Time)
entries.connotations: Can reference any birth or beginning. Does not mean ‘bear’ as in ‘to bear weight’ or ‘to bear arms’.
entries.etymology: Shares root with kiim ‘wife’ and kiir ‘child’.
entries.notes: Most commonly seen in the compound word dovahkiin ‘dragonborn’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. child
entries.usage: Di [sic] kiirre fen alok. My children will rise. (Alduin, 000ED35E) Nau daar revak golt drey Freda zahrahmiik ek Laas, ful tol ek pogaan kiir filok, ahrk osos sul qahnaar ek hokoron. On this sacred ground did Freda sacrifice her Life, so that her many children might escape, and some day vanquish her enemies. (Word Wall for Laas, Aura Whisper) Qethsegol vahrukiv kiir jun Jafnhar, wo los ag nahlaas naal Yol do lot dovah Lodunost. This stone commemorates the child king Jafnhar, who was burned alive by the Fire of the great dragon Lodunost. (Word Wall for Yol, Fire Breath)
entries.connotations: For dragons (esp. Alduin), refers to anything one is responsible for creating or giving life to.
entries.etymology: Shares root with kiim ‘wife’ and kiin ‘to birth’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. leader, esp. old and experienced
entries.usage: Het dir bruniik rek-grohiik Ulfeidr, kriid muz ahrk sunvaar, bruniik kinbok Sahqon Tah. Here died the savage she-wolf Ulfeidr, slayer of men and beasts, and savage leader of the Crimson Pack. (Word Wall for Tah, Animal Allegiance)
entries.connotations: Connotates someone that leads as a result of age, wisdom, or experience.
entries.etymology: May derive from bok ‘age’, though bok only refers to a period of time. Possibly a compound of kiin ‘born’ and bok, ‘born of age’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: adj. sharp adv. sharply n. sharpness v. to sharpen
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv daanik Fahliil kiir do Gravuun Frod, wo bovul ko Maar nol kinzon zahkrii do kruziik hokoron. This stone commemorates the doomed elf children of the Autumn Field, who fled in Terror from the sharp swords of the ancient enemy. (Word Wall for Maar, Dismay)

entries.expanded_definition: n. food
entries.usage: Occurs only in the compound words kipraan ‘meal’ and nahkip ‘to feed’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. meal, feast, esp. one had while sitting or lying down
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do Omluth fin Mey, wo unt wah nahkip bruniik Uderfrykte, sinon meyz kipraan. Here lies (the) body of Omluth the Fool, who tried to feed (the) savage Uderfrykte, (but) instead became (the) meal. (Unused Word Wall for Mey, Throw Voice)
entries.connotations: Connotates a devotion to eating; rest had while eating.
entries.etymology: Possibly a compound of kip ‘food’ and praan ‘to rest’. May also relate to kopraan ‘body’, in a carnivorous sense.
entries.notes: Does not refer to ‘meal’ as in ‘bonemeal’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. sand
entries.usage: Tiid klo ul! Time sand eternity! (Slow Time Shout) Het mah sahrot konahrik Aaban, kiin se Klo se Alikr, praan nu denek Keizaal. Here fell the mighty warlord Aaban, born of the Sand of the Alik’r, at rest now in the soil of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Klo, Slow Time)
entries.connotations: Word of Power in the Slow Time Shout. Shares connotations with the passage of time, ephemeralness, the erosion of land over the ages, and the shifting of sand over time.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. head
entries.usage: Het mah tahrodiis tafiir Skorji Lun-Sinak, wen klov govey naal rinik hahkun rok togaat wah gahrot. Here fell the treacherous thief Skorji LeechFingers, whose head was removed by the very axe he was attempting to steal. (Word Wall for Lun, Marked for Death) Ko KO +-------------------------------------+--------------------------------+

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: prep. in, inside (of), within; at, within the boundaries of; during, in the course of, over; participating in; by means of; experiencing
entries.usage: Ahrk fin Kel lost prodah, do ved viing ko fin krah, tol fod zeymah win kein meyz fundein! And the Scrolls have foretold, of black wings in the cold, that when brothers wage war come unfurled! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Thurri [sic] du hin sille ko Sovngarde! My lord will feast on your souls in Sovngarde! (Mirmulnir, 00056380) Wah Krii ko morokei kein los wah zin geinmaar. Wah dir ko morokei kein los wah zin pah do Keizaal. To Kill in glorious war is to honor oneself. To die in glorious war is to honor all of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Krii, Marked for Death) Qethsegol vahrukiv daanik Fahliil kiir do Gravuun Frod, wo bovul ko Maar nol kinzon zahkrii do kruziik hokoron. This stone commemorates the doomed elf children of the Autumn Field, who fled in Terror from the sharp swords of the ancient enemy. (Word Wall for Maar, Dismay)
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: v. to wield, use, esp. in battle; to possess a weapon or power n. wielding, usage, use, utilization
entries.usage: Ahrk fin zul, rok drey kod, nau tol morokei frod, rul lot Taazokaan motaad voth kein! And the Voice, he did wield, on that glorious field, when great Tamriel shuddered with war! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: To wield or use a weapon, instrument, or power, esp. in battle, or to possess a weapon, instrument, or power. Kodaav KOD1V +--------------------------------+-------------------------------------+

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. bear
entries.usage: Horvutah med kodaav. Caught like a bear in a trap... (Odahviing, 00048F04) Het nok Yngnavar Gaaf-Kodaav, wo drey Yah moro nau Frod do Krosis, nuz sinon siiv dinok ahrk dukaan. Here lies Yngnavar Ghost-Bear, who did Seek glory on the Battlefield of Sorrows, but instead found death and dishonor. (Word Wall for Yah, Aura Whisper)
entries.notes: Not to be confused with kiin ‘to bear, give birth to’
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: v. to bless n. blessing interj. thanks; thankfully
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, fah hin kogaan mu draal! Dragonborn, for your blessings we pray! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) I cannot tell you in detail. I never heard it used. Kogaan. It was the first Thu'um created solely by mortals. Kogaan = blessings (“thankfully”) (Paarthurnax, 0003FA43) There is no question. You are doom-driven. Kogaan Akatosh. The very bones of the earth are at your disposal. Kogaan Akatosh = “blessed of Akatosh” (Paarthurnax, 000C64EC)
entries.connotations: The intervention or influence of a god, fate, or other power. Also used to express relief or gratitude, referring to something as though it were a blessing.

entries.expanded_definition: n. crag, cliff, ridge, any protrusion of the earth
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv ahzid Viik do Briinahmaar do Sot Peyt, naako wah fin laat naal ufiik do Korvag Kol. This stone commemorates the bitter Defeat of the Sisterhood of the White Rose, eaten to the last by the Trolls of Korvag Crag. (Word Wall for Viik, Disarm)
entries.etymology: From gol ‘earth’.

entries.expanded_definition: conj. in which, during which, where, whereat
entries.usage: Het mah Arnvid faal Staadnau, wen Hass denos mindin Kein do Galik, kolos rok ofaal dilos ahraan. Here fell Arnvid the Unbound, whose Health declined after the War of Pines, in which he received a deadly wound. (Word Wall for Haas, Drain Vitality)
entries.etymology: Compound of ko ‘in’ and los ‘to be’.
entries.notes: Conjunction only, not to be confused for the adverb ‘where’ as in ‘Where is Whiterun?’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to issue, let loose n. issuing
entries.usage: Sahrot Thu'um, med aan tuz, vey zeim hokoron pah, ol fin Dovahkiin komeyt ok rein! Mighty Thu'um, like a blade, cut through enemies all, as the Dragonborn issued his roar! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Alduin komeyt tiid. Alduin set loose (by) time. (Paarthurnax, 000B94C5)

entries.expanded_definition: n. warlord Het mah Herfodr Shul-Kriid, sahrot konahrik do Lumnaar do Krent Hahnu. Here fell Herfodr Sun-Slayer, mighty warlord of the Valley of Broken Dreams. (Word Wall for Shul, Fire Breath)
entries.connotations: Someone who has triumphed in war, and leads in battle.
entries.etymology: May be related to qahnaar ‘to vanquish’ and qahnaarin ‘vanquisher’.
entries.notes: Namesake of the ninth dragon priest mask.

entries.expanded_definition: n. summer
entries.usage: Lok vah koor! Sky spring summer! (Clear Skies Shout)
entries.connotations: Appears only as a Word of Power, connotes fair weather and clear skies.

entries.expanded_definition: n. body, remains
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do sonaan Romerius, wo unt Ru nol osos gogil, nuz motmah. Here lies the body of the bard Romerius, who tried to Run from some goblins, but slipped. (Word Wall for Ru, Dismay) Het nok Fjolmod Bein-Su, wo pook ol pogaas nau gol ol ok kopraan dreh nu ko golt. Here lies Fjolmod Foul-Air, who stank as much on earth as his body does now in the ground. (Word Wall for Su, Elemental Fury)
entries.connotations: Used extensively in memorials. Refers exclusively to a dead body, the remains of the dead, indicating a final resting place. Contrast with slen ‘flesh’, which refers to the living body.
entries.etymology: May be a compound of ko ‘in’ and praan ‘rest’, roughly ‘in which one rests’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to see; to recognize, perceive, be aware of n. sight; recognition, perception; awareness
entries.usage: Ful, losei Dovahkiin? Zu'u koraav nid nol dov do hi. So, you're the Dragonborn? I see nothing of the dragon about you. (Alduin, 000C8EA0) Niid [sic] koraav zeim dinoksetiid. (There is) no seeing through (the) end of time. (Paarthurnax, 0009C20D) Onikaan koraav gein miraad. It is wise to recognize when you only have one choice. Onikaan koraav gein miraad = “Wisdom sees the one doorway” (Odahviing, 0004DE40)
entries.connotations: To see with one’s eyes, or to perceive in general. Should only be used to indicate understanding (as in ‘I see’) if it involves something that is physically seen. See instead mindok ‘to know’ or mindoraan ‘to understand’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Korvanjund
entries.usage: Korvanjund - A Small Fortified Settlement. Hides and Meat. (Book, Holdings of Jarl Gjalund)
entries.notes: Most likely Nordic in origin, and only exists in the dragon language as transcribed in Holdings of Jarl Gjalund.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to be, infinitive form n. being, the state of being (something) Paaz Keizaal fen kos stin nol bein Alduin jot, Dovahkiin kos fin saviik do muz! Fair Skyrim will be free from foul Alduin's maw, Dragonborn be the savior of men! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Skuldafn fen kos dinok. Skuldafn will be your death. (Dragon, 000E1704) Het nok brit kaaz Anurassa, wen faad nis kos evenaar orin naal Krah dinok. Here lies the beautiful cat Anurassa, whose warmth cannot be extinguished even by the Cold of death. (Word Wall for Krah, Frost Breath)
entries.notes: Only verb in the language that conjugates according to tense. Kos is infinitive and used either in the imperative (kos kril ‘be brave’) or with modal verbs (zu’u fen kos brave ‘I will be brave’). Kosil KOSIL +---------------------------------------+------------------------------+

entries.expanded_definition: adj. inner, inward, within, esp. within the soul or mind adv. inward, inwardly n. innerness, the state or quality of being within the mind or soul
entries.usage: Kendov krif ok kosil Vokul, nuz jun Gaar niin nau ok hokoron. The warrior fights his inner evils, but the king unleashes them on his enemies. (Word Wall for Gaar, Cyclone)
entries.connotations: Used to indicate something that is within the mind or soul, or metaphorically so. Generally not used in reference to inanimate things.
entries.etymology: Compound of ko ‘in’ and sil ‘soul’.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: prep. into; towards; to a state or condition
entries.usage: Amativ! Mu bo kotin stinselok. Onward! We fly into the sky's freedom. (Odahviing, 000E16F5) Nii los heyv do enook mun wah lahney voth ahkrin ahrk zin, leh rok Feim vodahmin kotin vulom. It is the duty of each man to live with courage and honor, lest he Fade unremembered into darkness. (Word Wall for Feim, Become Ethereal)
entries.etymology: From ko ‘in’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. cold adv. coldly n. cold, coldness v. to cool, chill, make or become cold
entries.usage: Fo krah diin! Frost cold freeze! (Frost Breath Shout) Het nok brit kaaz Anurassa, wen faad nis kos evenaar orin naal Krah dinok. Here lies the beautiful cat Anurassa, whose warmth cannot be extinguished even by the Cold of death. (Word Wall for Krah, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, embodies the freezing cold of Skyrim. Kras KRAS Het nok kopraan do Iglif Iiz-Sos, wo grind
entries.doubt: definition is misprinted in the copy (it repeats the previous entry); the expanded definition has "cold"

remarks_in_definition: Word Wall for Iiz, Ice Form
entries.usage: KRASNOV1R Occurs only in the derived
entries.etymology: adj. sick, sickly From kras ‘sick’. adv. sickly, in a sick manner v. to sicken, make sick Krasnovaar

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: From kras ‘sick’. n. sickness Kreh KREH
entries.connotations: (Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More) Lingering or unfaltering sickness, more (POGGLE, p. 1096) permanent than krasaar ‘sickness’. (PrimaGames.com)
entries.doubt: this region of the copy is interleaved; only the definition and source were read, by hand

entries.expanded_definition: adj. bent; twisted; distorted adv. in a bent or distorted manner n. bending; twist; distortion; the state or quality of being bent v. to bend, twist, distort
entries.usage: Kreh zini! (You) bend my honor! (Odahviing, 0004DE42) You have it. The Kel - the Elder Scroll. Tiid kreh... qalos. Time shudders at its touch. (Paarthurnax, 000C64EC) Orin pruzaan dwiin aal kreh ahrk kren, nuz Slen do vahzah muz los sindugahvon. Even the best steel may bend and break, but the Flesh of a true man is unyielding. (Word Wall for Slen, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: To distort, bend, or twist. May refer to physical distortion, or metaphorical distortion or tampering of a principle or thing.

entries.expanded_definition: n. sun; Magnus
entries.usage: Wo lost fron wah ney dov, ahrk fin reyliik do jul, voth aan suleyk wah ronit faal krein! Who was kin to both wyrm, and the races of man, with a power to rival the sun! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: Rarely used, refers to the celestial presence of the sun and the divine powers it possesses. See also shul ‘sun’, which has closer connotations to sunlight, daylight, heat, and fire.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to break, shatter n. breaking, shattering
entries.usage: Kren sosaal! [Break (and) bleed!] (Draugr, 0004C5A0) Orin pruzaan dwiin aal kreh ahrk kren, nuz Slen do vahzah muz los sindugahvon. Even the best steel may bend and break, but the Flesh of a true man is unyielding. (Word Wall for Slen, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: To physically break or shatter; to make pieces of something that is whole; to similarly disrupt or destroy.
entries.etymology: From kreh ‘to bend’.
entries.notes: Has an irregular past tense form in krent.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. broken, shattered, past part. of kren adv. brokenly, in a broken or shattered manner
entries.usage: Tiid krent. Time was... shattered here because of what the ancient Nords did to Alduin. (Paarthurnax, 0003FA49) Qethsegol vahrukiv Hrodmir fin Krent, wo sov pah ok eruvos ahrk faraan wah Nos tum krivaan do ok zeymah. This stone commemorates Hrodmir the Broken, who spent all his years and fortune to Strike down the killer of his brother. (Word Wall for Nos, Cyclone) Het mah Herfodr Shul-Kriid, sahrot konahrik do Lumnaar do Krent Hahnu. Here fell Herfodr Sun-Slayer, mighty warlord of the Valley of Broken Dreams. (Word Wall for Shul, FIre Breath)
entries.connotations: Not whole; disrupted, destroyed, or otherwise in fragments.
entries.etymology: From kren ‘to break’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. killer, slayer
entries.usage: Vegunthar wahlaan qethsegol bormahii vahrukt, Hungunthar Tiid-Naak, kriaan se junnesejer, kroniid se Dunkreath. Vegunthar built (this) stone (in) his father’s memory, Hungunthar Time-Eater, slayer of the Kings of the East, conqueror of Dunkreath. (Word Wall for Tiid, Slow Time)
entries.connotations: Rarely used compared to the more common kriid ‘killer/slayer’.
entries.etymology: From krii ‘to kill’ with the noun suffix -aan.
entries.notes: Not to be confused for the identical past participle of krii ‘to kill’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. killed, past part. of krii
entries.usage: Zu'u lost kriaan hi ont, nu hin sille fen nahkip suleyki. I've killed you once, now your souls will feed my power. (Alduin, 000ED365)
entries.etymology: Past participle of krii ‘to kill’.
entries.notes: Not to be confused for the identical noun kriaan ‘killer/slayer’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to fight, battle, struggle, esp. to the death n. fight, battle, struggle
entries.usage: Krif krin. Pruzah! (You) fight couragously [sic]. Good! (Mirmulnir, 0005637F) Zin krif horvut se suleyk. Honor (is) fighting the lure of power. (Paarthurnax, 0003C574) Kendov krif ok kosil Vokul, nuz jun Gaar niin nau ok hokoron. The warrior fights his inner evils, but the king unleashes them on his enemies. (Word wall for Gaar, Cyclone)
entries.connotations: To fight against, face in battle, esp. to the death.
entries.etymology: Likely shares root with krii ‘to kill’.
entries.notes: The phrase krif voth ahkrin is used to mean ‘fight bravely’ or ‘bravely fought’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to kill n. kill; killing
entries.usage: Krii lun aus! Kill leech suffer! (Marked for Death Shout) Sahloknir, krii daar joorre. Sahloknir, kill these mortals. (Alduin, 000C8EA1) Wah Krii ko morokei kein los wah zin geinmaar. Wah dir ko morokei kein los wah zin pah do Keizaal. To Kill in glorious war is to honor oneself. To die in glorious war is to honor all of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Krii, Marked for Death)
entries.connotations: For dragons, refers to permanent death.
entries.etymology: Likely shares root with krif ‘to fight’.
entries.doubt: definition is misprinted in the copy (it repeats the previous entry); the expanded definition has "to kill"

entries.expanded_definition: n. slayer, killer
entries.usage: Het dir bruniik rek-grohiik Ulfeidr, kriid muz ahrk sunvaar, bruniik kinbok Sahqon Tah. Here died the savage she-wolf Ulfeidr, slayer of men and beasts, and savage leader of the Crimson Pack. (Word Wall for Tah, Animal Allegiance) Het mah Herfodr Shul-Kriid, sahrot konahrik do Lumnaar do Krent Hahnu. Here fell Herfodr Sun-Slayer, mighty warlord of the Valley of Broken Dreams. (Word Wall for Shul, Fire Breath)
entries.connotations: More common than synonym kriaan ‘slayer’, connotates superiority in battle.
entries.etymology: From krii ‘to kill’ with the noun suffix -iid.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to slay n. slaughter
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do Svolo, wo piraak mulaag wah kriin dovah nuz ni Gaan wah kriin pogaan. Here lies the body of Svolo, who possessed the strength to slay dragons but not the Stamina to slay many. (Word Wall for Gaan, Drain Vitality)
entries.connotations: To kill, particularly a dragon, beast, or an enemy.
entries.etymology: From krii ‘to kill’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to stand n. stand; standing
entries.usage: Het ont kriist Miraak, wo ahtiid ok sahvot ol Qah, spaan naal Deyra fah ok unslaad midun. Here once stood Miraak, who wore his faith as Armor, shielded by the Daedra for his unending loyalty. (Word Wall for Qah, Dragon Aspect)

entries.expanded_definition: v. to murder n. murder
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.
entries.etymology: From krii ‘to kill’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. brave adv. bravely n. bravery, braveness v. to make or become brave
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv kril Thjodrek, wo dir zohungaar ko Grah do Vith Okaaz. This stone commemorates the brave Thjodrek, who died heroically in the Battle of the Serpent Sea. (Word Wall for Grah, Elemental Fury)
entries.connotations: Connotates bravery in battle, esp. in the face of death or defeat.
entries.etymology: May share root with krif ‘fight’ and krii ‘to kill’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. valiant adv. valiantly n. valor v. to make or become valiant
entries.usage: Odahviing will come to your challenge. Boziik. Krilot. He will not be able to resist your call, from the Hill of the Dovah itself... he will come. (Paarthurnax, 000D2CF4) Het nok bein nahgahdinok Azaran faal Munax, wo unt wah Gron krilot dilon do Sovngarde wah lein do jul, ahrk funt. Here lies the foul necromancer Azaran the Cruel, who tried to Bind the valiant dead of Sovngarde to the world of man, and failed. (Word Wall for Gron, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Greater in magnitude than kril ‘brave’ or krin ‘courageous’, connotates extreme bravery in the face of danger or challenge, or having performed a great feat.
entries.etymology: From kril ‘brave’, possibly a compound with lot ‘great’ meaning ‘great bravery’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. courageous adv. courageously v. to encourage, make or become courageous
entries.usage: Krif krin. Pruzah! (You) fight couragously [sic]. Good! (Mirmulnir, 000D2CF4) Qethsegol vahrukiv key Sarvirra, zok krin Raan alun wah fonaar odus frod, ahrk ofan ok sil fah ok drog. This stone commemorates the horse Sarvirra, the most courageous Animal ever to charge the snowy battlefields, and give his soul for his lord. (Word Wall for Raan, Animal Allegiance)
entries.etymology: May share root with krif ‘fight’ and krii ‘to kill’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. murderer, killer
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Hrodmir fin Krent, wo sov pah ok eruvos ahrk faraan wah Nos tum krivaan do ok zeymah. This stone commemorates Hrodmir the Broken, who spent all his years and fortune to Strike down the killer of his brother. (Word Wall for Nos, Cyclone)
entries.connotations: Connotes wrongful killing, not the triumph in battle implied with kriid ‘slayer’.
entries.etymology: From kriivah ‘to murder’ with the noun suffix -aan.

entries.expanded_definition: n. sorcerer
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list and Prima Games guide.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to conquer; to win, earn through victory; be victorious
entries.usage: Viik nuz ni kron. Defeat but not victory. [Defeated but not conquered.] (Paarthurnax, 0003FA46) Het nok Faal Vahlok, wo kron pogaas moro. Fah ok unslaad mid, rok aav dilon voth lot zin. Here lies the Guardian, who won much glory. For his eternal loyalty, he joins the dead with great honor. Become Ethereal (Word Wall for Mid, Battle Fury)

entries.expanded_definition: n. victory, conquest
entries.usage: Lot krongrah. You truly have the Voice of a dovah. Alduin's allies will think twice after this victory. Lot krongrah = “(a) great victory” (Paarthurnax, 00045919) You have won a mighty victory. Sahrot krongrah - one that will echo through all the ages of this world for those who have eyes to see. (Paarthurnax, 0009C212)
entries.connotations: To achieve victory in battle.
entries.etymology: Compound of kron ‘to conquer’ and grah ‘battle’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. conqueror; victor
entries.usage: Vegunthar wahlaan qethsegol bormahii vahrukt, Hungunthar Tiid-Naak, kriaan se junnesejer, kroniid se Dunkreath. Vegunthar built (this) stone (in) his father’s memory, Hungunthar Time-Eater, slayer of the Kings of the East, conqueror of Dunkreath. (Word Wall for Tiid, Slow Time)
entries.etymology: From kron ‘to conquer’ with the noun suffix -iid.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. sorrowful; unfortunate adv. sorrowfully; unfortunately n. sorrow v. to sorrow, feel sorrow; to make or become sorrowful interj. apologies, pardon, sorry
entries.usage: But you have indulged my weakness for speech long enough. Krosis. Now I will answer your question. Krosis = sorrow (“Apologies”) (Paarthurnax, 000556D9) Lingrah krosis saraan Strundu'ul, voth nid balaan klov praan nau. Long sorrowfully (has) waited the Stormcrown, with no worthy head to rest on. (Greybeards, 000C43AB) Het nok Yngnavar Gaaf-Kodaav, wo drey Yah moro nau Frod do Krosis, nuz sinon siiv dinok ahrk dukaan. Here lies Yngnavar Ghost-Bear, who did Seek glory on the Battlefield of Sorrows, but instead found death and dishonor. (Word Wall for Yah, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: Often used as an interjection to express misfortune or regret, not to be confused as exclusively meaning ‘apologies’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. ancient adv. in an ancient manner n. ancientness v. to age greatly, make or become ancient; to pass out of time or memory
entries.usage: Alduin, feyn do jun, kruziik vokun staadnau, voth aan bahlok wah diivon fin lein! Alduin, Bane of Kings, ancient shadow unbound, with a hunger to swallow the world! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Alduin, thuri! Boaan tiid vokriiha suleyksejun kruziik? Alduin, my king (overlord)! Has the time arrived (flown) to restore (unkill) your ancient dominion (power-of-king)? (Sahloknir, 00035F88) Qethsegol vahrukiv daanik Fahliil kiir do Gravuun Frod, wo bovul ko Maar nol kinzon zahkrii do kruziik hokoron. This stone commemorates the doomed elf children of the Autumn Field, who fled in Terror from the sharp swords of the ancient enemy. (Word Wall for Maar, Dismay)
entries.connotations: Refers to something old beyond memory, or powerful due to its age.
entries.etymology: May share adjective suffix iik with boziik ‘bold’ and bruniik ‘savage’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. son; child, descendant
entries.usage: Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, Ahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Brothi wahlaan qethsegol kulii vahrukt, Odrav Keyn-Haal, wo drun pogaas zin wah Brod Sahqo-Strunmah. Brothi raised this stone for her son Odrav, Anvil-Hand, who brought much honor to Clan Red-Mountain. (Word Wall for Haal, Disarm)
entries.connotations: May be a gender neutral word referring to any child, descendant, or heir given the etymology of kulaan ‘prince’ and kulaas ‘princess’.
entries.notes: Not to be confused with kul ‘good’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. good, moral good
entries.usage: Occurs only as the root of vokul ‘evil’.
entries.connotations: Refers to moral good; a good deed. rightness.
entries.etymology: Reverse-derived from vokul ‘evil’, described by official notes as ‘literally “ungood”’.
entries.notes: Not to be confused with pruzah, which means ‘good’ as in ‘well’ or ‘fair’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. prince; male heir
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list and Prima Games guide.
entries.etymology: From kul ‘son’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. princess; female heir
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv paaz kulaas Yrsa, wo ensosin pah do Taazokaan voth ek Dun ahrk brii. This stone commemorates the fair princess Yrsa, who bewitched all of Tamriel with her Grace and beauty. (Word Wall for Dun, Elemental Fury)
entries.etymology: From kul ‘son/descendant’, or likely a variation of kulaan ‘prince’ that disregards the root word kul.

entries.expanded_definition: n. light; rightness, goodness, the right path
entries.usage: I have tasted the voices of Alduin's allies on the wind. Pogaan nahlaas, vokrii wah jun [sic]. Pogaan nahlaas, vokrii wah jun [sic] = “many alive, restored to (the) light” (Paarthurnax, 000D2CF5)
entries.connotations: Literal light, or as a metaphor for right cause or purpose.
entries.etymology: Does not officially occur in-game or in official material. Based on the word vokun ‘shadow’ (most likely ‘unlight’).
entries.doubt: cites a dialogue line, but the entry says the word is inferred and the line reads jun

entries.expanded_definition: v. to want; to request; to ask, inquire n. want; request; question, query, inquiry
entries.usage: You will release me - ro laan - if in return I promise to take you to Skuldafn and stop helping Alduin? Ro laan = balanced request (Odahviing, 000E16EE) Zu'u lost ofan hin laan. I have given your want/request. (Odahviing, 00048F05)
entries.connotations: Not equivalent to ‘want’ as in ‘desire’, something that is asked or requested.
entries.notes: Ro laan ‘balanced request’ seems to a favour done in return for another favour, quid pro quo.

entries.expanded_definition: n. life
entries.usage: Laas yah nir! Life seek hunt! (Aura Whisper Shout) Hin laas los dii. Your life (is) mine. (000E16F7)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, refers to the life of an individual, not in the abstract sense (as in ‘life is short’).
entries.etymology: Possibly related to lah ‘magicka’, lahney ‘live’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. last, end or conclusion
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv ahzid viik do Briinahmaar do Sot Peyt, naako wah fin laat naal ufiik do Korvag Kol This stone commemorates the bitter Defeat of the Sisterhood of the White Rose, eaten to the last by the Trolls of Korvag Crag. (Word Wall for Viik, Disarm)
entries.connotations: Noun only, means ‘last’ or ‘end’ as in ‘the last of day’.
entries.etymology: Possibly related to unslaad ‘unending/ceaseless/eternal’

entries.expanded_definition: n. magicka
entries.usage: Lungerd wahlaan qethsegol ahmulii vahrukt Thorgrima Deinmaar do sahqon yolos ahrk drog do lah. Lungerd raised this stone in memory of her husband, Thorgrima, keeper of the crimson flame, and lord of Magicka. (Word Wall for Lah, Drain Vitality)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, refers to the essence of Magicka, not magic in general.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to live
entries.usage: Nii los heyv do enook mun wah lahney voth ahkrin ahrk zin leh rok feim vodahmin kotin vulom. It is duty of each man to live with courage and honor lest he fade unremembered into darkness. (Word Wall for Feim, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Used in the sense ‘to spend one’s life’ (not ‘to be alive’, or ‘to reside, dwell’).
entries.etymology: Likely from laas ‘life’, or related to lah ‘magicka’,

entries.expanded_definition: v. to muster, gather, esp. an army n. mustering, gathering
entries.usage: Mindoraan, pah ok middovahhe lahvraan til. As you know, all his dragon-loyalists (are) mustered there. (Odahviing, 00048F05)
entries.connotations: Primarily military in definition, ‘to gather an army’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. army
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do Wynjolf faal wuld wen viintaas tuz vey zeim lahvu do Rahgron ogiim. Here lies the body of Wynjolf the Whirlwind, whose shining blades cut through an army of angry Orcs. (Word Wall for Wuld, Whirlwind Spirit)
entries.connotations: Refers to any gathered military force.
entries.etymology: Related to lahvraan ‘muster/gather’.

entries.expanded_definition: conj. lest; for fear that
entries.usage: Nii los heyv do enook mun wah lahney voth ahkrin ahrk zin leh rok feim vodahmin kotin vulom. It is duty of each man to live with courage and honor lest he fade unremembered into darkness. (Word Wall for Feim, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Used to express fear, caution, or danger.

entries.official_definition: World (equivalent to Mundus - the universe, everything)
remarks_in_definition: equivalent to Mundus - the universe, everything
entries.expanded_definition: n. Mundus, the world; world
entries.usage: Alduin, feyn do jun, kruziik vokun staadnau, voth aan bahlok wah diivon fin lein! Alduin, Bane of Kings, ancient shadow unbound, with a hunger to swallow the world!
