(Book, Songs of Skyrim) Grik los lein. Such is the world. (Paarthurnax, 0009C20C) Daar Lein los dii. This world is mine. (Alduin, 000ED35F) Zu'u Alduin, zok sahrot do naan ko Lein. I (am still) Alduin, most mighty of any in Mundus (the world). (Alduin, 000ED362)
entries.notes: Sometime used as a proper noun; Lein means “the World” in and by itself. The definite article fin is only used for metric reasons in the Song of the Dragonborn.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to wither n. withering
entries.usage: Him hinde [sic] pah liiv! Your hopes (are) all withered! (Alduin, 000CD9DF) Het nok kopraan do Iglif Iiz-sos wo grind ok oblaan ni ko morokei vukein nuz ahst munax haalvut do liiv krasaar. Here lies the body of Iglif Ice-Blood, who met his end not in glorious combat, but at the cruel touch of the withering sickness. (World Wall for Iiz, Ice Form)
entries.notes: Often used as a participle ‘withered, withering’. Featured in the dragon name Nahagliiv ‘fury burn wither’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to diminish n. diminishment
entries.usage: Ni liivrah hin moro. Do not diminish /wither/ your glory. (Paarthurnax, 0004591A)
entries.connotations: Generally transitive, used in the transferred sense ‘to belittle’, to cause something to diminish or wither.
entries.etymology: From liiv ‘to wither’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. long, enduring, lasting adv. lengthily, at length n. length (of time), duration v. to lengthen, prolong
entries.usage: Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, Aahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Lingrah morah. Long concentration/thought. (Paarthurnax, 000D2CF5) Lingrah krosis saraan Strundu'ul, voth nid balaan klov praan nau. Long sorrowfully (has) waited the Stormcrown, with no worthy head to rest on. (Greybeards, 000C4368)
entries.connotations: Used exclusively in reference to time, not physical length or distance as in ‘a long river’ or ‘a long ways off’. See instead gut ‘far’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. worm; vermin; weakling
entries.usage: Bolog aaz, mal lir! [Beg (for) mercy, little worm!] (Draugr, 0004C59E)
entries.connotations: Vulgar, used as a taunt or insult.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to deceive n. deception
entries.usage: Fiik lo sah! Mirror deceive phantom! (Phantom Form Shout) Lo ni hin kiim, fah rek los wol ko hin spaan, dwiin ko hin zahkrii. [Deceive not your wife, for she is the oak in your shield, and the steel in your sword.] (Unused Word Wall for Lo, Phantom Form)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, associated with illusion and trickery.
entries.notes: Possibly featured in the dragon name Lodunost.

entries.expanded_definition: n. sky
entries.usage: Lok vah koor! Sky spring summer! (Clear Skies Shout) Lok, Thu'um. Sky (above), Voice (within). (Arngeir, 000BF4B0) Drem Yol Lok. Peace Fire Sky. (Paarthurnax, 0003F88B) Amativ! Mu bo kotin stinselok. Onward! We fly into the sky's freedom. (Odahviing, 000E16F5)
entries.connotations: Strong association with freedom, openness, unbridled strength and power.
entries.notes: Drem Yol Lok ‘Peace Fire Sky’ is a phrase of greeting. Similarly, Lok, Thu’um ‘Sky above, voice within’ is a phrase of parting and goodwill among the Greybeards. Featured in the dragon name Sahloknir ‘phantom sky hunt’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. fist
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to have, possess (formal or obsolete)
entries.usage: Oblivion loost nid nah med spaan vahdin beyn. Oblivion hath no Fury like a shield maiden scorned. (Word Wall for Nah, Whirlwind Spirit)
entries.connotations: Rarely seen, either formal, archaic, or obsolete.
entries.etymology: From lost ‘have/was’.
entries.notes: Though from lost ‘have’, lost is exclusively an auxiliary verb (‘have returned’), not ‘to have’ as in ‘to possess’. Piraak ‘to possess’ should be used instead of loost to avoid this confusion.

entries.official_definition: Is/Was (Combine with other verbs to form present tense: “is helping”, “Is sworn”)
remarks_in_definition: Combine with other verbs to form present tense: “is helping”, “Is sworn”
entries.expanded_definition: v. is, are, am, present or past tense conjugation of kos
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, Dovahkiin, naal ok zin los vahriin, wah dein vokul mahfaeraak ahst vaal! Dragonborn, Dragonborn, by his honor is sworn, To keep evil forever at bay! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Rok los Dovahkiin, Strundu'ul. He is Dragonborn, Stormcrown. (Einarth, 000B3980) Thu'umii los nahlot. His Voice is silenced. (Dragon, 0009E072) Nii los heyv do enook mun wah lahney voth ahkrin ahrk zin leh rok feim vodahmin kotin vulom. It is duty of each man to live with courage and honor lest he fade unremembered into darkness. (Word Wall for Feim, Become Ethereal) Qethsegol vahrukiv kiir jun Jafnhar wo los ag nahlaas nal yol do lot dovah Lodunost. This stone commemorates the child king Jafnhar, who was burned alive by the Fire of the great dragon Lodunost. (Word Wall for Yol, Fire Breath) Sigruuf wahlaan qethsegol briinahii vahrukt Lanal wen brit luft los ol kinzon ahrk sot ol nus dwiirok nol nahlaas ozinvey. Sigruuf raised this stone for his sister, Lanal, whose beautiful face was as sharp and white as a Statue, carved from living ivory. (Word Wall for Nus, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: Always indicates present tense in spoken dialogue. On Word Walls may be used for past or perfect, as well as present tense.
entries.etymology: From kos ‘be’.
entries.notes: Typically omitted from regular speech (as in Alduin mahlaan ‘Alduin (is) fallen’, rok mul ‘he (is) strong, and nu hin sil dii ‘now your soul (is) mine’). May be used to create emphasis.

entries.expanded_definition: v. you’re, contraction of los hi
entries.usage: Ful, losei Dovahkiin? Zu'u koraav nid nol dov do hi. So, you’re the Dragonborn? I see nothing of the dragon about you. (Alduin, 000C8EA0)
entries.connotations: Colloquialism, only used in question formation.
entries.etymology: Contraction of los hi ‘are you’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. have, was (indicates past and present perfect tenses)
entries.usage: Wo lost fron wah ney dov, ahrk fin reyliik do jul … Ahrk fin Kel lost prodah, do ved viing ko fin krah ... Who was kin to both wyrm, and the races of man … And the Scrolls have foretold, of black wings in the cold ... (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Zeymahi lost ont du'ul Bormahu. My brother was once the crown of our father (Paarthurnax, 0009C213) Zu'u lost kriaan hi ont I've killed you once. (Alduin, 000ED365) Lost funt. (You) have failed. (Paarthurnax, 00044C4F)
entries.etymology: From los ‘is’.
entries.notes: Can be omitted when the sense is clear, as in Zu'u uth nall [sic] thurri [sic] ‘I (was) ordered by my lord’ (000E16FA), Alduin mah ‘Alduin (has) fallen’ (000E16FD). Not used in the sense “possess, contain”. See instead piraak.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. great adv. greatly n. greatness v. to make or become great
entries.usage: Lot krongrah. (A) great victory. (Paarthurnax, 00045919) Het mah faasnu ronaan Undveld aar kriid grohiik ahrk drog do Lot Nir. Here fell the fearless archer Undveld, servant, slayer of wolves, and lord of the Great Hunt. (Word Wall for Nir, Aura Whisper) Het nok Faal Vahlok, wo kron pogaas moro. Fah ok unslaad mid, rok aav dilon voth lot zin. Here lies the Guardian, who won much glory. For his eternal loyalty, he joins the dead with great honor. (Word Wall for Mid, Battle Fury)
entries.connotations: Great in magnitude, power, or significance. Should not be used colloquially as ‘that is great’. See instead pruzah ‘good/well’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to sing; to make music; to voice through song n. music, song; singing voice
entries.usage: Pah werid Sonaan Lunerio wen yuvon lovaas meyz fo het ko vulon. All praise Bard Lunerio whose golden music became frost here in night. (Word Wall for Fo, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: Refers to ‘voice’ as in ‘singing voice’, not the voice used for speech or for Shouting.
entries.etymology: Possibly related tinvaak ‘talk’, or may share feminine suffix -aas with kulaas ‘princess’ and sivaas ‘beast/animal’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. face
entries.usage: Sigruuf wahlaan qethsegol briinahii vahrukt Lanal wen brit luft los ol kinzon ahrk sot ol nus dwiirok nol nahlaas ozinvey. Sigruuf raised this stone for his sister, Lanal, whose beautiful face was as sharp and white as a Statue, carved from living ivory. (Word Wall for Nus, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: Noun only, refers to the bodily face, rather than ‘to face in battle’. See instead grind ‘to meet’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. valley
entries.usage: Het mah Herfodr Shul-Kriid sahrot konahrik do Lumnaar do Krent Hahnu. Here fell Herfodr Sun-Slayer, mighty warlord of (the) Valley of Broken Dreams. (Word Wall for Shul, Fire Breath)
entries.etymology: Possibly a compound of naar ‘summit’ with an unattested word lum meaning ‘low’ or ‘descent’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to leech, sap n. leeching; leech, something that leeches
entries.usage: Krii lun aus! Kill leech suffer! (Marked for Death Shout) Het mah tahrodiis tafiir Skorji Lun-Sinak wen klov govey naal rinik hahkun rok togaat wah gahrot. Here fell the treacherous thief Skorji LeechFingers, whose head was removed by the very axe he was attempting to steal. (Word Wall for Lun, Marked for Death)
entries.connotations: Word of Power in the Marked for Death Shout, connotates the draining of strength and vitality. Negative connotation, as in a parasite or corruption.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to cry, to tear up n. tear; crying
entries.usage: Bekkhild wahlaan qethsegol ahmulii vahrukt Eyolf wen veysun los sizaan ko vul kest ko okaaz do luv. Bekkhild raised this stone for her husband, Eyolf, whose ship was lost in a dark Tempest in the Sea of Tears. (Word Wall for Kest, Whirlwind Spirit)
entries.etymology: Possibly related to unattested word lum found in lumnaar ‘valley’ meaning ‘low’ or ‘descent’.
entries.notes: See vaaz for the ‘tear’ in the sense of ‘to rip’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: v. to terrify, terrorize n. terror adj. terrifying, terrible; terrified, terrorized adv. terrifyingly, terribly
entries.usage: Faas ru maar! Fear run terror! (Dismay Shout) Maar saraan ko Sovngarde Terror awaits in Sovngarde. (Alduin, 000CDDF6) Qethsegol vahrukiv daanik Fahliil kiir do Gravuun Frod, wo bovul ko Maar nol kinzon zahkrii do kruziik hokoron. This stone commemorates the doomed elf children of the Autumn Field, who fled in Terror from the sharp swords of the ancient enemy. (Word Wall for Maar, Dismay)
entries.connotations: Connotes an absolute loss of courage or hope, doom.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to fall, esp. in battle n. fall
entries.usage: Zu'u tiiraaz ahst ok mah. I am sad at his fall. (Paarthurnax, 0009C20A) Alduin mah nol thur. Alduin (has) fallen from (the) overlord(ship). (Odahviing, 000E16FD) Het mah spaan vahdin Valkrys wo krif voth ahkrin nuz los folaas vah ov mulaag do bodiis tuz. Here fell the shield maiden Valkrys, who fought bravely, but was wrong to Trust the strength of a borrowed blade. (Word Wall for Ov, Kyne’s Peace)
entries.connotations: Used in the sense ‘to be defeated’, but the metaphorical phrase mah nol thur ‘fell from overlordship’ implies that the original sense is that of actual, spatial fall. Mahfaeraak M4FAER1 K

entries.expanded_definition: adv. forever
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, Dovahkiin, naal ok zin los vahriin, wah dein vokul mahfaeraak ahst vaal! Dragonborn, Dragonborn, by his honor is sworn, To keep evil forever at bay! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Nonvul Bron, mahfaeraak dahmaan sahrot Vahlok wen lot ahkrin shaan ney muz ahrk dovah. Noble Nord, forever remember the mighty Guardian whose great courage inspired both men and dragons. (Word Wall for Shaan, Battle Fury)
entries.notes: Only word in the language to use ‘ae’ instead of ‘ey’, likely created early in development.

entries.expanded_definition: v. fallen, past part. of mah
entries.usage: Alduin mahlaan. Alduin is fallen. (Dragon, 0009E051) Het nok un mahlaan drogge erei suleyk se Alduin vokrii. Here lie our fallen lords until power of Alduin (is) restored. (Dragonstone Inscription)
entries.connotations: Used in the sense ‘defeated’ or ‘killed’.
entries.etymology: Past participle of mah ‘to fall’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. little, small, short adv. in a little or small manner n. littleness, smallness, shortness v. to belittle; to shrink, make or become small
entries.usage: Bolog aaz, mal lir! [Beg (for) mercy, little worm!] (Draugr, 0004C59E) Laknir Mal-Tu wahlaan qethsegol aarii vahrukt bonaar Vakeeza wo vaat mir wah jun do Keizaal ahrk dir ko sadon gravuun. Laknir Little-Hammer raised (this) stone in memory of his servant, humble Vakeeza, who swore allegiance to (the) kings of Skyrim and died in Gray Autumn. (Word Wall for Mir, Animal Allegiance)
entries.connotations: Physically small or a small amount of time.
entries.notes: Likely from English ‘small’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. brief, short, momentary adv. briefly, shortly, momentarily n. briefness, brevity, shortness, momentariness v. to shorten, make or become brief
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Vulgrum fin Zahkrii ko fin ven sovrahzun wen moro lost maltiid nuz ko vahrukt unslaad. This stone commemorates Vulgrum the Sword in the Wind, the mercenary whose glory was brief, but in memory eternal. (Word Wall for Ven, Cyclone)
entries.connotations: Refers to a short span or duration, not used to mean ‘briefly’ or ‘shortly’ as in ‘soon’.
entries.etymology: Compound of mal ‘little’ and tiid ‘time’.
entries.notes: Antonym of lingrah ‘long (of time)’.

entries.expanded_definition: prep. like, similar to
entries.usage: Sahrot Thu'um, med aan tuz, vey zeim hokoron pah, ol fin Dovahkiin komeyt ok rein! Mighty Thu'um, like a blade, cut through enemies all, as the Dragonborn issued his roar! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Horvutah med kodaav. Caught like a bear in a trap... (Odahviing, 00048F04)
entries.connotations: May have been inspired by Scandinavian med ‘with’.
entries.etymology: May have been inspired by Scandinavian med ‘with’.
entries.notes: Not to be confused for the verb ‘to like’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to fool n. fool; foolery
entries.usage: Zul mey gut! Voice fool far! (Throw Voice Shout) Boziik, Dovahkiin. Nuz mey. (You are) bold, Dovahkiin. But a fool. (Dragon, 000E1707) Modir fin gut wahlaan qethsegol zeymahii vahrukt Oskar fin Mey wen zul los sahlo ahrk ni sahrot thu’um do ok brod. Modir the Far raised this stone for his brother, Oskar the Fool, whose Voice was weak, and not the mighty Thu’um of his clan. (Word Wall for Throw Voice)
entries.connotations: Word of Power to trick and deceive. Used as a derogatory term to refer to someone who is easily fooled, or is prone to foolish action.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to come, become n. becoming
entries.usage: Ahrk fin Kel lost prodah, do ved viing ko fin krah, tol fod zeymah win kein meyz fundein! And the Scrolls have foretold, of black wings in the cold, that when brothers wage war come unfurled! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Meyz nu Ysmir, Dovahsebrom. (You have) become now Ysmir, Dragon of the North. (Greybeards, 000C43AE) Wo meyz wah dii vul junaar? Who comes to my dark kingdom? (Morokei, 0008010B) Ahrk ond drey sahrot Heimverlund meyz nol hevno brom And lo did mighty Heimverlund come from the brutal north (Word Wall for Strun, Storm Call)
entries.notes: Can be used with nouns (‘to become king’) or adjectives (‘to become cold’). Officially defined as meaning ‘to become’, but used in some cases in the sense of ‘arrive’. Bo ‘to fly/move’ should be used instead. Mid MID +--------------------------------------+-------------------------------+

entries.expanded_definition: adj. loyal, leal adv. loyally n. loyalty v. to make or become loyal; to swear loyalty
entries.usage: Mid vur shaan! Loyal valor inspire! (Battle Fury Shout) So los mid fahdon. Sorrow is (a) loyal friend. (Paarthurnax, 0009C212) Het nok Faal Vahlok, wo kron pogaas moro. Fah ok unslaad mid, rok aav dilon voth lot zin. Here lies the Guardian, who won much glory. For his eternal loyalty, he joins the dead with great honor. Become Ethereal (Word Wall for Mid, Battle Fury) as a noun is rare, and both midun and midrot should be favored.
entries.connotations: Word of Power that inspires loyalty, embodies the bond of loyalty between allies.
entries.etymology: Shares root with mir ‘allegiance’.
entries.notes: Featured in the compound middovah ‘loyalist / dragon ally’. May possibly be compounded with other nouns to form similar words (e.g. middok ‘a loyal dog’).
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: n. dragon loyalist or ally
entries.usage: Mindoraan, pah ok middovahhe lahvraan til. As you know, all his dragon-loyalists (are) mustered there. (Odahviing, 00048F05)
entries.connotations: Can only reference dragons. See GrahZeymahzin ‘ally’ for a more general word.
entries.etymology: Compound of mid ‘loyal’ and dovah ‘dragon’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. loyalty; oath, vow; sworn word
entries.usage: Alduin sizaan midroti. Alduin has lost my loyalty. (Odahviing, 000E16FE)
entries.etymology: suggests sworn loyalty, loyalty as given by an oath. Compound of mid ‘loyal’ and rot ‘word’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. loyalty
entries.usage: Het ont kriist Miraak, wo ahtiid ok sahvot ol Qah, spaan naal Deyra fah ok unslaad midun. Here once stood Miraak, who wore his faith as Armor, shielded by the Daedra for his unending loyalty. (Word Wall for Qah, Dragon Aspect)
entries.connotations: More general than synonym midrot, which refers to loyalty specifically given by word or vow.
entries.etymology: From mid ‘loyal’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. eye
entries.usage: Wulfin wahlaan qethsegol judii vahrukt Hrefna Ruvaak-Om wen miin diin sos do naan jul. Wulfik raised this stone in memory of his queen, Hrefna Raven-Hair, whose eyes could Freeze the blood of any man. (Word Wall for Diin, Frost Breath)
entries.etymology: Possibly related to miiraad ‘doorway’, miiraak ‘portal’ (compare window from Old Norse vindauga ‘wind-eye’).

entries.expanded_definition: n. door, doorway; opening, path, option, opportunity
entries.usage: Onikaan koraav gein miraad [sic]. Wisdom sees the one doorway. (Odahviing, 0004DE40) Het ont kriist Fiik do Amusan, miiraad wah hahvulon ahrk miiraak do hahnu. Here once stood the Mirror of Amusan, doorway to nightmares and portal of dreams. (Unused Word Wall for Fiik, Phantom Form)
entries.connotations: Given dragons’ limited experience with doorways, may be a much broader word that refers to any opening, metaphorically an option or opportunity.
entries.etymology: Related to miiraak ‘portal’ (and possibly to miin ‘eye’; compare window from Old Norse vind-auga ‘wind-eye’). Might also be connected to Ayleidoon mitta ‘enter’.
entries.notes: Spelt miiraad in the dictionary on PrimaGames.com, miraad in the in-game dialogue.

entries.expanded_definition: n. portal
entries.usage: Zu'u uth nall [sic] thurri dein daar miiraak. I (was) ordered by my lord to keep/guard this portal. (Nahkriin, 000E16FA)
entries.etymology: Related to miiraad ‘doorway’ (and possibly to miin ‘eye’; compare window from Old Norse vind-auga ‘wind-eye’). May also relate to aak ‘guide’, in the sense of something that leads somewhere. Possibly connected to Ayleidoon mitta ‘enter’.
entries.notes: Not to be confused for the dragon priest name Miraak ‘allegiance-guide’.

entries.expanded_definition: prep. after
entries.usage: Het mah Arnvid faal Staadnau, wen Haas denos mindin Kein do Galik, kolos rok ofaal dilos ahraan. Here fell Arnvid the Unbound, whose Health declined after the War of Pines, in which he received a deadly wound. (Word Wall for Haas, Drain Vitality)
entries.connotations: After the time of, not pursuit (as in ‘to go after something’).

entries.expanded_definition: v. to think; to know n. thought; knowledge
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.
entries.connotations: Never occurs in dialogue or inscriptions, though the related words mindol ‘to think’, mindoraan ‘to understand’ suggest that the primary meaning is ‘to use one’s mental faculty’, not ‘believe, suppose’.
entries.etymology: Related to vomindok ‘unknown’, mindol ‘think’, mind oraan ‘understanding’.
entries.notes: Likely from English ‘mind’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to think n. thought Occurs only in the compound grahmindol ‘battle-thought’ (‘strategem’).
entries.connotations: May be closer in meaning to ‘devise’, ‘plan’, or ‘plot’ given its association with grahmindol ‘stratagem’.
entries.etymology: Related to mindok ‘to know’, mindoraan ‘to understand’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to understand, comprehend n. understanding, comprehension
entries.usage: Mindoraan, pah ok middovahhe lahvraan til. As you know, all his dragon-loyalists (are) mustered there. (Odahviing, 00048F05)

entries.expanded_definition: adj. allied, loyal adv. loyally, in the manner of an ally n. allegiance, loyalty v. to ally with, make or become loyal to
entries.usage: Raan mir tah! Animal allegiance pack! (Animal Allegiance Shout) Geh, Sahloknir, kaali mir. Yes, Sahloknir, my loyal champion. (Alduin, 00035B4B) Laknir Mal-Tu wahlaan qethsegol aarii vahrukt bonaar Vakeeza wo vaat mir wah jun do Keizaal ahrk dir ko sadon gravuun. Loknir Little-Hammer erected this stone in memory of his servant, humble Vakeeza, who swore Allegiance to the kings of Skyrim, and died in the gray autumn. (Word Wall for Mir, Animal Allegiance)
entries.connotations: Word of Power in the Animal Allegiance Shout, unwavering loyalty, the binding of cause and strength.
entries.etymology: Shares root with mid ‘loyal’
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: n. doorway, see miiraad
entries.usage: Onikaan koraav gein miraad [sic]. Wisdom sees the one doorway. (Odahviing, 0004DE40)
entries.notes: Misspelling of miiraad.

entries.expanded_definition: n. daughter
entries.usage: Thoringar wahlaan qethsegol monii vahrukt, Noomi, wen dez los wah Aus nin do pogaan Ogiim ronaaz. Thoringar raised this stone for his daughter’s memory, Noomi, whose fate it was to Suffer the sting of many Orc arrows. (Word Wall for Aus, Marked for Death)
entries.connotations: Unlike kul, specifically refers to a female child or descendant.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to mother, raise or create as a mother n. mother; origin; creator
entries.usage: Occurs only in the name Monahven ‘Throat of the World’ (lit. ‘Mother of the Wind’).
entries.etymology: From mon ‘daughter’.
entries.notes: Like bormah ‘father’, original meaning may be much broader. Associated with Kyne and nature.

entries.official_definition: Throat of the World = Mother (of the) Wind
entries.expanded_definition: n. Throat of the World Do you know why I live here, at the peak of the Monahven - what you name Throat of the World? Monahven = “Mother (of the) Wind” = dragon name for Throat of the World (Paarthurnax, 0003FA3F)
entries.connotations: Proper noun but may be used with definite articles. Refers to the entire mountain, not just the peak.
entries.etymology: Compound of monah ‘mother’ and ven ‘wind’
entries.notes: Reference to the Nordic belief that they are Children of the Sky, where the Throat of the World was “where the sky exhaled on the land and formed them” (Book, Children of the Sky). Officially noted as being dragon in origin, which either corroborates the legend or refers to ‘wind’ in a more literal sense, given the altitude and fierce winds of the mountain.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to focus, concentrate, give attention to; to contemplate, think n. focus, concentration, attention; contemplation, thought
entries.usage: Su'um ahrk morah. Breath and focus. (Paarthurnax, 000E8276) Lingrah morah. Long concentration/thought. (Paarthurnax, 000D2CF5)
entries.connotations: Refers to mental focus and concentration, meditation, and long thought. Not to be used in non-mental senses such as “to focus efforts’ or ‘to concentrate forces’. See instead ro ‘balance’.
entries.notes: Su'um ahrk morah ‘Breath and focus’ is officially noted as “sort of a mantra for the Greybeards” (0003FAF8).

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. glory Ni liivrah hin moro. Do not diminish [wither] your glory. (Paarthurnax, 0004591A) Het nok Yngnavar Gaaf-Kodaav, wo drey Yah moro nau Frod do Krosis, nuz sinon siiv dinok ahrk dukaan. Here lies Yngnavar Ghost-Bear, who did Seek glory on the Battlefield of Sorrows, but instead found death and dishonor. (Word Wall for Yah, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: Personal glory in battle.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: adj. glorious adv. gloriously v. to glorify
entries.usage: Ahrk fin zul, rok drey kod, nau tol morokei frod, rul lot Taazokaan motaad voth kein! And the Voice, he did wield, on that glorious field, when great Tamriel shuddered with war! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Wah Krii ko morokei kein los wah zin geinmaar. Wah dir ko morokei kein los wah zin pah do Keizaal. To Kill in glorious war is to honor oneself. To die in glorious war is to honor all of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Krii, Marked for Death) Zok morokei! Most glorious! (Mirmulnir, 000A27BD)
entries.connotations: Glorious as a result of triumph, or something that will bring glory.
entries.etymology: From moro ‘glory’
entries.notes: Name of one of the eight dragon priests.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to shudder, tremble, shake n. shudder, tremble, shake Ahrk fin zul, rok drey kod, nau tol morokei frod, rul lot Taazokaan motaad voth kein! And the Voice, he did wield, on that glorious field, when great Tamriel shuddered with war! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: The shaking or trembling of the earth as from some cataclysm or great power. Does not refer to fear as in ‘to tremble with fear’.
entries.etymology: Possibly related to motmah ‘slip’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to slip n. slip
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do sonaan Romerius, wo unt Ru nol osos gogil, nuz motmah. Here lies the body of the bard Romerius, who tried to Run from some goblins, but slipped. (Word Wall for Ru, Dismay)
entries.connotations: Primarily ‘to trip or fall’. Given motmahus ‘slippery/elusive’, may also be used to mean ‘to slip away’.
entries.etymology: Related to motaad ‘shudder’ and mah ‘fall’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. slippery; elusive, tricky, difficult to grasp adv. in a slippery manner; elusively n. slipperiness; elusiveness v. to make or become slippery or elusive
entries.usage: Dez motmahus. Fate is elusive/slippery. (Paarthurnax, 000556DB) Yes... one of his allies could tell us. Motmahus... But it will not be so easy to... convince one of them to betray him. Motmahus = “slippery” = “tricky” (Paarthurnax, 0004591B)
entries.connotations: Means slippery, elusive; hard to catch, difficult to grasp.
entries.etymology: From motmah ‘slip’ with the adjective suffix -us.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. we, first person plural
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, fah hin kogaan mu draal! Dragonborn, for your blessing we pray! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Mu bo kotin stinselok. We fly into the sky's freedom. (Odahviing, 000E16F5)
entries.etymology: Possibly related to zu’u ‘I’, mun ‘man’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. strong adv. strongly n. strength v. to strengthen
entries.usage: Mul qah diiv! Strength armor wyrm! (Dragon Aspect Shout) Dovahkiin zol [sic] mul. Zu'u gahvon miri Alduin. Dovahkiin is most strong (=stronger). I yield my allegiance (to) Alduin. (Odahviing, 000E16FE) Pah werid morokei Miraak, zok suleykaar do pah Sonaak wen Mul bolaav naal Fahluaan do Jul. All praise the glorious Miraak, most powerful of all priests, whose Strength was granted by the Gardener of Men. (Word Wall for Mul, Dragon Aspect)
entries.connotations: Connotes power in general, physical or otherwise. Also connotes truth, rightness, the right to rule based on strength. As a Word of Power, embodies the inborn strength and power of dragonkind.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. strong, powerful adv. strongly, powerfully, with strength n. strength, power v. to strengthen, gain power Suleyki mulaag, Paarthurnax. My power (has) strengthened, Paarthurnax. (Alduin, 00044968) Het mah spaan vahdin Valkrys, wo krif voth ahkrin, nuz los folaas wah Ov mulaag do bodiis tuz. Here fell the shield maiden Valkrys, who fought bravely, but was wrong to Trust the strength of a borrowed blade. (Word Wall for Ov, Kyne’s Peace)
entries.connotations: Refers to any form of strength or power, or the magnitude of that strength. Connotates truth, rightness, the right to rule based on strength.
entries.etymology: From mul ‘strong’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. unmoving, unchanging, still adv. unchangingly, in a still or unmoving manner n. stillness, lack of motion or change v. to still, make or become still
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Bhar fin Golah wo praal het mulhaan ol gol saraan onikiv nunon wah meyz wuth sinon do onik. This stone commemorates Bhor the Stubborn, who sat here still as Earth awaiting enlightenment, only to become old instead of wise. (Word Wall for Gol, Bend Will)
entries.etymology: Likely related to mul ‘strong’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. man, person, individual person
entries.usage: Nii los heyv do enook mun wah lahney voth ahkrin ahrk zin leh rok feim vodahmin kotin vulom. It is duty of each man to live with courage and honor lest he fade unremembered into darkness. (Word Wall for Feim, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Means ‘person’ or ‘human’, not gender specific. Refers to an individual person.
entries.etymology: Possibly related to mu ‘we’ or mul ‘strong’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. cruel adv. cruelly v. to make or become cruel
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do Iglif Iiz-Sos wo grind ok oblaan ni ko morokei vukein nuz ahst munax haalvut do liiv krasaar. Here lies the body of Iglif Ice-Blood, who met his end not in glorious combat, but at the cruel touch of the withering sickness. (World Wall for Iiz, Ice Form) Het nok bein nahgahdinok Azaran faal munax wo unt wah gron krilot dilon do Sovngarde wah lein do jul ahrk funt. Here lies the foul necromancer Azaran the Cruel, who tried to Bind the valiant dead of Sovngarde to the world of man, and failed. (Word Wall for Gron, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Cruel in nature or disposition; unfair, unjust.
entries.etymology: From nax ‘cruelty’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. men, plural of mun
entries.usage: Dovahkiin kos fin saviik do muz! Dragonborn, be the savior of men! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Nivahriin muz fent siiv nid aaz het. Cowardly men shall find no mercy here. (Morokei, 00080103) Het dir bruniik Rek-Grohiik Ulfeidr kriid muz ahrk sunvaar bruniik kinbok sahqon tah. Here died the savage she-wolf Ulfeidr, slayer of men and beasts, and savage leader of the Crimson Pack. (Word Wall for Tah, Animal Allegiance)
entries.connotations: Not gender specific, means ‘humans’ rather than ‘male persons’.
entries.etymology: Irregular plural of mun ‘man’.
entries.notes: Only known irregular plural noun in the language. Not to be confused with jul ‘mankind / the races of man’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to eat n. eating, consumption
entries.usage: Vegunthar wahlaan qethsegol bormahii vahrukt, Hungunthar Tiid-Naak, kriaan se junnesejer, kroniid se Dunkreath. Vegunthar built (this) stone (in) his father’s memory, Hungunthar Time-Eater, slayer of the Kings of the East, conqueror of Dunkreath. (Word Wall for Tiid, Slow Time)
entries.notes: Irregular past participle naako. Featured in the dragon name Vuljotnaak ‘dark maw eat’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. eaten adv. in an eaten manner, having been eaten
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv ahzid Viik do Briinahmaar do Sot Peyt, naako wah fin laat naal ufiik do Korvag Kol. This stone commemorates the bitter Defeat of the Sisterhood of the White Rose, eaten to the last by the Trolls of Korvag Crag. (Word Wall for Viik, Disarm)
entries.etymology: Irregular past participle of naak ‘to eat’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: prep. by, according to; with; through the authority or action of
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, Dovahkiin, naal ok zin los vahriin, wah dein vokul mahfaeraak ahst vaal! Dragonborn, Dragonborn, by his honor is sworn, To keep evil forever at bay! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Naal Thu'umu, mu ofan nii nu, Dovahkiin, naal suleyk do Kaan, naal suleyk do Shor, ahrk naal suleyk do Atmorasewuth. By our Voice we give it now (to you), Dragonborn, by (the) power of Kyne, by the power of Shor, and by the power of Atmora-ofold. (Greybeards, 000C43A7) Het mah tahrodiis tafiir Skorji Lun-Sinak, wen klov govey naal rinik hahkun rok togaat wah gahrot. Here fell the treacherous thief Skorji LeechFingers, whose head was removed by the very axe he was attempting to steal. (Word Wall for Lun, Marked for Death) Zu'u uth nall [sic] thurri [sic] dein daar miiraak. I (was) ordered by my lord to keep/guard this portal. (Nahkriin, 000E16FA)
entries.notes: Not used to mean ‘at’ or ‘near’.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. any, anyone adj. any
entries.usage: Wulfik wahlaan qethsegol judii vahrukt, Hrefna Ruvaak-Om, wen miin Diin sos do naan jul. Wulfik raised this stone in memory of his queen, Hrefna Raven-Hair, whose eyes could Freeze the blood of any man. (Word Wall for Diin, Frost Breath) Zu'u Alduin, zok sahrot do naan ko Lein. I (am still) Alduin, most mighty of any in Mundus (the world). (Alduin, 000ED362)
entries.connotations: Typically in reference to a person, not inanimate things.
entries.notes: Used as both a pronoun ‘any/anyone’, and an adjective as in ‘any thing’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. summit, peak
entries.usage: May only occur as the root of lumnaar ‘valley’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. fury
entries.usage: Wuld nah kest! Whirlwind fury tempest! (Whirlwind Sprint Shout) Oblivion loost nid Nah med spaan vahdin beyn. Oblivion hath no Fury like a shield maiden scorned. (Word Wall for Nah, Whirlwind Sprint) Faaz! Nah! “Pain, fury!” = “damn you!” (Alduin, 000D2D72)
entries.connotations: Word of Power that embodies the sudden release of strength, speed, or power. Used as a curse to express anger. Nahgahdinok N4G4DI NOK

entries.expanded_definition: n. necromancer
entries.usage: Het nok bein nahgahdinok Azaran faal Munax, wo unt wah Gron krilot dilon do Sovngarde wah lein do jul, ahrk funt. Here lies the foul necromancer Azaran the Cruel, who tried to Bind the valiant dead of Sovngarde to the world of man, and failed. (Word Wall for Gron, Become Ethereal)
entries.etymology: From dinok, ‘death’, possibly a compound with nah ‘fury’ and/or portmanteau with gahvon ‘to yield’ meaning ‘fury yields death’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to feed; to be fed by n. feeding
entries.usage: Bahloki nahkip sillesejoor. My hunger has been fed by mortal souls. (Alduin, 000CDDF1) Zu'u lost kriaan hi ont, nu hin sille fen nahkip suleyki. I've killed you once, now your souls will feed my power. (Alduin, 000ED365) There are many hungers it is better to deny than to feed. Dreh ni nahkip. Dreh ni nahkip = “do not feed” (Paarthurnax, 0003F9E2, 0003F9E2)
entries.connotations: Can refer to the feeding of any power or force, esp. from the devouring of souls.
entries.etymology: Possibly a compound of naak ‘to eat’ and kip ‘food’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to kill in revenge; to exact vengeance n. revenge, vengeance
entries.usage: Ahrk ond drey sahrot Heimverlund meyz, nol hevno Brom, med Strun do uznahgaar nahkriin nol Sovngarde nimaar. And lo did the mighty Heimverlund come, from the brutal North, like a Storm of unbridled vengeance from Sovngarde itself. (Word Wall for Strun, Storm Call)
entries.etymology: Compound of nah ‘fury’ and kriin ‘to slay’, ‘to slay in fury’.
entries.notes: Namesake of one of the dragon priest masks.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. living, alive adv. in a living manner v. to liven, enliven, make or become living
entries.usage: Nahl...Daal...Vus! Living return Nirn! (Tsun, 000EC399, 000EC397)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, appears only in the Shout used by Tsun to return a person from Sovngarde to Nirn. Generally not used in regular speech. See instead nahlaas ‘alive’.
entries.etymology: From nahlaas ‘alive’, and laas ‘life’, likely truncated from nahlaas to form a Word of Power.
entries.notes: Homophone of naal ‘by’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. alive adv. while alive v. to liven, enliven, make or become alive
entries.usage: Pogaan nahlaas, vokrii wah jun. Many alive, restored to (the) light. (Paarthurnax, 000D2CF5) Sigruuf wahlaan qethsegol briinahii vahrukt, Lanal, wen brit luft los ol kinzon ahrk sot ol Nus, dwiirok nol nahlaas ozinvey. Sigruuf raised this stone for his sister, Lanal, whose beautiful face was as sharp and white as a Statue, carved from living ivory. (Word Wall for Nus, Ice Form) Qethsegol vahrukiv kiir jun Jafnhar, wo los ag nahlaas naal Yol do lot dovah Lodunost. This stone commemorates the child king Jafnhar, who was burned alive by the Fire of the great dragon Lodunost. (Word Wall for Yol, Fire Breath)
entries.connotations: Can describe a living person, or something metaphorically said to be living or alive.
entries.etymology: From laas ‘life’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. silent adv. silently n. silence v. to silence
entries.usage: Nuz aan sul, fent alok, fod fin vul dovah nok, fen kos nahlot mahfaeraak ahrk ruz! But a day, shall arise, when the dark dragon's lies, will be silenced forever and then! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Thu'umii los nahlot. His Voice is silenced. (Dragon, 0009E072)
entries.connotations: In reference to the Voice, refers to death or the removal of former power.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: prep. on, upon; at, down upon
entries.usage: Ahrk fin zul, rok drey kod, nau tol morokei frod, rul lot Taazokaan motaad voth kein! And the Voice, he did wield, on that glorious field, when great Tamriel shuddered with war! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) The freedom of the sky beckons! Yet I stay here, nau gol, as promised. Nau gol = “on earth” = “grounded” (Odahviing, 0004DE42) Kendov krif ok kosiil Vokul, nuz jun Gaar niin nau ok hokoron. The warrior fights his inner evils, but the king unleashes them on his enemies. (Word Wall for Gaar, Cyclone)
entries.notes: Means ‘on top of’ or ‘down upon’. Does not mean ‘active’ as in ‘to turn on’. Not used in reference to time as in ‘on time’ or ‘on this day’. Not used to indicate condition, as in ‘on cue’ or ‘on demand’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. cruelty
entries.usage: Occurs only in the dragon name Paarthurnax ‘ambition overlord cruelty’ and as the root of munax ‘cruel’.
entries.connotations: Given relations to munax, is closer in meaning to ‘injustice’ than ‘atrocity’, the cruelties of unfair circumstances or something that is unyielding and beyond control.

entries.expanded_definition: adv. never
entries.usage: Occurs only in the dragon name Durnehviir ‘curse never dying’.
entries.etymology: Negative related to ni ‘not’ and nid ‘no’.

entries.expanded_definition: conj. both; alike, equally
entries.usage: Wo lost fron wah ney dov, ahrk fin reyliik do jul, voth aan suleyk wah ronit faal krein! Who was kin to both wyrm, and the races of man, with a power to rival the sun! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Nonvul Bron, mahfaeraak dahmaan sahrot Vahlok wen lot ahkrin shaan ney muz ahrk dovah. Noble Nord, forever remember the mighty Guardian whose great courage inspired both men and dragons. (Word Wall for Shaan, Battle Fury)
entries.notes: Not used as an adjective meaning ‘two’ as in ‘both kings’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: adv. not, no (indicates negative)
entries.usage: Ni faas, Dovahkiin! (I do) not fear (you), Dragonborn! (Odahviing, 000D2DBB) And he is no fool. Ni mey, rinik gut nol. Ni mey = “no fool”, Rinik gut nol = “very far from” (Paarthurnax, 000556DB) Ni liivrah hin moro. Do not diminish [wither] your glory. (Paarthurnax, 0004591A) Het nok kopraan do Iglif Iiz-Sos, wo grind ok oblaan ni ko morokei vukein, nuz ahst munax haalvut do liiv krasaar. Here lies the body of Iglif Ice-Blood, who met his end not in glorious combat, but at the cruel touch of the withering sickness. (Word Wall for Iiz, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: Broadly used to indicate a negative of any kind. Should be used instead of nid ‘no’ to indicate a negative in phrases such as zu’u ni mey ‘I am no fool’ unless for emphasis.
entries.notes: Homophone with pronoun nii ‘it’.

entries.expanded_definition: adv. no adj. no, none n. nothing pron. none
entries.usage: Ful, losei Dovahkiin? Zu'u koraav nid nol dov do hi. So, you're the Dragonborn? I see nothing of the dragon about you. (Alduin, 000C8EA0) Lingrah krosis saraan Strundu'ul, voth nid balaan klov praan nau. Long sorrowfully (has) waited the Stormcrown, with no worthy head to rest on. (Greybeards, 000C43AB) Oblivion loost nid Nah med spaan vahdin beyn. Oblivion hath no Fury like a shield maiden scorned. (Word Wall for Nah, Whirlwind Sprint)
entries.connotations: Interchangeable with ni ‘not’ in some cases, such as zu’u nid mey ‘I am no fool’. Ni is more common but nid may be used as a matter of emphasis or formality.
entries.etymology: From ni ‘not’.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. it; an inanimate object; a concept or abstract idea
entries.usage: Naal Thu'umu, mu ofan nii nu, Dovahkiin, naal suleyk do Kaan, naal suleyk do Shor, ahrk naal suleyk do Atmorasewuth. By our Voice we give it now (to you), Dragonborn, by (the) power of Kyne, by the power of Shor, and by the power of Atmora-ofold. (Greybeards, 000C43A6) Ful nii los. Ful nii los. = “so it is” = “so be it” (Paarthurnax, 0009C20C) Nii los heyv do enook mun wah lahney voth ahkrin ahrk zin, leh rok Feim vodahmin kotin vulom. It is the duty of each man to live with courage and honor, lest he Fade unremembered into darkness. (Word Wall for Feim, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Third person singular neuter. May refer to inanimate objects (a crown), or abstractions as the subject of ‘to be’ as in ‘it is an honor’ or ‘it is cold here’.
entries.notes: Homophone with ni ‘not’. May lengthen pronunciation or stress to avoid confusion.

entries.expanded_definition: adv. no; see nid
entries.usage: Niid koraav zeim dinoksetiid. (There is) no seeing through (the) end of time. (Paarthurnax, 0009C20D)
entries.notes: Likely a misspelling of nid ‘no’.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. them
entries.usage: Kendov krif ok kosil Vokul, nuz jun Gaar niin nau ok hokoron. The warrior fights his inner evils, but the king unleashes them on his enemies. (Word Wall for Gaar, Cyclone)
entries.connotations: Third person plural accusative.
entries.notes: Homophone with nin ‘to sting’. Only known pronoun with an explicit accusative form.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. cowardly adv. cowardly, like a coward n. coward v. to cower, lose courage, become cowardly; to dishearten, dismay, make cowardly
entries.usage: Faal Kel...?! Nikriinne… Elder Scroll...? Cowards... (Alduin, 000CD9DE)
entries.connotations: Connotes a loss of courage, unwillingness to face a fear, danger, or challenge.
entries.etymology: Likely a compound of ni ‘not’ and krin ‘courageous’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. void, empty adv. emptily, in a void manner n. void, emptiness v. to empty, make void
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.
entries.etymology: From ni ‘not’ and nid ‘nothing’.
entries.notes: Unknown whether a general word or a proper noun referring to the space beyond the Aurbis.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. itself
entries.usage: Ahrk ond drey sahrot Heimverlund meyz, nol hevno Brom, med Strun do uznahgaar nahkriin nol Sovngarde nimaar. And lo did the mighty Heimverlund come, from the brutal North, like a Storm of unbridled vengeance from Sovngarde itself. (Word Wall for Strun, Storm Call)
entries.connotations: Third person singular neuter reflexive. Used for emphasis (e.g. ‘the Empire itself’).
entries.etymology: From nii ‘it’ with the reflexive suffix -maar.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to sting, strike; to pierce n. sting, strike; piercing
entries.usage: Come, Dovahkiin. Nin Yol. Strike me with the fire of your Thu'um. (Paarthurnax, 000559DC) Thoringar wahlaan qethsegol monii vahrukt, Noomi, wen dez los wah Aus nin do pogaan Ogiim ronaaz. Thoringar raised this stone for his daughter’s memory, Noomi, whose fate it was to Suffer the sting of many Orc arrows. (Word Wall for Aus, Marked for Death)
entries.connotations: Connotes a painful or piercing strike, as from an arrow, or the burning of flames.
entries.etymology: Possibly from nos ‘to strike’.
entries.notes: Homophone with the pronoun niin ‘them’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to hunt n. hunt
entries.usage: Het mah faasnu ronaan Undveld, aar, kriid grohiik, ahrk drog do Lot Nir. Here fell the fearless archer Undveld, servant, slayer of wolves, and lord of the Great Hunt. (Word Wall for Nir, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, encompasses the bond between hunter and prey, and a hunter’s skill and sight.
entries.etymology: May share root with nos ‘to strike’ and nin ‘to sting’.
entries.notes: Featured in the dragon name Sahloknir ‘phantom sky hunt’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. cannot, can’t
entries.usage: Zu'u unslaad! Zu'u nis oblaan! I am eternal! I cannot end! (be ended/be killed) (Alduin, 000ED359) Het nok brit kaaz Anurassa, wen faad nis kos evenaar orin naal Krah dinok. Here lies the beautiful cat Anurassa, whose warmth cannot be extinguished even by the Cold of death. (Word Wall for Krah, Frost Breath)
entries.etymology: From ni ‘not’, possibly a contraction of ni and an unattested word his ‘can’ analogous to losei (los hi).

entries.expanded_definition: adj. cowardly; disloyal; having abandoned an oath adv. cowardly, like a coward n. cowardice; disloyalty v. to become cowardly; to abandon an oath
entries.usage: Ruth wah nivahriin joor! Rage/curses to (you) cowardly mortal! (Alduin, 000C64F1) Draal ni fah Drem, fah grik los hind do sahlo ahrk nivahriin. Pray not for Peace, for such is the wish of the weak and cowardly. (Word Wall for Drem, Kyne’s Peace) is comparable to nikriin ‘cowardly’, but etymology suggests the abandonment of loyalty. May have originally meant this but grew to encompass a broader meaning.
entries.etymology: Likely a compound of ni ‘not’ and vahriin ‘sworn’.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: v. to lie (buried), rest (as in death); to lay or be laid to rest; to lie, tell a falsehood n. rest; lie
entries.usage: Nuz aan sul, fent alok, fod fin vul dovah nok, fen kos nahlot mahfaeraak ahrk ruz! But a day, shall arise, when the dark dragon's lies, will be silenced forever and then! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Het nok Yngnavar Gaaf-Kodaav, wo drey Yah moro nau Frod do Krosis, nuz sinon siiv dinok ahrk dukaan. Here lies Yngnavar Ghost-Bear, who did Seek glory on the Battlefield of Sorrows, but instead found death and dishonor. (Word Wall for Yah, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: Specifically refers to death, the final resting place of a body or thing, usually buried.
entries.notes: Used in the Song of the Dragonborn to mean ‘lie’ as in ‘deceive’, but used extensively in Word Walls as ‘to lie buried’. Should only be used pertaining to death, and lo ‘to deceive’ should be used instead pertaining to deception.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: prep. from, indicating difference or separation; indicating source or origin
entries.usage: Paaz Keizaal fen kos stin nol bein Alduin jot! Fair Skyrim will be free from foul Alduin's maw! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Ni mey, rinik gut nol. No fool, very far from. (Paarthurnax, 000556DB) Het nok kopraan do sonaan Romerius, wo unt Ru nol osos gogil, nuz motmah. Here lies the body of the bard Romerius, who tried to Run from some goblins, but slipped. (Word Wall for Ru, Dismay) Sigruuf wahlaan qethsegol briinahii vahrukt, Lanal, wen brit luft los ol kinzon ahrk sot ol Nus, dwiirok nol nahlaas ozinvey. Sigruuf raised this stone for his sister, Lanal, whose beautiful face was as sharp and white as a Statue, carved from living ivory. (Word Wall for Nus, Ice Form) Ahrk ond drey sahrot Heimverlund meyz, nol hevno Brom, med Strun do uznahgaar nahkriin nol Sovngarde nimaar. And lo did the mighty Heimverlund come, from the brutal North, like a Storm of unbridled vengeance from Sovngarde itself. (Word Wall for Strun, Storm Call)
entries.notes: Do ‘of’ and se ‘of’ are more commonly used to indicate origin than nol.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. noble, honorable adv. nobly, honorably n. nobleness, nobility v. to distinguish, ennoble, dignify, make or become noble
entries.usage: Nonvul Bron, mahfaeraak dahmaan sahrot Vahlok wen lot ahkrin shaan ney muz ahrk dovah. Noble Nord, forever remember the mighty Guardian whose great courage inspired both men and dragons. (Word Wall for Shaan, Battle Fury) Qethsegol vahrukiv vur do Faal Vahlok, nonvul aar se dovah wen dez lost wah qahnaar tahrodiis Miraak. This stone commemorates the valor of the Guardian, noble servant of dragons whose fate it was to vanquish the treacherous Miraak. (Word Wall for Vur, Valor)
entries.connotations: Means ‘honorable’ and ‘worthy’ rather than ‘highborn’, not pertaining to royalty or royal families.
entries.etymology: Possibly an antonym of vul ‘dark’.

entries.official_definition: Fierce (“Fiercest” in the Song of the Dragonborn)
remarks_in_definition: “Fiercest” in the Song of the Dragonborn
entries.expanded_definition: adj. fierce adv. fiercely n. fierceness, ferocity v. to make or become fierce
entries.usage: Ahrk fin norok paal graan fod nust hon zindro zaan! And the fiercest foes rout when they hear triumph's shout! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: Fierce or unyielding in battle, fighting to the last; does not connotate viciousness or wildness, as in a fierce animal. See instead fel ‘feral’ or bruniik ‘savage’.
entries.notes: The superlative meaning in the Song of the Dragonborn is implied and should be considered inherent to norok.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to strike, attack n. strike, attack
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Hrodmir fin Krent, wo sov pah ok eruvos ahrk faraan wah Nos tum krivaan do ok zeymah. This stone commemorates Hrodmir the Broken, who spent all his years and fortune to Strike down the killer of his brother. (Word Wall for Nos, Cyclone)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, to strike with a weapon, Voice, or withheld power. Not used to mean ‘inflict’ as in ‘to strike fear’.

entries.expanded_definition: adv. now; currently, presently; yet, still
entries.usage: Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, Ahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Hin aar, orin nu. Your servant/slave, even now. (Odahviing, 0004DE35) Het mah sahrot konahrik Aaban, kiin se Klo se Alikr, praan nu denek Keizaal. Here fell the mighty warlord Aaban, born of the Sand of the Alik’r, at rest now in the soil of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Klo, Slow Time)
entries.notes: Not to be confused with the suffix -nu seen in the words hahnu ‘dream’ and faasnu ‘fearless’.

entries.expanded_definition: conj. only; except, but
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Bhor fin Golah, wo praal het mulhaan ol Gol saraan onikiv, nunon wah meyz wuth sinon do onik. This stone commemorates Bhor the Stubborn, who sat here still as Earth awaiting enlightenment, only to become old instead of wise. (Word Wall for Gol, Bend Will)
entries.etymology: May relate to sinon ‘instead’, indicating the contrary, root nuz ‘but’.
entries.notes: Conjunction only, used to indicate the contrary, not used as in ‘only a dragon can fly’ or ‘an only child’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. statue
entries.usage: Iiz slen nus! Ice flesh statue! (Ice Form Shout) Sigruuf wahlaan qethsegol briinahii vahrukt, Lanal, wen brit luft los ol kinzon ahrk sot ol Nus, dwiirok nol nahlaas ozinvey. Sigruuf raised this stone for his sister, Lanal, whose beautiful face was as sharp and white as a Statue, carved from living ivory. (Word Wall for Nus, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, permanent and unchanging, facilitates and the transition between flesh and ice.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. they; those
entries.usage: Ahrk fin norok paal graan fod nust hon zindro zaan! And the fiercest foes rout when they hear triumph's shout! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Nust wo ni qiilaan fen kos duaan. Those who (do) not bow will be devoured. (Alduin, 000ED363)
entries.connotations: Third person plural nominative.
entries.notes: Pronoun only. Not to be confused with the adjective daar ‘this/these/those’.

entries.expanded_definition: conj. but, on the contrary
entries.usage: Nuz aan sul, fent alok, fod fin vul dovah nok, fen kos nahlot mahfaeraak ahrk ruz! But a day, shall arise, when the dark dragon's lies, will be silenced forever and then! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Viik nuz ni kron. Defeat but not victory. (Paarthurnax, 0003FA46) Het nok Yngnavar Gaaf-Kodaav, wo drey Yah moro nau Frod do Krosis, nuz sinon siiv dinok ahrk dukaan. Here lies Yngnavar Ghost-Bear, who did Seek glory on the Battlefield of Sorrows, but instead found death and dishonor. (Word Wall for Yah, Aura Whisper)
entries.notes: Used as a conjunction only to indicate the contrary; not used as in ‘there is but one king’ or ‘no one knew but me’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: v. to end; to die, be killed n. end; death
entries.usage: Zu'u unslaad! Zu'u nis oblaan! I am eternal! I cannot end! (be ended/be killed) (Alduin, 000ED359) Het nok kopraan do Iglif Iiz-Sos, wo grind ok oblaan ni ko morokei vukein, nuz ahst munax haalvut do liiv krasaar. Here lies the body of Iglif Ice-Blood, who met his end not in glorious combat, but at the cruel touch of the withering sickness. (Word Wall for Iiz, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: Typically refers to death (of a person, period of time, rule, etc.).
entries.etymology: Typically refers to death (of a person, period of time, rule, etc.).

entries.expanded_definition: n. Oblivion
entries.usage: Oblivion loost nid Nah med spaan vahdin beyn. Oblivion hath no Fury like a shield maiden scorned. (Word Wall for Nah, Whirlwind Sprint)
entries.etymology: Origin of the Tamrielic name ‘Oblivion’ is unknown. Appearance as a loanword in the Word Walls indicates it was contemporary with the ancient Nords.

entries.expanded_definition: n. snow
entries.usage: Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, ahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, relates to both the sky and the land of Skyrim.
entries.notes: Featured prominently in the dragon name Odahviing ‘snow hunter wing’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. snowy adv. snowily n. snowiness v. to make or become snowy
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv key Sarvirra, zok krin Raan alun wah fonaar odus frod, ahrk ofan ok sil fah ok drog. This stone commemorates the horse Sarvirra, the most courageous Animal ever to charge the snowy battlefields, and give his soul for his lord. (Word Wall for Raan, Animal Allegiance)
entries.etymology: From od ‘snow’ with the suffix -us.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to receive, earn, acquire n. reception, acquisition, the act of earning
entries.usage: Het mah Arnvid faal Staadnau, wen Haas denos mindin Kein do Galik, kolos rok ofaal dilos ahraan. Here fell Arnvid the Unbound, whose Health declined after the War of Pines, in which he received a deadly wound. (Word Wall for Haas, Drain Vitality)
entries.etymology: Related to ofan ‘to give’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to give n. giving; gift
entries.usage: Zu'u lost ofan hin laan. I have given your want/request. (Odahviing, 00048F05) Naal Thu'umu, mu ofan nii nu, Dovahkiin, naal suleyk do Kaan, naal suleyk do Shor, ahrk naal suleyk do Atmorasewuth. By our Voice we give it now (to you), Dragonborn, by (the) power of Kyne, by the power of Shor, and by the power of Atmora-ofold. (Greybeards, 000C43A7) Qethsegol vahrukiv key Sarvirra, zok krin Raan alun wah fonaar odus frod, ahrk ofan ok sil fah ok drog. This stone commemorates the horse Sarvirra, the most courageous Animal ever to charge the snowy battlefields, and give his soul for his lord. (Word Wall for Raan, Animal Allegiance)
entries.etymology: Related to ofaal ‘to receive’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. orc, orsimer adj. orcish
entries.usage: Thoringar wahlaan qethsegol monii vahrukt, Noomi, wen dez los wah Aus nin do pogaan Ogiim ronaaz. Thoringar raised this stone for his daughter’s memory, Noomi, whose fate it was to Suffer the sting of many Orc arrows. (Word Wallf for Aus, Marked for Death)
entries.etymology: May relate to gogil ‘goblin’.
entries.notes: Occurs as an adjective meaning ‘orcish’.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. his
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, Dovahkiin, naal ok zin los vahriin, wah dein vokul mahfaeraak ahst vaal! Dragonborn, Dragonborn, by his honor is sworn, To keep evil forever at bay! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Dovahkiin los ok dovahkriid. The Dragonborn is his dragonslayer - The Dragonborn slew him. (Dragon, 0009E058) Qethsegol vahrukiv key Sarvirra, zok krin Raan alun wah fonaar odus frod, ahrk ofan ok sil fah ok drog. This stone commemorates the horse Sarvirra, the most courageous Animal ever to charge the snowy battlefields, and give his soul for his lord. (Word Wall for Raan, Animal Allegiance)
entries.etymology: From rok ‘he’.
entries.notes: The possessive suffix -ii can be used instead of ok to indicate third person possession.

entries.expanded_definition: n. sea, ocean
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv kril Thjodrek, wo dir zohungaar ko Grah do Vith Okaaz. This stone commemorates the brave Thjodrek, who died heroically in the Battle of the Serpent Sea. (Word Wall for Grah, Elemental Fury) Bekkhild wahlaan qethsegol ahmulii vahrukt, Eyolf, wen veysun los sizaan ko vul Kest ko Okaaz do Luv. Bekkhild raised this stone for her husband, Eyolf, whose ship was lost in a dark Tempest in the Sea of Tears. (Word Wall for Kest, Whirlwind Sprint)

entries.expanded_definition: adv. as, similarly, equally conj. in the degree or manner of; while, when
entries.usage: Sahrot Thu'um, med aan tuz, vey zeim hokoron pah, ol fin Dovahkiin komeyt ok rein! Mighty Thu'um, like a blade, cut through enemies all, as the Dragonborn issued his roar! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Pruzah ol aar. Good as (a) slave. (Alduin, 000EDF49) Qethsegol vahrukiv Bhor fin Golah, wo praal het mulhaan ol Gol saraan onikiv, nunon wah meyz wuth sinon do onik. This stone commemorates Bhor the Stubborn, who sat here still as Earth awaiting enlightenment, only to become old instead of wise. (Word Wall for Gol, Dragon Aspect) Het nok Fjolmod Bein-Su, wo pook ol pogaas nau gol ol ok kopraan dreh nu ko golt. Here lies Fjolmod Foul-Air, who stank as much on earth as his body does now in the ground. (Word Wall for Su, Elemental Fury)
entries.notes: Used to mean ‘while/when’ only in the Song of the Dragonborn. Should only be used to form comparisons.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: n. hair
entries.usage: Wulfik wahlaan qethsegol judii vahrukt, Hrefna Ruvaak-Om, wen miin Diin sos do naan jul. Wulfik raised this stone in memory of his queen, Hrefna Raven-Hair, whose eyes could Freeze the blood of any man. (Word Wall for Diin, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: Used to refer to human hair rather than animal hair or fur.

entries.expanded_definition: interj. lo (look, hearken)
entries.usage: Ahrk ond drey sahrot Heimverlund meyz, nol hevno Brom, med Strun do uznahgaar nahkriin nol Sovngarde nimaar. And lo did the mighty Heimverlund come, from the brutal North, like a Storm of unbridled vengeance from Sovngarde itself. (Word Wall for Strun, Storm Call)
entries.connotations: Rarely used, calls attention to a particular statement or detail.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. wise adv. wisely v. to wisen
entries.usage: They see me as master. Wuth. Onik. Old and wise. (Paarthurnax, 0003F88E) Qethsegol vahrukiv Bhor fin Golah, wo praal het mulhaan ol Gol saraan onikiv, nunon wah meyz wuth sinon do onik. This stone commemorates Bhor the Stubborn, who sat here still as Earth awaiting enlightenment, only to become old instead of wise. (Word Wall for Gol, Bend Will)
entries.connotations: Connotes wisdom gained from experience.

entries.expanded_definition: n. wisdom
entries.usage: I can be trusted. I know this. But they do not. Onikaan ni ov dovah. It is always wise to mistrust a dovah. Onikaan ni ov dovah = “Wisdom is not trusting a dragon” (Paarthurnax, 0003C574) Qethsegol vahrukiv lot Miraak – sonaak do lot onikaan, aar do faal Diiv, ahrk hokoron do jul. This stone commemorates the great Miraak – priest of great wisdom, servant of the Wyrm, and enemy of man. (Word Wall for Diiv, Dragon Aspect)
entries.connotations: Connotes wisdom gained from experience.
entries.etymology: From onik ‘wise’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to enlighten n. enlightenment
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Bhor fin Golah, wo praal het mulhaan ol Gol saraan onikiv, nunon wah meyz wuth sinon do onik. This stone commemorates Bhor the Stubborn, who sat here still as Earth awaiting enlightenment, only to become old instead of wise. (Word Wall for Gol, Bend Will)
entries.connotations: To gain wisdom, become wise, have an experience that gives wisdom.
entries.etymology: From onik ‘wise’.

entries.expanded_definition: adv. once, formerly, at one time; already
entries.usage: Zeymahi lost ont du'ul Bormahu. My brother was once the crown of our father. (Paarthurnax, 0009C213) Zu'u lost kriaan hi ont, nu hin sille fen nahkip suleyki. I've killed you once, now your souls will feed my power. (Alduin, 000ED365) Het ont kriist Miraak, wo ahtiid ok sahvot ol Qah, spaan naal Deyra fah ok unslaad midun. Here once stood Miraak, who wore his faith as Armor, shielded by the Daedra for his unending loyalty. (Word Wall for Qah, Dragon Aspect)
entries.notes: Likely from English ‘once’. Used to mean ‘in the past’, not ‘one time’ (‘he struck once’) or ‘whenever’ (‘once he strikes, strike back’).

entries.expanded_definition: adv. even, fully, quite (used to emphasize coincidence, occurrence, or unlikeliness)
entries.usage: Orin brit ro. “(A) fully beautiful balance” = dragon phrase for irony. (Odahviing, 0004DE36) Hin aar, orin nu. Your servant/slave, even now. (Odahviing, 0004DE35) Het nok brit kaaz Anurassa, wen faad nis kos evenaar orin naal Krah dinok. Here lies the beautiful cat Anurassa, whose warmth cannot be extinguished even by the Cold of death. (Word Wall for Krah, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: Can indicates unlikeliness. Emphasizes an adjective or agent.
entries.notes: Adverb only. Not used to mean ‘even’ as in ‘equal’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. uncertain or unspecified; an unspecified number of
entries.usage: Nau daar revak golt drey Freda zahrahmiik ek Laas, ful tol ek pogaan kiir filok, ahrk osos sul qahnaar ek hokoron. On this sacred ground did Freda sacrifice her Life, so that her many children might escape, and some day vanquish her enemies. (Word Wall for Laas, Aura Whisper) Het nok kopraan do sonaan Romerius, wo unt Ru nol osos gogil, nuz motmah. Here lies the body of the bard Romerius, who tried to Run from some goblins, but slipped. (Word Wall for Ru, Dismay)
entries.notes: Not technically a pronoun but may be used similarly (osos fen hon ‘some (one) will listen’).

entries.expanded_definition: n. orphan
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to trust, have confidence in, rely on n. trust, confidence, reliance
entries.usage: Kaan drem ov! Kyne peace trust! (Kyne’s Peace Shout) I can be trusted. I know this. But they do not. Onikaan ni ov dovah. It is always wise to mistrust a dovah. Onikaan ni ov dovah = “Wisdom is not trusting a dragon” (Paarthurnax, 0003C574 ) Het mah spaan vahdin Valkrys, wo krif voth ahkrin, nuz los folaas wah Ov mulaag do bodiis tuz. Here fell the shield maiden Valkrys, who fought bravely, but was wrong to Trust the strength of a borrowed blade. (Word Wall for Ov, Kyne’s Peace)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, implies lowering one’s guard or suspicion (around a predator or fellow dragon), inhibiting territorial urges. To believe in or depend on the strength of something (a weapon, force, or power).

entries.expanded_definition: adj. ivory, ivory-like, made of ivory adv. in an ivory-like manner, as if made of ivory n. ivory; the quality of being like ivory v. to make ivory; to become like ivory
entries.usage: Sigruuf wahlaan qethsegol briinahii vahrukt, Lanal, wen brit luft los ol kinzon ahrk sot ol Nus, dwiirok nol nahlaas ozinvey. Sigruuf raised this stone for his sister, Lanal, whose beautiful face was as sharp and white as a Statue, carved from living ivory. (Word Wall for Nus, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: Precious to the ancient Nords, whose main source of ivory would have been mammoths, horkers, and sabre cats. As an adjective, connotes something perfect, valuable, and perhaps deadly given the dangerous means to obtain it.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. shamed, ashamed adv. ashamedly n. shame, ashamedness v. to shame
entries.usage: I do not know how he came to be caught. But the bronjun... the Jarl... was very proud of his pet. Paak! Paak = “shame” - said with deep disgust. (Paarthurnax, 00045D09) Faaz! Paak! Dinok! [Pain! Shame! Death!] (Draugr, 0004C59F)
entries.connotations: Often used as an interjection to indicate despicable or horrid circumstances, or as a taunt, impending shame (in defeat).

entries.expanded_definition: n. foe, enemy, adversary
entries.usage: Ahrk fin norok paal graan fod nust hon zindro zaan, Dovahkiin, fah hin kogaan mu draal! And the fiercest foes rout when they hear triumph's shout, Dragonborn, for your blessing we pray! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: More conversational than hokoron ‘enemy’, which is more common in formal speech or writing.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to ambition, seek after or aspire to, crave, yearn; to pursue n. ambition, desire
entries.usage: Occurs only in the dragon name Paarthurnax ‘ambition cruelty overlord’.
entries.connotations: Close synonym to bahlok ‘hunger’, the drive to achieve or accomplish, typically through strength or power. Not positive or constructive in connotation as the English word ‘aspiration’, connotes acts of dominance.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. fair adv. fairly n. fairness v. to make or become fair
entries.usage: Paaz Keizaal fen kos stin nol bein Alduin jot! Fair Skyrim will be free from foul Alduin's maw! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Paaz. A fair answer. (Paarthurnax, 00055771) Qethsegol vahrukiv paaz kulaas Yrsa, wo ensosin pah do Taazokaan voth ek Dun ahrk brii. This stone commemorates the fair princess Yrsa, who bewitched all of Tamriel with her Grace and beauty. (Word Wall for Dun, Elemental Fury)
entries.connotations: Closer in meaning to ‘great’, ‘beautiful’, or ‘pleasant’ (‘a fair day’), should typically not be used to mean ‘equal’ or ‘just’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. all, the whole of; every adv. all, wholly, entirely, completely pron. all, everyone
entries.usage: Sahrot Thu'um, med aan tuz, vey zeim hokoron pah, ol fin Dovahkiin komeyt ok rein! Mighty Thu'um, like a blade, cut through enemies all, as the Dragonborn issued his roar! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Meyye! Tahrodiis aanne! Him hinde pah liiv! Zu'u hin daan! Fools! Treacherous slaves! Your hopes (are) all withered! I (am) your doom. (Alduin, 000CD9DF) Pah werid morokei Miraak, zok suleykaar do pah Sonaak wen Mul bolaav naal Fahluaan do Jul. All praise the glorious Miraak, most powerful of all priests, whose Strength was granted by the Gardener of Men. (Word Wall for Mul, Dragon Aspect)

entries.expanded_definition: adj. arrogant adv. arrogantly n. arrogance v. to make or become arrogant
entries.usage: Alduin always was pahlok - arrogant in his power. Uznahgar paar. He took domination as his birthright. Uznahgar [paar] = unending ambition. (Paarthurnax, 0004591A) You did what was necessary. Alduin had flown far from the path of right action in his pahlok. (Paarthurnax, 0009C219)
entries.connotations: For dragons, the belief of power or rule that one is not right to, heedless of consequence or greater strength.
entries.etymology: May share root with paar ‘ambition’ or relate to bahlok ‘hunger’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to write n. writing; writ
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.
entries.etymology: Possibly from kel ‘scroll’, though kel is generally attested to refer to an Elder Scroll, which is not ‘written’ by conventional means.
entries.notes: Possibly from English ‘spell’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. rose
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv ahzid Viik do Briinahmaar do Sot Peyt, naako wah fin laat naal ufiik do Korvag Kol. This stone commemorates the bitter Defeat of the Sisterhood of the White Rose, eaten to the last by the Trolls of Korvag Crag. (Word Wall for Viik, Disarm)
entries.notes: The flower, see alok for the verb ‘to rise’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. plain, field
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Kendov se Ved Ronax, Sille nu yoriik pindaar se Sovngarde pah Ul. This stone commemorates the warriors of the Black Regiment, whose souls now march on the plains of Sovngarde for all Eternity. (Word Wall for Ul, Slow Time) Het mah Hrothmar, Bah Grohiik do bruniik pindaar. Aal ok sil rovaan Sovngarde mahfaeraak. Here fell Hrothmar, Wrath Wolf of the savage plains. May his soul wander Sovngarde forever. (Word Wall for Bah, Storm Call)
entries.connotations: Refers to a geographical plain, more general than frod ‘battlefield’ which specifically refers to a field of battle.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to have, possess n. possession
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do Svolo, wo piraak mulaag wah kriin dovah nuz ni gaan wah kriin pogaan. Here lies the body of Svolo, who possessed the strength to slay dragons, but not the stamina to slay many. (Word Wall for Gaan, Drain Vitality)
entries.connotations: To possess a trait, skill, power, or ability. Does not refer to supernatural possession. Unknown if it can refer to the ownership of property.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. many, numerous pron. many (of something)
entries.usage: Pogaan nahlaas, vokrii wah jun [sic]. Many alive, restored to (the) light. (Paarthurnax, 000D2CF5) Het nok kopraan do Svolo, wo piraak mulaag wah kriin dovah nuz ni gaan wah kriin pogaan. Here lies the body of Svolo, who possessed the strength to slay dragons, but not the stamina to slay many. (Word Wall for Gaan, Drain Vitality) Nau daar revak golt drey Freda zahrahmiik ek Laas, ful tol ek pogaan kiir filok, ahrk osos sul qahnaar ek hokoron. On this sacred ground did Freda sacrifice her Life, so that her many children might escape, and some day vanquish her enemies. (Word Wall for Laas, Aura Whisper)
entries.etymology: Related to pogaas ‘much’.
entries.notes: Used with countable nouns (people, animals, things). See pogaas ‘much’ for the equivalent used with uncountable nouns.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. much; great in measure or degree
entries.usage: Het nok Faal Vahlok, wo kron pogaas moro. Fah ok unslaad mid, rok aav dilon voth lot zin. Here lies the Guardian, who won much glory. For his eternal loyalty, he joins the dead with great honor. (Word Wall for Mid, Battle Fury) Het nok Fjolmod Bein-Su, wo pook ol pogaas nau gol ol ok kopraan dreh nu ko golt. Here lies Fjolmod Foul-Air, who stank as much on earth as his body does now in the ground. (Word Wall for Su, Elemental Fury)
entries.etymology: Related to pogaan ‘many’.
entries.notes: Used with uncountable nouns (abstract). See pogaan ‘many’ for the equivalent used with countable nouns. Also used in comparisons, but not ‘so much’ or ‘too much’. Not a noun as in ‘much of the time’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to stink, reek n. stink, stench
entries.usage: Het nok Fjolmod Bein-Su, wo pook ol pogaas nau gol ol ok kopraan dreh nu ko golt. Here lies Fjolmod Foul-Air, who stank as much on earth as his body does now in the ground. (Word Wall for Su, Elemental Fury)
entries.connotations: The stink of decay, rot, and death.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to sit, lie n. seat; sitting
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Bhor fin Golah, wo praal het mulhaan ol Gol saraan onikiv, nunon wah meyz wuth sinon do onik. This stone commemorates Bhor the Stubborn, who sat here still as Earth awaiting enlightenment, only to become old instead of wise. (Word Wall for Gol, Bend Will)
entries.connotations: To sit, or for dragons, to lie down or otherwise rest on the ground or a perch in an upright position. Compare to nok ‘to lie’ and praan ‘to rest’, which both refer to death and burial.
entries.etymology: Related to praan ‘to rest’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to rest (upon); to lie in rest; to lay to rest, bury n. rest; death, the state of death
entries.usage: Lingrah krosis saraan Strundu'ul, voth nid balaan klov praan nau. Long sorrowfully (has) waited the Stormcrown, with no worthy head to rest on. (Greybeards, 000C43AB) Het nok kopraan do Hela, Fahdon wah pah sivaas aar do Kaan. Aal rek siiv unahzaal praan ko Feykro do Hahnu. Here lies the body of Hela, friend to all beasts and servant of Kyne. May she find eternal rest in the Forest of Dreams. (Word Wall for Kaan, Kyne’s Peace) Het mah sahrot konahrik Aaban, kiin se Klo se Alikr, praan nu denek Keizaal. Here fell the mighty warlord Aaban, born of the Sand of the Alik’r, at rest now in the soil of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Klo, Slow Time)
entries.connotations: To rest motionless in or upon something. Commonly used in reference to death along with nok ‘to lie’. See praal ‘to sit’ for a word that does not connotate death.
entries.etymology: Related to praal ‘to sit’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to foretell, prophesy; to predict, warn of n. foretelling, prophecy, premonition; prediction, portent, warning
entries.usage: Ahrk fin Kel lost prodah, do ved viing ko fin krah, tol fod zeymah win kein meyz fundein! And the Scrolls have foretold, of black wings in the cold, that when brothers wage war come unfurled! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Ah. I have expected you. Prodah. (Paarthurnax, 0003FA40)
entries.connotations: To foretell or predict, as due to prophecy, or the culmination of circumstances or consequences.
entries.notes: Likely inspired by words derived from the prefixes pro- and pre- meaning ‘before’, such as ‘prophet’, ‘prophecy’, and ‘premonition’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. best adv. best, in the best way n. the quality of being best; something that is best v. to best, become better than, get the better of; to make or become best
entries.usage: Pruzaan Zun ko Keizaal los hahdrim do dwiin-sil kendov. The best Weapon in Skyrim is the mind of a steel-souled warrior. (Word Wall for Zun, Disarm) Orin pruzaan dwiin aal kreh ahrk kren, nuz Slen do vahzah muz los sindugahvon. Even the best steel may bend and break, but the Flesh of a true man is unyielding. (Word Wall for Slen, Ice Form)
entries.etymology: From pruzah ‘good/well’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. good, well (in state, quality, or condition); fitting adv. good, well; fittingly n. goodness, wellness v. to make or become good or well
entries.usage: Pruzah wundunne wah Wuth Gein. Good travels to the old one. (Odahviing, 0009E069) Krif krin. Pruzah! (You) fight couragously [sic]. Good! (Mirmulnir, 0005637F) You are persistent, Dovahkiin. Pruzah ol aar. A fine slave you would have made. Pruzah ol aar = “good as (a) slave” (Alduin, 000EDF49)
entries.connotations: Means ‘good’ as in ‘well’ (‘a good day’, ‘well fought’), not ‘morally good’. See instead kul.

entries.expanded_definition: n. armor; hide, scales, plating, any outward defense; defense, protection
entries.usage: Mul qah diiv! Strength armor wyrm! (Dragon Aspect Shout) Het ont kriist Miraak, wo ahtiid ok sahvot ol Qah, spaan naal Deyra fah ok unslaad midun. Here once stood Miraak, who wore his faith as Armor, shielded by the Daedra for his unending loyalty. (Word Wall for Qah, Dragon Aspect)
entries.connotations: Given its role in the Dragon Aspect Shout, may better refer to a dragon’s scales or hide; any outward defense or protection.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to vanquish; to eliminate; to deny, resist n. vanquishment; elimination; denial, resistance
entries.usage: Sahrot thur qahnaraan! The mighty overlord is vanquished! (Dragon, 0009E075) There are many hungers it is better to deny than to feed. … Discipline against the lesser aids in qahnaar... denial of the greater. (Paarthurnax, 0003F9E2) Nau daar revak golt drey Freda zahrahmiik ek Laas, ful tol ek pogaan kiir filok, ahrk osos sul qahnaar ek hokoron. On this sacred ground did Freda sacrifice her Life, so that her many children might escape, and some day vanquish her enemies. (Word Wall for Laas, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: Primarily means ‘to defeat in battle’. Can also mean ‘to eliminate or resist’ a thought or desire, as though in a mental struggle.

entries.expanded_definition: n. vanquisher
entries.usage: My claws have rended the flesh of innumerable foes, but I have never once been felled on the field of battle. I therefore honor-name you Qahnaarin, or Vanquisher in your tongue. (Durnehviir, 0201156B)
entries.connotations: Used as a formal title for someone who has defeated a worthy opponent (esp. a dragon) in battle.
entries.etymology: From Qahnaar ‘to vanquish’. -in may be a distinct suffix or the word in ‘master’, forming ‘master of vanquishing.

entries.expanded_definition: n. touch, presence, existence
entries.usage: You have it. The Kel - the Elder Scroll. Tiid kreh... qalos. Time shudders at its touch. (Paarthurnax, 000C64EC)
entries.connotations: Meaning may be closer to ‘presence’ than ‘physical touch’. Paarthurnax’s pause (as though searching for the right word) may also indicate this word’s meaning is more complex, perhaps related to time or the Elder Scrolls in an as of yet unknown way.
entries.etymology: May derive from los, present tense conjugation of kos ‘to be’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. bone
entries.usage: Occurs only in the compound word qethsegol ‘stone’, lit. ‘bone of the earth’.
entries.connotations: Paarthurnax’s dialogue (‘There is no question. You are doom-driven … The very bones of the earth are at your disposal.’, 000C64EC) may indicate that the dragon word for ‘bone’ connotates a root or source of power. Dragon bones persist even after death, connotating something that is permanent or everlasting.
entries.etymology: May relate to qoth ‘tomb’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. stone
entries.usage: Nafni wahlaan qethsegol bormahii vahrukt, Rognvald, wen Zii fen mahfaeraak aak ok brod, ahrk folook ok hokoron. Nafni raised this stone for his father, Rognvald, whose Spirit will forever guide his clan, and haunt his enemies. (Word Wall for Zii, Become Ethereal)
