entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Vulgrum fin Zahkrii ko fin Ven, sovrahzun wen moro lost maltiid, nuz ko vahrukt unslaad. This stone commemorates Vulgrum the Sword in the Wind, the mercenary whose glory was brief, but in memory eternal. (Word Wall for Ven, Cyclone) Qethsegol vahrukiv lot Miraak – sonaak do lot onikaan, aar do faal Diiv, ahrk hokoron do jul. This stone commemorates the great Miraak – priest of great wisdom, servant of the Wyrm, and enemy of man. (Word Wall for Diiv, Dragon Aspect)
entries.connotations: To preserve the memory of, preserve in memory.
entries.etymology: Related to vahrukt ‘memory’. May stem from an unattested word vahruk ‘to remember’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. memory; remembrance
entries.usage: Vahrukt unslaad... perhaps none but me now remember how /Alduin/ was defeated. Vahrukt unslaad = memory unceasing (Paarthurnax, 0003FA48) Qethsegol vahrukiv Vulgrum fin Zahkrii ko fin Ven, sovrahzun wen moro lost maltiid, nuz ko vahrukt unslaad. This stone commemorates Vulgrum the Sword in the Wind, the mercenary whose glory was brief, but in memory eternal. (Word Wall for Ven, Cyclone) Lungerd wahlaan qethsegol ahmulii vahrukt, Thorgrima, deinmaar do sahqon yolos, ahrk drog do Lah. Lungerd raised this stone in memory of her husband, Thorgrima, keeper of the crimson flame, and lord of Magicka. (Word Wall for Lah, Drain Vitality)
entries.connotations: Prominent in Word Wall memorials alongside vahrukiv ‘to commemorate’. Something done ko vahrukt ‘in (someone’s) memory’ is to commemorate someone, ensure their memory lives on. Also refers to overarching, general memory, as in the memory of a people.
entries.etymology: Related to vahrukiv ‘to commemorate’. May stem from an unattested word vahruk ‘to remember’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. true; right adv. truly; rightly v. to make or become true
entries.usage: Yes. Vahzah. You speak true, Dovahkiin. Forgive me. Vahzah = true (Paarthurnax, 0003F88C) Orin pruzaan dwiin aal kreh ahrk kren, nuz Slen do vahzah muz los sindugahvon. Even the best steel may bend and break, but the Flesh of a true man is unyielding. (Word Wall for Slen, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: Factually true, or true in moral character. Strength also determines truth, rightness, the right to be.
entries.etymology: Related to vahzen ‘truth’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. truth, rightness
entries.usage: Many of the dovahhe are now scattered across Keizaal. Without Alduin's lordship, they may yet bow to the vahzen... rightness of my Thu'um. (Paarthurnax, 0009E073)
entries.connotations: A factual or moral truth, something that has been determined to be true as a matter of strength or domination.
entries.etymology: Related to vahzah ‘true’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. black adv. blackly n. black, blackness v. to blacken Ahrk fin Kel lost prodah, do ved viing ko fin krah, tol fod zeymah win kein meyz fundein! And the Scrolls have foretold, of black wings in the cold, that when brothers wage war come unfurled! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Qethsegol vahrukiv Kendov se Ved Ronax, Sille nu yoriik pindaar se Sovngarde pah Ul. This stone commemorates the warriors of the Black Regiment, whose souls now march on the plains of Sovngarde for all Eternity. (Word Wall for Ul, Slow Time)
entries.connotations: May be associated with darkness, but not necessarily death or evil. See synonym ruvaak ‘raven’ for a word more closely associated with death.

entries.expanded_definition: n. wind, current
entries.usage: Ven gaar nos! Wind unleash strike! (Cyclone Shout) Ven Mul Riik! /Wind Strength Gale!/ Alduin shouts his evil mist back across Sovngarde. (Alduin, 0005094B) Qethsegol vahrukiv Vulgrum fin Zahkrii ko fin Ven, sovrahzun wen moro lost maltiid, nuz ko vahrukt unslaad. This stone commemorates Vulgrum the Sword in the Wind, the mercenary whose glory was brief, but in memory eternal. (Word Wall for Ven, Cyclone)
entries.connotations: Word of Power in both the Cyclone Shout and Alduin’s mist Shout, associated with the sky, turbulence; something that controls and directs, but is itself uncontrollable.
entries.notes: The noun ‘wind’, not to be confused for ‘wind’ as in ‘to wind up’ or ‘a winding road’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. the currents of time, the winds of time, fate, destiny You once told me you did not believe in destiny. … Perhaps now you have some insight into the forces that shape the vennesetiid... the currents of Time. (Paarthurnax, 0009C215)
entries.connotations: A formal compound word referring to destiny and its turbulent nature. Characterized by unpredictability and inevitability, something that cannot be fought against. To fight against fate is akin to flying against the wind.
entries.etymology: Se compound of venne ‘winds’ and tiid ‘time’, lit. ‘winds of time’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to cut, as with a blade n. cut; cutting
entries.usage: Sahrot Thu'um, med aan tuz, vey zeim hokoron pah, ol fin Dovahkiin komeyt ok rein! Mighty Thu'um, like a blade, cut through enemies all, as the Dragonborn issued his roar! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Het nok kopraan do Wynjolf ahrk Wuld, wen viintaas tuz vey zeim lahvu do rahgron Ogiim. Here lies the body of Wynjolf the Whirlwind, whose shining blades cut through an army of angry Orcs. (Word Wall for Wuld, Whirlwind Sprint)
entries.connotations: To cut, as with a blade. Vey zeim ‘to cut through’ is used to mean ‘to handily defeat’.
entries.etymology: May share root with vaaz ‘to tear’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. grass
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.

entries.expanded_definition: n. ship, vessel Bekkhild wahlaan qethsegol ahmulii vahrukt, Eyolf, wen veysun los sizaan ko vul Kest ko Okaaz do Luv. Bekkhild raised this stone for her husband, Eyolf, whose ship was lost in a dark Tempest in the Sea of Tears. (Word Wall for Kest, Whirlwind Sprint)
entries.connotations: Any seafaring vessel. The Nords have a long maritime history, and a ship would have been equivalent to a Nord’s own hall and home.
entries.etymology: Possibly related to vey ‘to cut’, describing a ship cutting through water.
entries.notes: Possibly from English ‘vessel’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. poison
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.
entries.connotations: A swallowed poison.
entries.etymology: Possibly from diivon ‘to swallow’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to defeat n. defeat
entries.usage: Zun haal viik! Weapon hand defeat! (Disarm Shout) Kel drey ni viik. The Elder Scroll did not defeat me. (Alduin, 000ED35D) Zok frini grind ko grah drun viiki, Dovahkiin. My most eagerness (to) meet (you) in battle brought my defeat. (Odahviing, 00048F09) Qethsegol vahrukiv ahzid Viik do Briinahmaar do Sot Peyt, naako wah fin laat naal ufiik do Korvag Kol. This stone commemorates the bitter Defeat of the Sisterhood of the White Rose, eaten to the last by the Trolls of Korvag Crag. (Word Wall for Viik, Disarm)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, connotes the total loss of battle. Synonym of kron ‘to conquer’, but negative in connotation towards the object; lack of strength and ability in battle.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to shine n. shine
entries.usage: Occurs only in the dragon name Viinturuth ‘shine hammer rage’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. wing
entries.usage: Od ah viing! Snow hunter wing! (Call Dragon Shout) Ahrk fin Kel lost prodah, do ved viing ko fin krah, tol fod zeymah win kein meyz fundein! And the Scrolls have foretold, of black wings in the cold, that when brothers wage war come unfurled! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, associated with strength, the extent of one’s power.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. shining adv. shiningly n. to make or become shining
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do Wynjolf ahrk Wuld, wen viintaas tuz vey zeim lahvu do rahgron Ogiim. Here lies the body of Wynjolf the Whirlwind, whose shining blades cut through an army of angry Orcs. (Word Wall for Wuld, Whirlwind Sprint)
entries.etymology: From viin ‘to shine’. Suffix -taas may form present participles or otherwise form adjectives from verbs.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. dying, nearing death adv. in a dying manner n. the state of nearing death v. to mortally wound; to make or become dying
entries.usage: Dur neh viir! Curse never dying! (Summon Durnehviir Shout)
entries.etymology: Possibly related to dir ‘to die’.
entries.notes: Not used to mean ‘final’ as in ‘her dying words’ or ‘his dying wish’. Also not used to express want as in ‘we are dying to eat’. Not to be confused as the present participle of dir ‘to die’; should only be used in reference to something that is close to death.

entries.expanded_definition: n. serpent, snake
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv kril Thjodrek, wo dir zohungaar ko Grah do Vith Okaaz. This stone commemorates the brave Thjodrek, who died heroically in the Battle of the Serpent Sea. (Word Wall for Grah, Elemental Fury)
entries.notes: Not a synonym of dovah ‘dragon’ or diiv ‘wyrm’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to undo, reverse n. undoing, reversal
entries.usage: Slen Tiid Vo! [Flesh time undo!] (Alduin, 000B3987)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, used by Alduin to ‘undo time’ and return a dragon’s soul to its flesh.
entries.etymology: The origin of the prefix vo- ‘un-, opposite of’ or derived from it.
entries.notes: Official meaning is unknown. Possibly means ‘to undo’ or ‘to reverse’ given its context in Alduin’s dragon resurrection Shout and its relationship with the prefix vo- ‘un-, opposite of’. Possibly occurs in the dragon name Kahvozein ‘pride undo worship’.

entries.official_definition: Un- (prefix meaning “opposite of”, e.g. unkind, unlikeable, etc.)
remarks_in_definition: prefix meaning “opposite of”, e.g. unkind, unlikeable, etc.
entries.expanded_definition: pref. un-, opposite of
entries.usage: Vobalaan ‘unworthy’; vodahmin ‘unremembe red/forgotten’; vokrii ‘to revive, restore’ (lit. ‘un-kill’); vokul ‘evil’ (lit. ‘ungood’); vokun ‘shadow’ (lit. ‘unlight’); volaan ‘intruder’ (lit. ‘unwant(ed)’); vomir ‘unallied’; vonun ‘unseen’; vonuz ‘invisible’; vosaraan ‘to hasten’ (lit. ‘un-wait’); vothaarn ‘disobedience’
entries.etymology: Related to vo ‘to undo, reverse’.
entries.notes: Appears as von in vonmindoraan ‘incomprehensible idea’. Unknown whether this is intentional or a typo of vomindoraan. Appears to be used in dialogue to form a negative imperative (vosaraan ‘do not wait’, 000C64F6); more likely that vosaraan is a separate vocabulary word meaning ‘to hasten’ (li. ‘un-wait’)

entries.expanded_definition: adj. unworthy adv. unworthily n. unworthiness v. to make or become unworthy
entries.usage: Zu'u ni tahrodiis. It was you that lured me here and took me prisoner... vobalaan grahmindol. I have done nothing to earn your distrust. Zu'u ni tahrodiis = “I (am) not treacherous” vobalaan grahmindol = “unworthy strategem” (Odahviing, 0004DE32)
entries.connotations: Associated with treachery and dishonor, not befitting of something (a battle, event, etc.).
entries.etymology: From balaan ‘worthy’ with the prefix vo ‘un-, opposite of’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. ago, gone, past adv. ago, gone by, in the past n. past; the quality of being past v. to pass, to make or become past
entries.usage: Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, ahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Vodahmin VOD4MIN +--------------------------------------+-------------------------------+

entries.expanded_definition: adj. unremembered, forgotten adv. unremembered, forgotten, having been forgotten n. the quality of being forgotten v. to be forgotten; to make or become forgotten
entries.usage: Nii los heyv do enook mun wah lahney voth ahkrin ahrk zin, leh rok Feim vodahmin kotin vulom. It is the duty of each man to live with courage and honor, lest he Fade unremembered into darkness. (Word Wall for Feim, Become Ethereal)
entries.etymology: From dahmaan ‘to remember’ with the prefix vo- ‘un-, opposite of’.
entries.notes: Not to be confused for ‘to forget’.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: adj. unborn, not yet born or made adv. in an unborn or nonexistent manner n. the quality or state of being unborn, nonexistence v. to unmake, undo; to make or become unborn
entries.usage: Perhaps this world is simply the Egg of the next kalpa? Lein vokiin? Would you stop the next world from being born? Lein vokiin = world unborn (Paarthurnax, 0003FA13)
entries.connotations: More closely associated with creation than destruction, unmaking something for the purpose of making something new.
entries.etymology: Kiin ‘born’ with the prefix vo- ‘un’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to restore, revive, return (to a state or condition) n. restoration, revival, return (to a state or condition)
entries.usage: I have tasted the voices of Alduin's allies on the wind. Pogaan nahlaas, vokrii wah jun [sic]. Pogaan nahlaas, vokrii wah jun [sic] = “many alive, restored to (the) light” (Paarthurnax, 000D2CF5) Alduin, thuri! Boaan tiid vokriiha suleyksejun kruziik? Alduin, my king (overlord)! Has the time arrived (flown) to restore (unkill) your ancient dominion (power-of-king)? (Sahloknir, 00035B4A) Het nok un mahlaan drogge erei suleyk se Alduin vokrii. [Here lie our fallen lords until the power of Alduin (is) restored.] (Dragonstone Inscription)
entries.connotations: To restore, return to power or existence. May also refer to literal resurrection.
entries.etymology: From krii ‘to kill’ with the prefix vo- ‘un-, opposite of’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. evil adv. evilly, in an evil manner n. evilness; evil v. to make or become evil
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, Dovahkiin, naal ok zin los vahriin, wah dein vokul mahfaeraak ahst vaal! Dragonborn, Dragonborn, by his honor is sworn, To keep evil forever at bay! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Kendov krif ok kosil Vokul, nuz jun Gaar niin nau ok hokoron. The warrior fights his inner evils, but the king unleashes them on his enemies. (Word Wall for Gaar, Cyclone)
entries.connotations: Moral evil, more prominently used by Nords than dragons, whose morals are based on strength and truth.
entries.etymology: From kul ‘good’ with the prefix vo- ‘un-, opposite of’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. shadow; darkness
entries.usage: Alduin, feyn do jun, kruziik vokun staadnau, voth aan bahlok wah diivon fin lein! Alduin, Bane of Kings, ancient shadow unbound, with a hunger to swallow the world! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: Associated with darkness and doom, possibly also evil.
entries.etymology: From kun ‘light’ with the prefix vo- ‘un-, opposite of’.
entries.notes: Namesake of one of the eight dragon priest masks.

entries.expanded_definition: n. horror
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list and Prima Games official guide.
entries.connotations: Associated with darkness and doom, possibly also evil.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to intrude n. intrusion; intruder
entries.usage: Tell me. Why do you come here, volaan? Why do you intrude on my meditation? (Paarthurnax, 0003FA14) Dir volaan! /Die, intruder!/ (Draugr, 0004C59D)
entries.connotations: Not necessarily equivalent to ‘trespasser’ where the intrusion is intentional; someone or something in a place that is not wanted, whether knowingly intruding or otherwise.
entries.etymology: From laan ‘want/request’ with the prefix vo ‘un-, opposite of’, someone or something that is not wanted.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Volunruud
entries.usage: Volunruud - Volunruud - A Fortified Wooden Hall near Giants' Gap. Meat and Worked Ivory. (Book, Holdings of Jarl Gjalund)
entries.etymology: Unknown whether dragon or Nordic in origin, but most likely Nordic.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. unknown, unknowable adv. in an unknown or unknowable manner, incomprehensibly n. obscurity; unknown, something that is unknown v. to make or become unknown
entries.usage: Return [The Elder Scroll] here, to the TiidAhraan. Then... Kelle vomindok. Nothing is certain with such things… Kelle vomindok = “The Elder Scrolls are unknown/unknowable” (Paarthurnax, 000BD16A) Vomindok. I do not know. Perhaps in the very doing they erased the knowing of /Dragonrend/ from Time itself. (Paarthurnax, 0003FA42)
entries.etymology: From mindok ‘to know’ with the prefix vo ‘un-, opposite of’.
entries.notes: Can be used as an interjection to mean ‘I don’t know’ or ‘That’s unknown’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. unallied, free of fealty, independent adv. in a manner free of fealty, independently n. independence, the quality of being unallied, free of fealty v. to become unallied, free of fealty, be released from an oath
entries.usage: Mu los vomir. We are unallied/free of fealty. (Dragon, 0009E06E)
entries.etymology: From mir ‘allegiance’ with the prefix vo ‘un-, opposite of’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. incomprehensible adv. incomprehensibly n. incomprehension; the quality of being incomprehensible; an incomprehensible thing or idea v. to make or become incomprehensible
entries.usage: [Dragonrend] was said to force a dragon to experience the concept of Mortality. A truly vonmindoraan... incomprehensible idea to the immortal dov. (Paarthurnax, 0003FA43)
entries.etymology: From mindoraan ‘to understand’ with the prefix vo- ‘un-, opposite of’.
entries.notes: Unknown whether the n is accidental and the intended word is vomindoraan, or if it is intentional for an unknown reason. Vonmindoraan does not appear in any other source besides the dialogue cited above.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. unseen, hidden adv. hiddenly, in an unseen manner n. hiddenness, the quality of being unseen; something that is unseen v. to hide, vanish, disappear, make or become unseen
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv sod do Siglif fin Vonun wo aam lot Keizaal ni ol kendov ko vu nuz ol sah ko suvulaan. This stone commemorates the deeds of Siglif the Unseen, who served great Skyrim not as a warrior in the dawn, but as a phantom in the twilight. (Unused Word Wall for Sah, Phantom Form)
entries.etymology: From an unattested word nun ‘seen’ (possibly ‘to see or spot’) with the prefix vo ‘un-, opposite of’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. invisible adv. invisibly n. invisibility; something that is invisible v. to vanish, disappear, make or become invisible
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.
entries.etymology: Possibly from an unattested word nuz ‘visible’ with the prefix vo- ‘un-, opposite of’. Much more likely a variation of vonun ‘unseen’ made without regard to the prefix vo-.

entries.official_definition: Do not wait / Do not delay
entries.expanded_definition: v. to hasten, make haste, be without delay n. haste, lack of delay
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, vosaraan! Use Dragonrend before Alduin consumes you! Vosaraan = do not wait, vosaraan = do not delay (Paarthurnax, 000C64F0, 000C64F6)
entries.etymology: From saraan ‘to wait, delay’ with the prefix vo- ‘un-, opposite of’.
entries.notes: May be interpreted as a negative imperative of saraan ‘to wait, delay’. Very likely exists as an independent word meaning ‘to hasten’ or ‘to not delay’.

entries.official_definition: With (Song of the Dragonborn - avoid using)
remarks_in_definition: Song of the Dragonborn - avoid using
entries.expanded_definition: prep. with; possessing; using, by (instrumental); from, due to
entries.usage: Wo lost fron wah ney dov, ahrk fin reyliik do jul, voth aan suleyk wah ronit faal krein! Who was kin to both wyrm, and the races of man, with a power to rival the sun! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Lingrah krosis saraan Strundu'ul, voth nid balaan klov praan nau. Long sorrowfully (has) waited the Stormcrown, with no worthy head to rest on. (Greybeards, 000C43AB) Qethsegol vahrukiv paaz kulaas Yrsa, wo ensosin pah do Taazokaan voth ek Dun ahrk brii. This stone commemorates the fair princess Yrsa, who bewitched all of Tamriel with her Grace and beauty. (Word Wall for Dun, Elemental Fury) Ahrk fin zul, rok drey kod, nau tol morokei frod, rul lot Taazokaan motaad voth kein! And the Voice, he did wield, on that glorious field, when great Tamriel shuddered with war! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.notes: Not used to mean ‘together’ as in ‘cheese with mead’ or ‘to travel with a companion’. Also not used to mean ‘supporting’ as in ‘I am with you’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. disobedient adv. disobediently n. disobedience v. to disobey; to make or become disobedient
entries.usage: Sosaal fah hin vothaarn. (You will) bleed for your disobedience. (Alduin, 000E16F9)
entries.connotations: Associated with betrayal and treachery, heresy for not following the rightful power.
entries.etymology: From thaarn ‘obedience’ with the prefix vo ‘un-, opposite of’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. dawn; the end of darkness
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv sod do Siglif fin Vonun wo aam lot Keizaal ni ol kendov ko vu nuz ol sah ko suvulaan. [(This) stone commemorates (the) deeds of Siglif the Unseen, who served great Skyrim not as (a) warrior in dawn, but as (a) phantom in twilight.] (Unused Word Wall for Sah, Phantom Form)
entries.connotations: In close proximity to vul ‘dark’, vulom ‘darkness’, and vulon ‘night’. May be more closely associated with the passing night than the coming day.
entries.notes: Not used as a verb meaning ‘to occur’ as in ‘to dawn on someone’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: v. to combat, face in combat, fight in war n. combat
entries.usage: Het nok kopraan do Iglif Iiz-Sos, wo grind ok oblaan ni ko morokei vukein, nuz ahst munax haalvut do liiv krasaar. Here lies the body of Iglif Ice-Blood, who met his end not in glorious combat, but at the cruel touch of the withering sickness. (Word Wall for Iiz, Ice Form)
entries.connotations: To fight, battle against, esp. single combat.
entries.etymology: From kein ‘war’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. dark adv. darkly v. to darken
entries.usage: Nuz aan sul, fent alok, fod fin vul dovah nok, fen kos nahlot mahfaeraak ahrk ruz! But a day, shall arise, when the dark dragon's lies, will be silenced forever and then! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Bekkhild wahlaan qethsegol ahmulii vahrukt, Eyolf, wen veysun los sizaan ko vul Kest ko Okaaz do Luv. Bekkhild raised this stone for her husband, Eyolf, whose ship was lost in a dark Tempest in the Sea of Tears. (Word Wall for Kest, Whirlwind Sprint) Wo meyz [sic] wah dii vul junaar? [Who comes to my dark kingdom?] (Morokei, 0008010B)
entries.connotations: Without light, associated with doom, loss of hope.
entries.etymology: Possibly shares root with vu ‘dawn’.
entries.notes: Featured in the dragon name Vuljotnaak ‘dark maw eat’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. darkness
entries.usage: Nii los heyv do enook mun wah lahney voth ahkrin ahrk zin, leh rok Feim vodahmin kotin vulom. It is the duty of each man to live with courage and honor, lest he Fade unremembered into darkness. (Word Wall for Feim, Become Ethereal) Het nok Faal Vahlok, deinmaar do Dovahgolz ahrk aan Fus do unslaad rahgol ahrk vulom. Here lies The Guardian, keeper of the Dragonstone and a Force of eternal rage and darkness. (Word Wall for Fus, Unrelenting Force)
entries.connotations: Without light, associated with doom, loss of hope. Also associated with being lost or forgotten.
entries.etymology: From vul ‘dark’ with noun suffix -om.

entries.expanded_definition: n. night
entries.usage: Pah werid sonaan Lunerio, wen yuvon lovaas meyz Fo, het ko vulon. All praise the bard Lunerio, whose golden voice became Frost, here in the night. (Word Wall for Fo, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: Associated with vulom ‘darkness’, the threat of doom, treachery, the unseen.
entries.etymology: From vul ‘dark’. In close proximity to vu ‘dawn’, suvulaan ‘twilight’, and sul ‘day’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. beard
entries.usage: Occurs only in the compound word sadonvum ‘graybeard’.
entries.etymology: May share root with tum ‘down’ and possible unattested word lum in lumnaar ‘valley’ meaning ‘low’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. valor
entries.usage: Mid vur shaan! Loyal valor inspire! (Battle Fury Shout) Qethsegol vahrukiv vur do Faal Vahlok, nonvul aar se dovah wen dez lost wah qahnaar tahrodiis Miraak. This stone commemorates the valor of the Guardian, noble servant of dragons whose fate it was to vanquish the treacherous Miraak. (Word Wall for Vur, Battle Fury)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, bravery in battle, perseverance to fight or accomplish a great deed.

entries.expanded_definition: n. Nirn
entries.usage: Nahl...Daal...Vus! Living return Nirn! (Tsun, 000EC399, 000EC397)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, appears only in the Shout used by Tsun to return a person from Sovngarde to Nirn. Refers specifically to the planetary body.
entries.etymology: Possibly from vu ‘dawn’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: prep. to (indicates infinitive); to (indicates indirect object); to, with (indicates relation); to (expressing condition or state); to, at, towards; versus, against
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, Dovahkiin, naal ok zin los vahriin, wah dein vokul mahfaeraak ahst vaal! Dragonborn, Dragonborn, by his honor is sworn, To keep evil forever at bay! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Huzrah nu, kul do od, wah aan bok lingrah vod, Aahrk fin tey, boziik fun, do fin gein! Hearken now, sons of snow, to an age, long ago, and the tale, boldly told, of the one! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Wo lost fron wah ney dov, ahrk fin reyliik do jul, voth aan suleyk wah ronit faal krein! Who was kin to both wyrm, and the races of man, with a power to rival the sun! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Pogaan nahlaas, vokrii wah jun. Many alive, restored to (the) light. (Paarthurnax, 000D2CF5) Ruth wah nivahriin joor! Rage/curses to (you) cowardly mortal! (Alduin, 000C64F1) Thu'um wah Thu'um! Shout versus Shout! (Odahviing, 000D2DBF)
entries.notes: Used most commonly to indicate infinitive verbs. Often absent from speech and writing. May sometimes be contracted as a. (Rok funta koraav ‘he failed to see’, 0009C218)

entries.expanded_definition: v. to build, raise, create, construct, erect
entries.usage: Occurs as a past participle wahlaan.
entries.connotations: Generally only in reference to structures, such as a stone or hall.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: v. built, created, raised, erected, past part. of wahl
entries.usage: Alduin wahlaan daanii. Alduin created his (own) doom. (Paarthurnax, 0009C216) Dov wahlaan fah rel. Dragons were created for domination. (Paarthurnax, 0003C574) Loknir Mal-Tu wahlaan qethsegol aarii vahrukt, bonaar Vakeeza, wo vaat Mir wah jun do Keizaal, ahrk dir ko sadon gravuun. Loknir Little-Hammer erected this stone in memory of his servant, humble Vakeeza, who swore Allegiance to the kings of Skyrim, and died in the gray autumn. (Word Wall for Mir, Animal Allegiance) Nafni wahlaan qethsegol bormahii vahrukt, Rognvald, wen Zii fen mahfaeraak aak ok brod, ahrk folook ok hokoron. Nafni raised this stone for his father, Rognvald, whose Spirit will forever guide his clan, and haunt his enemies. (Word Wall for Zii, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Common in Word Wall memorials. Generally only in reference to structures, such as a stone or hall.
entries.etymology: From wahl ‘to build, raise’ with the suffix aan.

entries.expanded_definition: n. creation, something that is raised or built
entries.usage: It is an... artifact from outside time. It does not exist, but it has always existed. Rah wahlaan. They are...hmm... fragments of creation. Rah wahlaan = gods (of) creation, or creator gods. (Paarthurnax, 000BBEAA)
entries.connotations: Generally only in reference to structures, such as a stone or hall.
entries.etymology: From wahl ‘to build, raise’.
entries.notes: Identical to the past participle wahlaan.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: pron. whose
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Vulgrum fin Zahkrii ko fin Ven, sovrahzun wen moro lost maltiid, nuz ko vahrukt unslaad. This stone commemorates Vulgrum the Sword in the Wind, the mercenary whose glory was brief, but in memory eternal. (Word Wall for Ven, Cyclone) Pah werid sonaan Lunerio, wen yuvon lovaas meyz Fo, het ko vulon. All praise the bard Lunerio, whose golden voice became Frost, here in the night. (Word Wall for Fo, Frost Breath) Thoringar wahlaan qethsegol monii vahrukt, Noomi, wen dez los wah Aus nin do pogaan Ogiim ronaaz. Thoringar raised this stone for his daughter’s memory, Noomi, whose fate it was to Suffer the sting of many Orc arrows. (Word Wall for Aus, Marked for Death)
entries.etymology: From wo ‘who’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to praise, exalt n. praise, exaltation
entries.usage: Pah werid morokei Miraak, zok suleykaar do pah Sonaak wen Mul bolaav naal Fahluaan do Jul. All praise the glorious Miraak, most powerful of all priests, whose Strength was granted by the Gardener of Men. (Word Wall for Mul, Dragon Aspect) Pah werid sonaan Lunerio, wen yuvon lovaas meyz Fo, het ko vulon. All praise the bard Lunerio, whose golden voice became Frost, here in the night. (Word Wall for Fo, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: Religious praise, or general compliments, regard, or esteem.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to wage, carry out (a war, conflict) n. waging
entries.usage: Ahrk fin Kel lost prodah, do ved viing ko fin krah, tol fod zeymah win kein meyz fundein! And the Scrolls have foretold, of black wings in the cold, that when brothers wage war come unfurled! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.notes: Not to be confused for ‘wage’ as in ‘salary’.

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: pron. who, whom
entries.usage: Wo lost fron wah ney dov, ahrk fin reyliik do jul, voth aan suleyk wah ronit faal krein! Who was kin to both wyrm, and the races of man, with a power to rival the sun! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Nust wo ni qiilaan fen kos duaan. Those who (do) not bow will be devoured. (Alduin, 000ED363) Het nok Yngnavar Gaaf-Kodaav, wo drey Yah moro nau Frod do Krosis, nuz sinon siiv dinok ahrk dukaan. Here lies Yngnavar Ghost-Bear, who did Seek glory on the Battlefield of Sorrows, but instead found death and dishonor. (Word Wall for Yah, Aura Whisper)

entries.expanded_definition: adj. oak, oaken adv. in an oaken manner, as though made of oak n. oak v. to make or become oaken
entries.usage: Lo ni hin kiim, fah rek los wol ko hin spaan, dwiin ko hin zahkrii. [Deceive not your wife, for she is the oak in your shield, and the steel in your sword.] (Unused Word Wall for Lo, Phantom Form)
entries.connotations: Revered as strong, associated with protection.

entries.expanded_definition: n. whirlwind
entries.usage: Wuld nah kest! Whirlwind fury tempest! (Whirlwind Sprint Shout) Master Borri will teach you “Wuld,” which means “Whirlwind.” (Arngeir, 00078B3E) Even we who ride the currents of Time cannot see past Time's end. Wuldsetiid los tahrodiis. Wuldsetiid los tahrodiis = “the whirlwind/vortex of time is treacherous/turbulent” (Paarthurnax, 00055771) Het nok kopraan do Wynjolf ahrk Wuld, wen viintaas tuz vey zeim lahvu do rahgron Ogiim. Here lies the body of Wynjolf the Whirlwind, whose shining blades cut through an army of angry Orcs. (Word Wall for Wuld, Whirlwind Sprint)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, associated with the turbulence, unpredictability, and power of the wind and sky. Wuldsetiid WULDSET 3D

entries.expanded_definition: n. whirlwind of time
entries.usage: Even we who ride the currents of Time cannot see past Time's end. Wuldsetiid los tahrodiis. Wuldsetiid los tahrodiis = “the whirlwind/vortex of time is treacherous/turbulent” (Paarthurnax, 00055771)
entries.connotations: Metaphor that characterizes the currents of time as turbulent and unpredictable.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to travel n. travel
entries.usage: Pruzah wundunne wah Wuth Gein. Good travels to the old one. (Odahviing, 0009E069) Het mah siigonis Neivaan wo wundun Gut nol hofkiin dir voth zin ko ahmik do Zeymahzin. [Here fell (the) lizard Nievaan, who travelled Far from home (to) die with honor in service of (the) Companions.] (Unused Word Wall for Gut, Throw Voice)
entries.notes: Possibly from English ‘wander’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. traveller
entries.usage: Drem Yol Lok. Greetings, wunduniik. I am Paarthurnax. Wunduniik = traveller (Paarthurnax, 0003F88B) You are bold, wunduniik. You dare enter a Dovah's home without permission. (Paarthurnax, 0003F9E7)
entries.etymology: From wundun ‘to travel’ with the noun suffix -iik.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. old; for a long time adv. in an old manner, as though old; yore n. oldness, age; yore v. to age, grow or become old
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Bhor fin Golah, wo praal het mulhaan ol Gol saraan onikiv, nunon wah meyz wuth sinon do onik. This stone commemorates Bhor the Stubborn, who sat here still as Earth awaiting enlightenment, only to become old instead of wise. (Word Wall for Gol, Bend Will) You will see them... wuth fadonne [sic]... my friends - Hakon, Gormlaith, Felldir. Wuth fadonne [sic] = old friends (Paarthurnax, 000BD16A) Naal Thu'umu, mu ofan nii nu, Dovahkiin, naal suleyk do Kaan, naal suleyk do Shor, ahrk naal suleyk do Atmorasewuth. By our Voice we give it now (to you), Dragonborn, by (the) power of Kyne, by the power of Shor, and by the power of Atmora-ofold. (Greybeards, 000C43A7) [The Greybeards] see me as master. Wuth. Onik. Old and wise. (Paarthurnax, 0003F88E) Yah Y4 +--------------------------------------+-------------------------------+

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: v. to seek, pursue n. search, pursuit
entries.usage: Laas yah nir! Life seek hunt! (Aura Whisper Shout) Het nok Yngnavar Gaaf-Kodaav, wo drey Yah moro nau Frod do Krosis, nuz sinon siiv dinok ahrk dukaan. Here lies Yngnavar Ghost-Bear, who did Seek glory on the Battlefield of Sorrows, but instead found death and dishonor. (Word Wall for Yah, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, most closely associated with hunting and pursuit.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

entries.expanded_definition: n. fire
entries.usage: Yol toor shul! Fire inferno sun! (Fire Breath Shout) In your tongue, the Word simply means “Fire.” It is change given form. Power at its most primal. That is the true meaning of “Yol.” Suleyk. Power. You have it, as do all dov. But power is inert without action and choice. Think of this as the fire builds in your su'um, in your breath. Su'um ahrk morah. What will you burn? What will you spare? (Paarthurnax, 000E8275) Qethsegol vahrukiv kiir jun Jafnhar, wo los ag nahlaas naal Yol do lot dovah Lodunost. This stone commemorates the child king Jafnhar, who was burned alive by the Fire of the great dragon Lodunost. (Word Wall for Yol, Fire Breath)
entries.connotations: Word of Power in the Fire Breath Shout. Power at its most primal, change given form. Associated with wrath and destruction.
entries.notes: Not used to mean ‘fire’ as in ‘to fire an arrow’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. flame
entries.usage: Lungerd wahlaan qethsegol ahmulii vahrukt, Thorgrima, deinmaar do sahqon yolos, ahrk drog do Lah. Lungerd raised this stone in memory of her husband, Thorgrima, keeper of the crimson flame, and lord of Magicka. (Word Wall for Lah, Drain Vitality)
entries.connotations: An individual flame, as opposed to a larger fire or inferno.
entries.etymology: From yol ‘fire’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to march n. march
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Kendov se Ved Ronax, Sille nu yoriik pindaar se Sovngarde pah Ul. This stone commemorates the warriors of the Black Regiment, whose souls now march on the plains of Sovngarde for all Eternity. (Word Wall for Ul, Slow Time)
entries.connotations: Associated with military, war, and battle.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. gold, golden; fine, rich adv. goldenly; finely, richly n. gold; fineness, richness v. to make or become golden; to enrich
entries.usage: Pah werid sonaan Lunerio, wen yuvon lovaas meyz Fo, het ko vulon. All praise the bard Lunerio, whose golden voice became Frost, here in the night. (Word Wall for Fo, Frost Breath)
entries.connotations: Though official definition and etymology suggest color, is used in a way that more closely means ‘fine or rich in character’.
entries.etymology: Shares ending with sadon ‘gray’ and sahqon ‘crimson’.
entries.notes: Does not refer to money.

entries.expanded_definition: n. slave
entries.usage: Diil qoth zaam! Undead tomb slave! (Soul Cairn Summon Shout) Zu'u ni zaamiil. You cannot command me forever. Zu'u ni zaamiil. = I am not your slave. (Tamed Dragon, 0202AD11)
entries.connotations: Refers exclusively to an unwilling, permanent slave, contrast with aar ‘servant’ which refers to someone who may serve because of an oath or duty.
entries.etymology: From aam ‘to serve’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. slavery, enslavement, the state or condition of being a slave
entries.usage: Nahkriin fah zaamhus! Vengeance for my slavery! (Sahrotaar, 0202BC53)
entries.connotations: Refers to the enslavement of an individual person, not the institution of slavery.
entries.etymology: From zaam with the noun suffix -hus.

entries.official_definition: Shout (noun) (meaning yell, not use of Voice power)
remarks_in_definition: meaning yell, not use of Voice power
entries.expanded_definition: v. to shout, yell, cry n. shout, yell, cry
entries.usage: Ahrk fin norok paal graan fod nust hon zindro zaan! And the fiercest foes rout when they hear triumph's shout! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: Does not refer to the Thu’um; a shout, yell, or cry, esp. a battle cry. Zah Z4 +--------------------------------------+-------------------------------+

entries.expanded_definition: adj. finite adv. finitely n. finiteness
entries.usage: Joor zah frul! Mortal finite temporary! (Dragonrend Shout)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, forces the comprehension of finiteness the shackling of a dragon’s immortal and timeless nature.
entries.doubt_word_type: not read: the heading is laid out as a table in the copy

citations: Book, Dragon Language: Myth No More
entries.expanded_definition: n. sword
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv Vulgrum fin Zahkrii ko fin Ven, sovrahzun wen moro lost maltiid, nuz ko vahrukt unslaad. This stone commemorates Vulgrum the Sword in the Wind, the mercenary whose glory was brief, but in memory eternal. (Word Wall for Ven, Cyclone) Qethsegol vahrukiv daanik Fahliil kiir do Gravuun Frod, wo bovul ko Maar nol kinzon zahkrii do kruziik hokoron. This stone commemorates the doomed elf children of the Autumn Field, who fled in Terror from the sharp swords of the ancient enemy. (Word Wall for Maar, Dismay)
entries.etymology: Possibly a compound of zah ‘finite’ and krii ‘to kill’, a weapon that can slay a dragon but not permanently.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to sacrifice n. sacrifice
entries.usage: Nau daar revak golt drey Freda zahrahmiik ek Laas, ful tol ek pogaan kiir filok, ahrk osos sul qahnaar ek hokoron. On this sacred ground did Freda sacrifice her Life, so that her many children might escape, and some day vanquish her enemies. (Word Wall for Laas, Aura Whisper)
entries.connotations: Though word’s etymology may indicate ritual sacrifice, used more generally.
entries.etymology: Possibly from zah ‘finite’, rah ‘god’, or ahmik ‘service’.

entries.expanded_definition: prep. through; past, beyond
entries.usage: Sahrot Thu'um, med aan tuz, vey zeim hokoron pah, ol fin Dovahkiin komeyt ok rein! Mighty Thu'um, like a blade, cut through enemies all, as the Dragonborn issued his roar! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Even I cannot see past Time's ending to what comes next. Niid [sic] koraav zeim dinoksetiid. Niid [sic] koraav zeim dinoksetiid. = “(There is) no seeing through (the) end of time.” (Paarthurnax, 0009C20D)

entries.expanded_definition: prep. through; past, beyond
entries.usage: Occurs only in the dragon name Kahvozein ‘pride undo worship’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. brother, sibling, kin
entries.usage: Ahrk fin Kel lost prodah, do ved viing ko fin krah, tol fod zeymah win kein meyz fundein! And the Scrolls have foretold, of black wings in the cold, that when brothers wage war come unfurled! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Qethsegol vahrukiv Hrodmir fin Krent, wo sov pah ok eruvos ahrk faraan wah Nos tum krivaan do ok zeymah. This stone commemorates Hrodmir the Broken, who spent all his years and fortune to Strike down the killer of his brother. (Word Wall for Nos, Cyclone) Happy? No, I am not happy. Zeymahi lost ont du'ul Bormahu. Alduin was once the crown of our father Akatosh's creation. Zeymahi lost ont du'ul Bormahu = “My brother was once the crown of our father” (Paarthurnax, 0009C213) Yes. Alduin... zeymah. The elder brother. Gifted, grasping and troublesome as is so often the case with firstborn. (Paarthurnax, 000556DC)
entries.connotations: A literal brother or a gender-neutral term for someone close of kin (e.g. ‘brothers in arms’).

entries.expanded_definition: n. companion; the Companions
entries.usage: Het mah siigonis Neivaan wo wundun Gut nol hofkiin dir voth zin ko ahmik do Zeymahzin. [Here fell (the) lizard Nievaan, who travelled Far from home (to) die with honor in service of (the) Companions.] (Unused Word Wall for Gut, Throw Voice)
entries.connotations: Gender-neutral, refers to an honored friend or companion, esp. a person who serves besides someone.
entries.etymology: Compound of zeymah ‘brother’ and zin ‘honor’.
entries.notes: Can also refer to Ysgramor’s Five Hundred Companions.

entries.expanded_definition: n. spirit, soul
entries.usage: Feim zii gron! Fade spirit bind! (Become Ethereal Shout) Sahloknir! Ziil gro dovah ulse! Sahloknir! Your soul is bound to me for eternity! (Alduin, 000CC4F2) Sahrotaar! Ziil los dii du! Sahrotaar, your soul is mine to devour! (Miraak, 0202A8F0) “Fade” in your tongue. Mortals have greater affinity for this Word than the dov. Everything mortal fades away in time, but the spirit remains. Ponder the meaning of spirit. Unslaad zii. Where mortal flesh may wither and die, the spirit endures. (Paarthurnax, 000E8274) Nafni wahlaan qethsegol bormahii vahrukt, Rognvald, wen Zii fen mahfaeraak aak ok brod, ahrk folook ok hokoron. Nafni raised this stone for his father, Rognvald, whose Spirit will forever guide his clan, and haunt his enemies. (Word Wall for Zii, Become Ethereal)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, refers to the living soul and spirit, in contrast with sil ‘soul’ which better refers to souls in the afterlife.
entries.etymology: Related to rii ‘essence’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. honorable adv. honorably n. honor v. to honor, make or become honorable
entries.usage: Dovahkiin, Dovahkiin, naal ok zin los vahriin, wah dein vokul mahfaeraak ahst vaal! Dragonborn, Dragonborn, by his honor is sworn, To keep evil forever at bay! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Not until introductions are complete. Zin. Heyv. Test your Thu'um against mine, Dovahkiin! Zin = honor, heyv = duty (Paarthurnax, 0003F9E6) No day goes by where I am not tempted to return to my inborn nature. Zin krif horvut se suleyk. Zin krif horvut se suleyk. = “Honor (is) fighting the lure of power” (Paarthurnax, 0003C574) Wah Krii ko morokei kein los wah zin geinmaar. Wah dir ko morokei kein los wah zin pah do Keizaal. To Kill in glorious war is to honor oneself. To die in glorious war is to honor all of Skyrim. (Word Wall for Krii, Marked for Death)
entries.connotations: Central to ancient Nordic warrior culture, associated with loyalty and victory. For dragons, pertains to the following of ancient rite, abiding by the rule of strength.
entries.etymology: Possibly related to zii ‘spirit’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to triumph n. triumph
entries.usage: Ahrk fin norok paal graan fod nust hon zindro zaan! And the fiercest foes rout when they hear triumph's shout! (Book, Songs of Skyrim)
entries.connotations: Associated with honor, courage, and strength.
entries.etymology: Likely from zin ‘honor’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. fearful, frightening adv. fearfully, frighteningly n. fearfulness v. to make or become frightening
entries.usage: The Kelle... Elder Scrolls, as you name them, they have often been used for prophecy. … But this is only a small part of their power. Zofaas suleyk. (Paarthurnax, 000BBEAA)
entries.etymology: From faas ‘fear’ with the adjective prefix zo-.
entries.notes: Not to be confused for meaning ‘afraid’ or ‘frightened’.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. heroic adv. heroically v. to make or become heroic
entries.usage: Qethsegol vahrukiv kril Thjodrek, wo dir zohungaar ko Grah do Vith Okaaz. This stone commemorates the brave Thjodrek, who died heroically in the Battle of the Serpent Sea. (Word Wall for Grah, Elemental Fury)
entries.etymology: From hungaar ‘heroic/heroism’ with the adjective prefix zo-, meaning ‘full of heroism’.
entries.notes: To avoid confusion with hungaar ‘heroic’, hungaar should be used solely as a noun (‘heroism’), and zohungaar should be used solely as a weak adjective (‘heroic/heroically’). Otherwise, zohungaar is greater in degree than hungaar.

entries.expanded_definition: adj. great, greatest amount or degree of adv. most (superlative) n. most, greatest v. to make or become the greatest or most
entries.usage: Zu'u Alduin, zok sahrot do naan ko Lein. I (am still) Alduin, most mighty of any in Mundus (the world). (Alduin, 000ED362) Dovahkiin zol [sic] mul. Zu'u gahvon miri Alduin. Dovahkiin is most strong (=stronger). I yield my allegiance (to) Alduin. (Odahviing, 000E16FF) Zok frini grind ko grah drun viiki, Dovahkiin. My most eagerness (to) meet (you) in battle brought my defeat. (Odahviing, 00048F09) Qethsegol vahrukiv key Sarvirra, zok krin Raan alun wah fonaar odus frod, ahrk ofan ok sil fah ok drog. This stone commemorates the horse Sarvirra, the most courageous Animal ever to charge the snowy battlefields, and give his soul for his lord. (Word Wall for Raan, Animal Allegiance)
entries.notes: Used to form superlatives (zok mul ‘strongest / most strong’) and other comparisons. May also be used with nouns to mean ‘great amount of’. Not used to mean ‘majority’ as in ‘most people’, or a pronoun as in ‘most will fail’. See pogaan ‘many’ instead.

entries.expanded_definition: n. zombie
entries.usage: Rii vaaz zol! Essence tear zombie! (Soul Tear Shout)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, refers to a soulless, undead slave. Cannot refer to Draugr, who possess souls.
entries.notes: Occurs in the dialogue as a misspelling of zok ‘most’.

entries.expanded_definition: n. legend
entries.usage: Hun kaal zoor! Hero champion legend! (Call of Valor Shout)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, a person of great deeds, immortalized as a legend.
entries.notes: Refers to a person who is a legend, not ‘legend’ as in ‘myth’ or ‘tale’, or a cartographic ‘legend’.

entries.expanded_definition: v. to create n. creation
entries.usage: Attested only in the PrimaGames.com list.
entries.connotations: Likely more general than wahl ‘to build, create’, which is specific to structures or monuments.

entries.expanded_definition: pron. I (first person singular)
entries.usage: Zu'u unslaad! Zu'u nis oblaan! I am eternal! I cannot end! (be ended/be killed) (Alduin, 000ED359) Ful, losei Dovahkiin? Zu'u koraav nid nol dov do hi. So, you're the Dragonborn? I see nothing of the dragon about you. (Sahloknir, 000C8EA0) Zu'u Odahviing. Call me when you have need, and I will come if I can. (Odahviing, 0009C214) Go and see for yourself. Zu'u ni bo nol het. I will be here... unless Alduin returns before you do. Zu'u ni bo nol het = “I (am) not moving from here” (Odahviing, 0004DE37)
entries.notes: Two-syllable pronunciation used to indicate formality or for emphasis.
entries.doubt: word type is printed as a verb; the entry itself defines a pronoun

entries.official_definition: Voice (the actual mortal voice, not the power of the shouting [sic])
remarks_in_definition: the actual mortal voice, not the power of the shouting [sic]
entries.expanded_definition: n. voice (mortal voice)
entries.usage: Zul mey gut! Voice fool far! (Throw Voice Shout) Ahrk fin zul, rok drey kod, nau tol morokei frod, rul lot Taazokaan motaad voth kein! And the Voice, he did wield, on that glorious field, when great Tamriel shuddered with war! (Book, Songs of Skyrim) Modir fin Gut wahlaan qethsegol zeymahii vahrukt, Oskar fin Mey, wen Zul los sahlo, ahrk ni sahrot Thu’um do ok brod. Modir the Far raised this stone for his brother, Oskar the Fool, whose Voice was weak, and not the mighty Thu’um of his clan. (Word Wall for Throw Voice)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, not the formal name for the power of the Voice (see thu’um) but can be used in reference to it.
entries.etymology: Possibly related to zun ‘weapon’ or shares root with zaan ‘shout’.
entries.notes: At one point was vun rather than zul. Vun is still audible in the Throw Voice Shout and appears instead of zul in the dialogue file.

entries.expanded_definition: n. weapon, weaponry
entries.usage: Zun haal viik! Weapon hand defeat! (Disarm Shout) Pruzaan Zun ko Keizaal los hahdrim do dwiin-sil kendov. The best Weapon in Skyrim is the mind of a steel-souled warrior. (Word Wall for Zun, Disarm)
entries.connotations: Word of Power, generally refers to handheld weaponry but can refer to any implement of battle (e.g. voice).
entries.etymology: Possibly related to zul ‘voice’.
